zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾ — the Kufans said: the meaning of the lām is the meaning of "أنْ", and "أرَدْتُ" (I wanted) and "أمَرْتُ" (I commanded) both call for the future; you may not say "أرَدْتُ أنْ قُمْتُ" (I wanted that I stood) nor "أمَرْتُ أنْ قُمْتُ" (I commanded that I stood). They did not say why this is not permissible. It is an error that the lām of the genitive (lām al-jarr) should stand in the place of "أنْ" and convey its meaning, because the lām enters upon what has the meaning of "أنْ": you say "جِئْتُكَ لِكَيْ تَفْعَلَ كَذا وكَذا" (I came to you so that you might do such-and-such) and "جِئْتُ لِكَيْ تَفْعَلَ كَذا وكَذا" (I came so that you might do such-and-such). Likewise the lām in His saying ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾ is like the lām in "كَيْ"; the meaning is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed it for the sake of making things clear to you. The people of language recited:
أرَدْتُ لِكَيْما لا تُرى لِيَ عَثْرَةٌ ∗∗∗ ومَن ذا الَّذِي يُعْطى الكَمالَ فَيَكْمُلُ
(I wished that no stumble of mine be seen — yet who is it that is granted perfection and so becomes perfect?)
And Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad recited to us:
أرَدْتُ لِكَيْما يَعْلَمَ النّاسُ أنَّها ∗∗∗ سَراوِيلُ قَيْسٍ والوُفُودُ شُهُودُ
(I wished that people should know they were the trousers of Qays, while the delegations were witnesses.)
So he made this lām enter upon "كَيْ"; had it meant "أنْ", the lām would not have entered upon it. Likewise "أرَدْتُ لِأنْ تَقُومَ" (I wanted for you to stand) and "أُمِرْتُ لِأنْ أكُونَ مُطِيعًا" (I was commanded to be obedient). This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيا تَعْبُرُونَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 43], i.e. if your interpreting is for the vision; and likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic, too: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هم لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 154], i.e. those whose fear is for their Lord.
His saying: ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكم سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾, i.e. He guides you to obedience to Him, as He guided the prophets and those who followed them before you. The meaning of ﴿سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ is: the ways of those before you. We have explained this earlier in the book.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, i.e. He guides you, through obedience to Him, to what becomes a cause of your repentance, by which He forgives you your past sins.
﴿وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَواتِ أنْ تَمِيلُوا مَيْلا عَظِيمًا﴾, i.e. that you turn away from the right course.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿وَخُلِقَ الإنْسانُ ضَعِيفًا﴾, i.e. his desire sways him.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا أمْوالَكم بَيْنَكم بِالباطِلِ﴾ — so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, forbade wealth except when it is obtained through the ways He mentioned: the obligatory shares in inheritance, dowries, taking concubines, sale, and the charities whose channels He mentioned. ﴿إلا أنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً﴾: the meaning is "unless the wealth is trade". Whoever reads "إلّا أنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةٌ" «[Translator's note: with the nominative.]», its meaning is "unless trade occurs". ﴿عَنْ تَراضٍ مِنكم ولا تَقْتُلُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾: so He made known that trade is valid with the consent of the seller and the buyer.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ عُدْوانًا وظُلْمًا﴾, i.e. whoever consumes it (wealth) and kills a soul, because His saying ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 29] means: let not some of you kill others; so whoever does that in transgression and injustice...
The meaning of ʿudwān (transgression) is that one oversteps what he was commanded, and ẓulm (injustice) is that one puts a thing in other than its place.
His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نارًا﴾, and "نَصْلِيهِ نارًا" «[Translator's note: i.e. read with fatḥa on the nūn.]»: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, threatened the Fire for consuming wealth unjustly and for killing.
﴿وَكانَ ذَلِكَ عَلى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾, i.e. easy. One says "قَدْ يَسَرَ الشَّيْءُ، فَهو يَسِيرٌ" (the thing became easy, so it is easy) when it is easy, and "قَدْ عَسَرَ الشَّيْءُ، وعَسِرَ" (the thing became difficult) when it is not easy, so it is ʿasīr (difficult).

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾ — "تَجْتَنِبُوا": you leave entirely. The true definition of the major sins (kabāʾir) is that they are everything for which Allah has threatened the Fire, such as killing, fornication, theft and consuming the orphan's wealth. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "The major sins are nearer to being seventy than to being seven." Some said: the major sins are from the beginning of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ up to the head of the thirtieth (verse). The kabāʾir are the sins that are great and grave.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَنُدْخِلْكم مُدْخَلا كَرِيمًا﴾ — the noun is formed on "أدْخَلْتُ" (I caused to enter). Whoever said "مَدْخَلًا", with fatḥa on the mīm, it is built on "دَخَلَ مَدْخَلًا" (he entered an entering). By it here is meant Paradise.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلا تَتَمَنَّوْا ما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكم عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ — it was said: a man should not wish for another's wealth or another's station, for that is envy; rather let him say: "O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty." It was said that Umm Salama said: "Would that we were men, so that we could strive and go on campaigns and have the reward of men." Some said: the men said: "Would that we were favoured over the women in the Hereafter as we have been favoured in this world." All of this goes back to a person's wishing for what belongs to another.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مَوالِيَ مِمّا تَرَكَ الوالِدانِ والأقْرَبُونَ﴾, i.e. We have made the inheritance for whoever is the mawlā of the deceased. The mawlā is everyone who is close to you; everyone who befriends you is a mawlā to you in love; the mawlā is (also) the mawlā of favour, such as the master of a slave; and the mawlā is the slave when he is freed.
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أيْمانُكم فَآتُوهم نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾ — these were in the Jāhiliyya: a weak man would come to a mighty man and make a pact with him, i.e. ally himself with him, saying to him: "I am your son; you inherit from me and I inherit from you; my sanctity is your sanctity, my blood is your blood, and my vengeance is your vengeance." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that faith be kept with them. It was said that this was commanded before the inheritance shares were specified. It was also said: He commanded that their pact made in the Jāhiliyya be honoured for them, but that the Muslims not make the like of it. Some said: the one who makes a pact of alliance (muwālāt) must be given a share of the wealth — he holds that this is from the third that belongs to the deceased. The consensus of the jurists is that there is no inheritance for anyone other than those described: fathers, sons, the agnatic kin (ʿaṣaba), the mawālī and spouses.

zajjaj:91-91.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أنْ يَأْمَنُوكم ويَأْمَنُوا قَوْمَهُمْ﴾: you will find people who make a show of peace towards you so as to be safe from you, but when an occasion of fitna (sedition, strife) presents itself they are with its people against you.
His saying: ﴿كُلَّ ما رُدُّوا إلى الفِتْنَةِ أُرْكِسُوا فِيها﴾, that is: they relapsed from the covenant which they had concluded.
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ يَعْتَزِلُوكُمْ﴾, that is: if they do not withdraw from fighting you and do not refrain from aiding [others] against you.
﴿وَيُلْقُوا إلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ﴾, that is: submission and surrender; ﴿وَيَكُفُّوا أيْدِيَهُمْ﴾, that is: from war; ﴿فَخُذُوهم واقْتُلُوهم حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهم وأُولَئِكم جَعَلْنا لَكم عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانًا مُبِينًا﴾, that is: a clear proof that they are treacherous and do not keep the truce and peace on which they part from you.

zajjaj:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا إلا خَطَأً﴾: the meaning is: it is not for a believer at all [to kill a believer], and «إلّا خَطَأً» is an istithnāʾ (exception) that is not from the first [category, i.e. a disjoined exception]. The meaning is: unless the believer errs, in which case the expiation for his error is what is mentioned afterwards. Some of the people of knowledge said: «وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا إلّا خَطَأً» means that the blood of a Muslim is overlooked, so that the killer is not held [retaliatorily] liable for it, only in the case of error; he has been pardoned for killing by error, except that Allah — exalted be His praise — has prescribed in His Book, for the one who kills by error, the freeing of a slave and blood-money handed over to the guardians of the one killed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made clear that the blood-money for error is upon the ʿāqila (the killer's paternal kinsmen who bear the blood-money), and that the killer must pay in that, because of His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَمَن لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾. It is possible that the fasting is a substitute for the slave, and a substitute for what ought to be paid in blood-money. If a believer kills by error a believing man from a disbelieving people, he must free a slave, and no money goes to the disbelievers who are at war, because blood-money in [cases of] error was only instituted — and Allah knows best — so that people would be extremely wary of committing an error that leads to killing, and so that rancour between them would go away. ﴿وَإنْ كانَ مِن قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهم مِيثاقٌ فَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إلى أهْلِهِ وتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ﴾: if he is from a people between whom and the Muslims there is a covenant, then [there is] the freeing of a slave and the handing over of the blood-money to the people of the covenant, so that no rancour arises between the people of the covenant and the believers.
«تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ» is accusative (manṣūb) in the manner of the accusative in «فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ حَذارَ الشَّرِّ» ("I did that out of caution against evil"). The meaning is: he must fast two months, and he must pay blood-money if it is available, ﴿تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: he did that as a repentance [accepted] from Allah.
As for killing a soul [deliberately], its recompense is as Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 45] in this world, and in the Hereafter, Hell. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَمَن يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خالِدًا فِيها وغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ولَعَنَهُ وأعَدَّ لَهُ عَذابًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 93]. This is a severe threat concerning killing, by which Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made blood inviolable.

zajjaj:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا ضَرَبْتُمْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُوا﴾, and «فَتَثَبَّتُوا» — with thāʾ and with tāʾ. [Translator's note: i.e. the two readings «فَتَبَيَّنُوا» ("verify") and «فَتَثَبَّتُوا» ("make sure").] The meaning of «ضَرَبْتُمْ» is: you travelled in the land and went out on campaign.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَن ألْقى إلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِنًا﴾: it was read «اَلسَّلامَ» with alif, and it was read «اَلسَّلَمَ». As for «اَلسَّلامَ», it may be from «اَلتَّسْلِيمُ» (the greeting of peace), and it may be in the sense of «اَلسِّلْمُ», which is submission and yielding oneself to the will of the Muslims. It is related in the tafsīr that the occasion of this was that a man withdrew [from his people] and declared Islam, and a man of the Muslims killed him and took his spoils. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the due of one who offers submission is that his case be verified; and whoever read «فَتَثَبَّتُوا», [for him] his due is that one make sure about his case. And Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that everyone who became Muslim from among those who had been disbelievers is in the position of the one who sought refuge in Islam, so He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ كُنْتُمْ مِن قَبْلُ فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, that is: He conferred favour on you with Islam, and by accepting that from you according to what you outwardly showed. Then He repeated the command to verify, saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾

zajjaj:95-95.t:
﴿لا يَسْتَوِي القاعِدُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ والمُجاهِدُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: it was read «غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ» in the nominative (rafʿ), and «غَيْرَ» in the accusative (naṣb). As for the nominative, it is from two angles. One of them is that «غَيْرُ» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «القاعِدُونَ», even though its basic use is to be an adjective of an indefinite noun; the meaning is: those who stay behind, who are other than those with an impairment, are not equal — that is, the healthy ones who stay behind and those who strive are not equal, even if all of them are believers. And «غَيْرُ» may be nominative by way of istithnāʾ (exception); the meaning is: those who stay behind and those who strive are not equal, except those with an impairment, for they are equal to those who strive, because what kept them back from striving was the impairment. Ḍarar (impairment) is that one be blind, or sightless, or chronically disabled, or sick. It is related that Ibn Umm Maktūm said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Is striving obligatory on me?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "﴿انْفِرُوا خِفافًا وثِقالا﴾ [al-Tawba: 41] — so you are either among the light or among the heavy." Then Allah revealed: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلى الأعْمى حَرَجٌ ولا عَلى الأعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ ولا عَلى المَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 17].
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ المُجاهِدِينَ بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ عَلى القاعِدِينَ دَرَجَةً وكُلا وعَدَ اللَّهُ الحُسْنى﴾, that is: He promised Paradise; ﴿وَفَضَّلَ اللَّهُ المُجاهِدِينَ عَلى القاعِدِينَ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾.
And «غَيْرَ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ» may be accusative by way of exception from «اَلْقاعِدِينَ»; the meaning is: those who stay behind are not equal, except those with an impairment — according to the basic rule of exception, [which is] the accusative. And «غَيْرَ» may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: those who stay behind in the state of their health and those who strive are not equal, just as you say «جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ غَيْرَ مَرِيضٍ» ("Zayd came to me not sick"), that is: Zayd came to me healthy. And it is permissible to put «غَيْرَ» in the genitive (jarr) as an adjective of «اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ», that is: those who stay behind from among the healthy believers and those who strive are not equal. As for the nominative and the accusative, the reading with both is widespread; the genitive is a good option, except that the people of the cities [i.e. the canonical readers of the main centres] did not read it, even though it is a possible option, because reading is a sunna to be followed.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿دَرَجاتٍ مِنهُ ومَغْفِرَةً ورَحْمَةً﴾: «دَرَجاتٍ» is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for His saying ﴿أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 95], and it explains the other. The meaning is: Allah has favoured those who strive with degrees, forgiveness and mercy. It is also permissible that it be accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of «أجْرًا عَظِيمًا», because the great reward is the raising of degrees from Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — and forgiveness and mercy; just as you say «لَكَ عَلَيَّ ألْفُ دِرْهَمٍ» [followed by an emphatic maṣdar], because your saying «عَلَيَّ ألْفُ دِرْهَمٍ» is an acknowledgement, so it is as though you had said «أعْرِفُها عُرْفًا» ("I acknowledge it an acknowledgement"). [Translator's note: the phrase «لَكَ عَلَيَّ ألْفُ دِرْهَمٍ» appears to be the opening of the well-known example «لَهُ عَلَيَّ ألْفُ دِرْهَمٍ عُرْفًا»; the emphatic word seems to have dropped from the text as transmitted.] It is as if it were said: «غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهم مَغْفِرَةً، وأجَرَهم أجْرًا عَظِيمًا» ("Allah forgave them a forgiveness and rewarded them a great reward"), because His saying «أجْرًا عَظِيمًا» contains the meaning of "He forgave, had mercy and favoured".
The nominative is [also] permissible in His saying «دَرَجاتٍ مِنهُ ومَغْفِرَةً ورَحْمَةً»: if it were said «دَرَجاتٌ مِنهُ ومَغْفِرَةٌ ورَحْمَةٌ», it would be permissible by implying «تِلْكَ دَرَجاتٌ مِنهُ ومَغْفِرَةٌ» ("those are degrees from Him and forgiveness"), just as He — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلا ساعَةً مِن نَهارٍ بَلاغٌ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 35], that is: «ذَلِكَ بَلاغٌ» ("that is a proclamation").

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ ظالِمِي أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: by it are meant the idolaters who stayed behind from emigrating to the Prophet ﷺ. As for «تَوَفّاهم», if you wish, its form is past, meaning «إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّتْهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ», and the verb is made masculine because it is a proper verb [preceding a plural agent]. And it may have a future sense, meaning «إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ», with the second tāʾ elided because of the meeting of two tāʾs; we have explained this earlier in this book.
His saying: ﴿ظالِمِي أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is «تَتَوَفّاهم في حالِ ظُلْمِهِمْ أنْفُسَهم» ("they take them in the state of their wronging themselves"). The original is «ظالِمِينَ أنْفُسَهم», except that the nūn was elided for lightness while the meaning is that of its being present, just as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿هَدْيًا بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 95], where the meaning is that of the tanwīn being present, meaning «بالِغًا الكَعْبَةَ».
His saying: ﴿قالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ﴾: this wāw belongs to «اَلْمَلائِكَةُ», that is: the angels said to the idolaters: "In what [condition] were you?" — that is: were you among the idolaters or among the companions of Muḥammad ﷺ? This is a question of rebuke; its like has come before and we have exhausted its explanation.
His saying: ﴿كُنّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾: Allah made known that they had been too weak to emigrate, and the angels said to them: ﴿ألَمْ تَكُنْ أرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةً فَتُهاجِرُوا فِيها فَأُولَئِكَ مَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ وساءَتْ مَصِيرًا﴾

zajjaj:98-98.t: ﴿إلا المُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجالِ والنِّساءِ والوِلْدانِ﴾: «اَلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ» is accusative as the mustathnā (excepted) from His saying «مَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ... إلّا المُسْتَضْعَفِينَ», that is: except whoever truly is weak, not able to find a means and not guided to a way. Allah made known that these hope for pardon, as the believers hope, and He said:

zajjaj:99-99.t:
﴿فَأُولَئِكَ عَسى اللَّهُ أنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ﴾: «عَسى» expresses hope, and whatever Allah has commanded to be hoped for from His mercy is in the position of what has [already] taken place; such is the expectation [one should have] of the Most Merciful of the merciful.
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا﴾: people have differed over the interpretation of «كانَ» in this place. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: "He was forgiving to His servants and of His servants before He created them." The Basran grammarians said: "It is as if the people witnessed mercy from Allah, and were informed that this was nothing newly occurring, and that Allah has ever been thus." And a group of grammarians said: «كانَ» and «فَعَلَ» from Allah are in the position of what is in the present, so the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: and Allah is pardoning, forgiving. What al-Ḥasan and others said fits the language better and is closer to the speech of the Arabs. As for the third view, its meaning comes back to what al-Ḥasan and Sībawayh said, except that the past in the sense of the present is rare. The holder of this view has as evidence our saying «غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لِفُلانٍ» in the sense of «لِيَغْفِرِ اللَّهُ لَهُ» ("may Allah forgive him"): since in the situation there is an indication of the future, the past came to convey it for lightness, because the difference between the forms of verbs only arose because of the difference of times; so when the circumstances and times are made known, the form of some verbs suffices in place of the form of others. The proof of that is His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾ [al-Anʿām: 160].
And His saying: ﴿وَمَن تابَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا فَإنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إلى اللَّهِ مَتابًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 71] — its meaning is «مَن يَتُبْ» ("whoever repents"), and «مَن يَجِئْ بِالحَسَنَةِ يُعْطَ عَشْرَ أمْثالِها» ("whoever comes with a good deed will be given ten times its like").

zajjaj:100-100.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُهاجِرْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ في الأرْضِ مُراغَمًا كَثِيرًا وسَعَةً﴾: the meaning of «مُراغَمٌ» is the meaning of «مُهاجَرٌ» (place of emigration). The meaning is: he will find in the land a place to emigrate to, because the one who emigrates from his people and the one who defies [them] are in one position, even if the two words differ. The poet said:
؎إلى بَلَدٍ غَيْرِ دانِي المَحَلِّ ∗∗∗ بَعِيدِ المُراغَمِ والمُضْطَرَبْ
(To a land whose abode is not near, far-reaching in its place of refuge and room to roam.)
And it was said: «اَلْمُراغَمُ» here is «اَلْمُضْطَرَبُ» (room to move about), and al-murāgham here is nothing but the room to move about in a state of emigration, even though it is derived from «اَلرُّغامُ», and «اَلرُّغامُ» is dust. The interpretation of your saying «راغَمْتُ فُلانًا» is: I abandoned him and showed him enmity and did not care about the humbling of his nose — that is, even if his nose were stuck to the dust. «اَلرَّغامُ» and «اَلرُّغامُ» [also mean] what flows from the nose. The nose is described with raghm (being rubbed in dust), and so it is used as a proverb for every abased person, and it is said: «عَلى رَغْمِ أنْفِهِ» ("in spite of him", lit. "despite the dusting of his nose").

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿واعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ولا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا﴾, i.e. do not worship anything else along with Him, for that corrupts the worship of Him. ﴿وَبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾: the meaning is: Allah has enjoined upon you the worship of Him, and enjoined upon you kindness to parents. Likewise His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَضى رَبُّكَ ألا تَعْبُدُوا إلا إيّاهُ وبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 23], because the meaning of "قَضى" here is: He commanded and enjoined.
Some of the grammarians said: "إحْسانًا" is accusative (manṣūb) on the basis of "وَأحْسِنُوا بِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا" (and be kind to parents with kindness), just as you say "ضَرْبًا زَيْدًا", the meaning being "اِضْرِبْ زَيْدًا ضَرْبًا" (strike Zayd a striking). ﴿وَبِذِي القُرْبى﴾: Allah commanded kindness to relatives after parents. ﴿واليَتامى﴾ is in the position of the genitive (jarr); the meaning is: "and to orphans and the needy He has also enjoined you". Likewise everything mentioned in this verse; the meaning is: be kind to all of these. ﴿والجارِ ذِي القُرْبى﴾, i.e. the neighbour who is near to you, whom you know and who knows you. ﴿والجارِ الجُنُبِ﴾: and the neighbour who is near yet distant. ʿAlqama said:
فَلا تَحْرِمَنِّي نائِلًا عَنَ جَنابَةٍ ∗∗∗ فَإنِّي امْرُؤٌ وسْطَ القِبابِ غَرِيبُ
(So do not deny me a gift on account of my being a stranger, for I am a man who is a stranger among the domed tents.)
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والصّاحِبِ بِالجَنْبِ﴾ — it was said: he is the companion on a journey. ﴿وابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾: the guest, whose hospitality is obligatory, and who must be conveyed to where he wishes to go.
His saying: ﴿وَما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾, i.e. and be kind to what your right hands possess. The position of "ما" is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to what precedes it. The parting counsel of the Prophet ﷺ at his death was: «”اَلصَّلاةَ، وما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم“» (The prayer, and what your right hands possess).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ مَن كانَ مُخْتالا فَخُورًا﴾ — the mukhtāl is the boastful, the haughty, the ignorant. Haughtiness is mentioned in this context only because the haughty man disdains his relatives when they are poor, and his neighbours when they are so, and so he does not treat them well.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ ويَأْمُرُونَ النّاسَ بِالبُخْلِ﴾ — and "اَلْبَخْلِ": both are read. The Jews are meant by it, because they withheld the knowledge they had of the sending of the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿وَيَكْتُمُونَ ما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾, i.e. what He gave them of knowledge of the messengership of the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابًا مُهِينًا﴾, i.e. We have made that a provision (ʿatād) for them, or fixed for them. It is possible that the position of "اَلَّذِينَ" is accusative as a badal (substitute), the meaning being: Allah does not love whoever is haughty and boastful, i.e. He does not love those who are stingy. It is also possible that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 40], and that ﴿والَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أمْوالَهم رِئاءَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 38] is conjoined to ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ﴾ in the accusative and in the nominative. By these the hypocrites are meant: they used to display faith but did not believe in Allah and the Last Day.

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿وَمَن يَكُنِ الشَّيْطانُ لَهُ قَرِينًا فَساءَ قَرِينًا﴾, i.e. whoever's deeds are according to what Satan makes seem fair to him, then evil is the deed — his deed. "فَساءَ قَرِينًا" is accusative as an explanation (tafsīr) «[Translator's note: i.e. tamyīz (specification).]», just as you say "زَيْدٌ نِعْمَ رَجُلًا" (Zayd — how excellent a man!), and as He said: ﴿ساءَ مَثَلا القَوْمُ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 177].

zajjaj:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَماذا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ — it is sound for "ما" and "ذا" to be a single noun, the meaning being: and what thing is upon them? It is also possible for "ذا" to have the meaning of "اَلَّذِي" (which), or for "ما" alone to be a noun, the meaning being: and what is it that would be upon them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah provided them?! This indicates that those who are stingy are stingy with what they know. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ عَلِيمًا﴾.

zajjaj:40-40.t:
His saying, Exalted be His praise: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾ — "مِثْقالٌ" is of the pattern "مِفْعالٌ", from "اَلثِّقْلُ" (weight), i.e. whatever has the weight of an atom (dharra). It was said: for everything that is done, (the expression) "the weight of a mithqāl" is by way of representation, because prayer, fasting and deeds have no weight; but people were addressed concerning what is in their hearts by representing it with what is perceived by their eyes, because that — I mean what is seen — is clearer to them.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضاعِفْها﴾ — the origin of "تَكُنْ" is "تَكُونْ"; the ḍamma fell away for the jussive (jazm), and the wāw fell away because of its being quiescent along with the quiescence of the nūn. As for the dropping of the nūn from "تَكُنْ", the predominant usage in the Quran retains it, and dropping it is rare. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أوْ فَقِيرًا فاللَّهُ أوْلى بِهِما﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 135]. Two things combined in the nūn: that it resembles the soft letters (ḥurūf al-līn), and that it is quiescent; so it was elided for lightness because of frequent use, just as they said "لا أدْرِ" (I don't know) and "لَمْ أُبَلْ" (I did not care), though the better form is "لَمْ أُبالِ" and "لا أدْرِي". "حَسَنَةً" may take the nominative or the accusative; the meaning is: and if his deed is a good one, He multiplies it. Whoever reads "وَإنْ تَكُنْ حَسَنَةٌ" in the nominative makes it nominative as the noun (ism) of "كانَ", which has no khabar (predicate); here it is used in the complete sense (tāmma), and the meaning is: and if a good deed occurs, He multiplies it.
﴿وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَدُنْهُ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ — "وَيُؤْتِ" is without yāʾ; the yāʾ fell away for the jussive, it being conjoined to "يُضاعِفْها". "لَدُنْ" occurs here in the position of the genitive. It has several dialectal forms: one says "لَدُ", "لَدُنْ", "لَدُنٌ" and "لَدى", and the meaning is one: its meaning is "from His side". Except that it is not as fully flexible as "عِنْدَ", because you say "هَذا القَوْلُ عِنْدِي صَوابٌ" (this saying, in my view, is correct), but one does not say "اَلْوَقْتُ لَدُنِّي صَوابٌ"; and you say "عِنْدِي مالٌ عَظِيمٌ" (I have great wealth) while the wealth is absent from you, whereas "لَدُنْ" is for what is next to you.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذا جِئْنا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ﴾, i.e. so how will the state of these people be on the Day of Resurrection?! "تَكُونُ حالُهم" (their state will be) was omitted because there is in the speech an indication of what was omitted. "كَيْفَ" has the wording of a question, but its meaning is the meaning of rebuke. His saying: ﴿وَجِئْنا بِكَ عَلى هَؤُلاءِ شَهِيدًا﴾, i.e. We shall bring the prophet of each community to bear witness against it and for it.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ﴾ — the preferred choice is the ḍamma on the wāw in "عَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ" because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the kasra is permissible. We have explained this earlier.
His saying: ﴿لَوْ تُسَوّى بِهِمُ الأرْضُ﴾, and "بِهِمِ الأرْضُ", with ḍamma and with kasra on the mīm. ﴿وَلا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثًا﴾, i.e. they wish that they had not been resurrected, and that they and the earth were level. It has come in the exegesis that on the Day of Resurrection the beasts will become dust, and so they will wish that they became dust. His saying: ﴿وَلا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثًا﴾ — there is more than one view about it. Some said: they will wish that the earth had been levelled over them, and that they had not concealed any statement from Allah, because in their saying ﴿واللَّهِ رَبِّنا ما كُنّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 23] they lied. Others said: "﴿وَلا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثًا﴾" is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), because what they did is manifest to Allah and they are unable to conceal it.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وأنْتُمْ سُكارى﴾ — it was said in the exegesis that it was revealed before the prohibition of wine, because a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ gathered and drank wine before its prohibition; one man among them went forward and led them in prayer, and he recited: "قُلْ يا أيُّها الكافِرُونَ أعْبُدُ ما تَعْبُدُونَ، وأنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ، وأنا عابِدٌ ما عَبَدْتُمْ" «[Translator's note: a garbled recitation of Sūrat al-Kāfirūn in which the negations are dropped.]», so there was revealed: ﴿لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وأنْتُمْ سُكارى﴾. It is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "O Allah, wine harms the intellect and takes away wealth, so reveal Your command concerning it." So there was revealed in Sūrat al-Māʾida: ﴿إنَّما الخَمْرُ والمَيْسِرُ والأنْصابُ والأزْلامُ رِجْسٌ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 90]. And He said: ﴿يَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ الخَمْرِ والمَيْسِرِ قُلْ فِيهِما إثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 219]. The prohibition was stated explicitly by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ إنَّما حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ الفَواحِشَ ما ظَهَرَ مِنها وما بَطَنَ والإثْمَ والبَغْيَ بِغَيْرِ الحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 33]; so wine has been prohibited in that He said it is a great sin (ithm), and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited sin. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded at that time that the drunk should not approach prayer, and after that He prohibited intoxication, because the consensus of the community is that intoxication is forbidden; and what intoxicates was prohibited, because the reality of intoxication is that it has always been forbidden. We have explained this in Sūrat al-Baqara.
His saying: ﴿حَتّى تَعْلَمُوا ما تَقُولُونَ ولا جُنُبًا إلا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتّى تَغْتَسِلُوا﴾, i.e. do not approach prayer while you are in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), except those passing on a way, i.e. except travellers, because the traveller lacks water; and likewise the sick person whom washing harms. It is related «that some people washed a man with smallpox and he died, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "They killed him, may Allah kill them! Tayammum (dry ablution) would have sufficed him."» Some people said: (it means) "do not approach the place of prayer". Its true sense is: do not pray when you are junub until you have washed, unless you are unable to find water, or unless you fear that washing will harm you severely, and that only happens in a state of illness. ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا﴾: the meaning of "تَيَمَّمُوا" is: aim for. The ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth. So in tayammum a person must strike with his hands a single strike and wipe his face with both of them, and likewise strike a single strike and wipe his hands with them. The ṭayyib is the clean and pure. It does not matter whether there is dust in the place or not, because the ṣaʿīd is not dust; it is only the surface of the earth, whether dust or something else. If a land were entirely rock with no dust on it, and the one performing tayammum struck his hand on that rock, it would be a means of purification when he wiped his face with it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 40], so He made known to you that the ṣaʿīd may be slippery. The ṣuʿudāt are the roads. It was called "ṣaʿīd" only because it is the furthest point to which one ascends from the interior of the earth. I know of no disagreement among the people of language that the ṣaʿīd is the surface of the earth. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا﴾, i.e. He accepts from you what is easy (al-ʿafw) and forgives you, because His accepting tayammum is a facilitation for you.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الكِتابِ﴾ — some said: "ألَمْ تَرَ" means: have you not been told? The people of language said: have you not known? The meaning is: has your knowledge not reached these people? And its sense is: know them. By it are meant the scholars of the People of the Book: Allah gave them in their book knowledge of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ — that he is written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, commanding them what is right and forbidding them what is wrong.
His saying: ﴿يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلالَةَ﴾, i.e. they prefer denial of the matter of the Prophet ﷺ so as to take bribes for it and so that leadership may be secured for them.
His saying: ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أنْ تَضِلُّوا السَّبِيلَ﴾, i.e. that you stray from the way of guidance, because "اَلسَّبِيلُ" in the language is the way.

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِأعْدائِكُمْ﴾, i.e. He knows them better, so He informs you of what they are upon. ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ ولِيًّا وكَفى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيرًا﴾, i.e. Allah is your helper against them. The meaning of the bāʾ is emphasis (tawkīd); the meaning is: Allah suffices as a protector, and Allah suffices as a helper. Except that the bāʾ entered upon the noun of the agent (ism al-fāʿil) «[Translator's note: i.e. the fāʿil (agent) of كَفى.]» because the meaning of the speech is a command; the meaning is: be content with Allah.

zajjaj:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ﴾ — there are two views about it. It is possible that it is part of the ṣila (relative clause) of "اَلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ", the meaning being: "ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الكِتابِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا" (have you not seen those given a portion of the Book, from among those who are Jews). And it is possible that it is "مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا قَوْمٌ يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ" (among those who are Jews are people who distort words), with "يُحَرِّفُونَ" being a ṣifa (adjective) and the thing qualified being omitted. Sībawayh recited concerning the like of this the poet's saying:
وَما الدَّهْرُ إلّا تارَتانِ فَمِنهُما ∗∗∗ أمُوتُ وأُخْرى أبْتَغِي العَيْشَ أكْدَحُ
(Time is but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
The meaning is: of them, a turn in which I die. Some of the grammarians said: the meaning is "مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا مَن يُحَرِّفُونَهُ" (among those who are Jews are those who distort it), so he made "يُحَرِّفُونَ" the ṣila of "مَن". This is not permissible, because the relative (mawṣūl) is not omitted while its ṣila remains. Likewise the poet's saying:
لَوْ قُلْتُ ما في قَوْمِها لَمْ تِيثَمِ ∗∗∗ يَفْضُلُها في حَسَبٍ ومِيسَمِ
(Were you to say: "there is not among her people [one who] surpasses her in lineage and beauty", you would not be committing a sin.)
The meaning is: there is not among her people anyone who surpasses her. The grammarians claimed that this is permissible only with "مِن" and "في". It is (in fact) permissible whenever there is in what remains an indication of what was dropped: if you said "ما فِيهِمْ يَقُولُ ذاكَ" (there is not among them [one who] says that) or "ما عِنْدَهم يَقُولُ ذاكَ" (there is not with them [one who] says that), both would be permissible to the same degree, the meaning being: "ما عِنْدَهم أحَدٌ يَقُولُ ذاكَ" (there is not with them anyone who says that).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنا وعَصَيْنا واسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ﴾ — the Jews, may they be cursed, used to say to the Prophet ﷺ "Hear!", while saying to themselves "may you not be made to hear". It was also said: "غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ" means: not answered in what you call to.
His saying: ﴿وَراعِنا﴾ — this was a word that circulated among them by way of mockery and ridicule. Some said: they used to revile the Prophet ﷺ with this word. Others said: they used to say it out of arrogance, as if they were saying "lend us your hearing", i.e. make your speech a pasture for our hearing. This is something with which prophets — the blessings of Allah be upon them — are not addressed; they are addressed only with reverence and veneration.
His saying: ﴿لَيًّا بِألْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾, i.e. they do that in obstinacy against the truth and transgression in religion. The origin of "لَيًّا" is "لَوْيًا", but the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ because it preceded it with quiescence (sukūn).
His saying: ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾, i.e. they do not believe except with a little faith, by which they would not deserve to be called "the believers". Some said: ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ means: except a few of them, for they did believe.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Surat al-Nisaʾ
﷽
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ﴾. Allah began the sura with admonition: He informed [them] of what establishes that He is One, and that it is His right — Mighty and Majestic is He — to be feared. So He said: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ﴾, meaning: from Adam — peace be upon him. In the language ”واحِدَةٍ“ (feminine) was said only because the word nafs is feminine, while its meaning in this place is masculine; had it been said ”مِن نَفْسٍ واحِدٍ“, it would have been permissible. ﴿وَخَلَقَ مِنها زَوْجَها﴾: Eve, who was created from one of the ribs of Adam; and Allah spread forth the whole creation of mankind from her.

The meaning of ”بَثَّ“ is: spread out. One says: ”بَثَّ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ“ ("Allah spread forth creation"), and He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿كالفَراشِ المَبْثُوثِ﴾ [al-Qariʿa: 4], so this attests ”بَثَّ“. Some of the Arabs say ”أبَثَّ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ“, and one says ”بَثَثْتُكَ سِرِّي“ and ”أبْثَثْتُكَ سِرِّي“ ("I disclosed my secret to you").

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ”واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسّاءَلُونَ بِهِ“ with the doubling: the origin is ”تَتَساءَلُونَ“, and the tāʾ was assimilated into the sīn because of the closeness of the place [of articulation] of the one to the other. Whoever reads it without the doubling, the origin is [likewise] ”تَتَساءَلُونَ“, except that the second tāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of the two tāʾs, which is felt to be heavy in pronunciation; so the omission occurred for lightness, since the speech is not ambiguous.

The meaning of ﴿تَساءَلُونَ بِهِ﴾ is: you seek your rights by Him. ﴿والأرْحامَ﴾: the good reading is the accusative of ”اَلْأرْحامَ“, the meaning being: "and fear [to violate] the ties of kinship, lest you sever them." As for the genitive in ”اَلْأرْحامِ“, it is an error in Arabic, not permissible except under the constraint of poetry, and it is also a grave error in a matter of religion, because the Prophet ﷺ said: «”لا تَحْلِفُوا بِآبائِكم“» ("Do not swear by your fathers"); so how could it be, on this [reading], "you ask one another by Him and by the ties of kinship"? I saw Abū Isḥāq Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq holding that swearing by other than Allah is a grave matter, and that this is exclusive to Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — according to what the narration has brought.

As for Arabic, the grammarians agree unanimously that it is ugly to conjoin an overt noun to a pronoun in the genitive state except by repeating the preposition (al-jārr) overtly. The grammarians consider ugly ”مَرَرْتُ بِهِ وزَيْدٍ“ ("I passed by him and Zayd") and ”بِكَ وزَيْدٍ“, unless the preposition (al-khāfiḍ) is made overt, so that they say ”بِكَ وبِزَيْدٍ“. Some of them said: [this is] because the genitive [pronoun] is an attached particle, not a detached one, so it is as it were like the tanwīn in a noun; hence it is ugly to conjoin a noun that stands by itself to a noun that does not stand by itself. Al-Māzī [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably al-Māzinī] explained this convincingly, saying: the second in conjunction is a partner of the first, so if the first is fit to be a partner of the second [then well and good], otherwise the second is not fit to be its partner. He said: just as you do not say ”مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ وكَ“, likewise ”مَرَرْتُ بِكَ وزَيْدٍ“ is not permissible. It has, however, been allowed in poetry; Sībawayh recited:
؎فاليَوْمَ قَرَّبْتَ تَهْجُونا وتَشْتُمُنا ∗∗∗ فاذْهَبْ فَما بِكَ والأيّامِ مِن عَجَبِ
(So today you have set about satirising and reviling us — off with you, then! There is nothing to wonder at in you or in the days.)

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا اليَتامى أمْوالَهُمْ﴾, that is: give them their wealth when you perceive maturity of judgement in them. They are called ”يَتامى“ (orphans) after maturity has been perceived in them — when the name ”يَتامى“ has already left them — by the first name they used to have; [similarly,] it used to be said of the Prophet ﷺ: "the orphan of Abū Ṭālib".

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ﴾. "The good" is your own wealth, and "the bad" is the wealth of the orphan and anything else that is not yours; so do not consume the orphan's wealth in exchange for your own wealth. Likewise do not consume their wealth [added] to your wealth, that is, do not join their wealth to your wealth in consuming it; that is, if you are in need of it, you have no right to consume it together with your wealth. ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ حُوبًا كَبِيرًا﴾: ”اَلْحُوبُ“ is a great sin, and ”اَلْحُوبُ“ is [also] the man's act [of sinning]; you say ”حابَ حُوبًا“, as you say ”قَدْ خانَ خُونًا“ ("he betrayed").

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنْ خِفْتُمْ ألا تُقْسِطُوا في اليَتامى فانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكم مِنَ النِّساءِ﴾. Mujāhid said: If you feel it a sin to neglect the guardianship of orphans, out of faith and belief, then likewise feel it a sin to commit fornication. Someone else said: If you fear that you will not act justly in the matter of women, then marry [only] what Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has mentioned. Some of the exegetes stated a third view — the people of Basra among the people of Arabic said [it], that exegete says —: they used to marry ten of the orphan girls, or about that, out of desire for their wealth, so Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَإنْ خِفْتُمْ ألا تُقْسِطُوا في اليَتامى﴾, that is, in marrying the orphans, and ﴿فانْكِحُوا﴾ indicates this. Thus said Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], and it is the position of the people of reasoned inquiry among the exegetes.

﴿فانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكم مِنَ النِّساءِ مَثْنى وثُلاثَ ورُباعَ﴾: He did not say ”مَن طابَ“. The proper usage for human beings is to say ”مَن“ ("who"), and for attributes and generic nouns to say ”ما“ ("what"); you say ”ما عِنْدَكَ؟“ ("What do you have?") and he says: "A horse, and perfume." So the meaning is: marry the good and lawful, according to this number that has been described, because not all women are good [lawful] for you. He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكم وبَناتُكم وأخَواتُكم وعَمّاتُكم وخالاتُكم وبَناتُ الأخِ وبَناتُ الأُخْتِ وأُمَّهاتُكُمُ اللاتِي أرْضَعْنَكم وأخَواتُكم مِنَ الرَّضاعَةِ وأُمَّهاتُ نِسائِكم ورَبائِبُكُمُ اللاتِي في حُجُورِكم مِن نِسائِكُمُ اللاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَإنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisa: 23]; so none of those mentioned is among what is good [lawful].

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿مَثْنى وثُلاثَ ورُباعَ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ﴿ما طابَ لَكُمْ﴾, and its meaning is: two by two, three by three and four by four. However, it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) for two reasons which I do not know any of the grammarians to have mentioned, namely that two causes have come together in it: that it is shifted (maʿdūl) from "two two" and "three three", and that it is shifted from the feminine. Our colleagues said: two causes have come together in it — that it is shifted from the feminine, and that it is indefinite; but the indefinite is the base of nouns, so on this account we ought to make it light [i.e. fully declinable], because the indefinite is light and is not counted as secondary. Others said: it is definite — but this is impossible, because it is an adjective of an indefinite noun. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿جاعِلِ المَلائِكَةِ رُسُلا أُولِي أجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وثُلاثَ ورُباعَ﴾ [Fatir: 1], and it is impossible for this to be "possessing the three and the four wings"; its meaning is only "possessing wings, three by three and four by four". The poet said:
؎وَلَكِنَّما أهْلِي بِوادٍ أنِيسُهُ ∗∗∗ ذِئابٌ تَبَغّى النّاسَ مَثْنى ومَوْحَدُ
(But my people are in a valley whose only company is wolves, hunting men in twos and singly.)

If one of the Rāfiḍa says: "Nine have been made lawful for us, because His saying ﴿مَثْنى وثُلاثَ ورُباعَ﴾ means nine," it is answered: this is invalid on several counts. One of them, in the language, is that ”مَثْنى“ is only fit for "two by two", distributively. Another is that it would be the most incompetent of speech: if someone, in place of [saying] nine, said: "I will give you two and three and four," meaning nine, it would be said [to him]: "nine" spares you this, because "nine" was coined for this whole number, I mean from one to nine. Furthermore, according to their view, whoever marries fewer than nine or [other than] one is a sinner, because if what was made permissible for him were nine or one, we would have no way to "two"; for if someone whom you must obey commanded you, saying: "Enter this mosque nine times a day, or once," and you entered other than these two numbers of times that he specified for you, you would have disobeyed him. This is a view that does not deserve to be dwelt upon, but we have mentioned it so that the Muslims may know that the holders of this view are at variance with the people of Islam in their belief, and that they believe in this matter an error which is unclear to no one.

As for His saying ﴿ذَلِكَ أدْنى ألا تَعُولُوا﴾, its meaning is: that is nearer to your not acting unjustly. It is said in the exegesis: "that you not incline", and the meaning of "incline" is: act unjustly. As for whoever said that ”ألّا تَعُولُوا“ means "that your dependants not become many", all the people of the language claim that this is an error, because a single wife [also] brings dependants, and the permission of all that the right hand possesses adds more to the dependants than four [wives] do. There was no limit to the number in marriage when this verse was revealed. The proof that they used to desire to marry orphan girls for their wealth is that they did not care if they did not act justly in their affair.

[And] His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ في النِّساءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكم فِيهِنَّ وما يُتْلى عَلَيْكم في الكِتابِ في يَتامى النِّساءِ اللاتِي لا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ ما كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ وتَرْغَبُونَ أنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ [al-Nisa: 127]. So the meaning is: if you fear that you will not act equitably in marrying orphans, then marry the good which has been made lawful for you from among other women. And the meaning [also] is: if you are secure from injustice regarding the orphans, then marry of them according to this number, because "women" includes the orphans and others.

zajjaj:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّها عَلى أدْبارِها﴾ — there are three views about it. Some said: "We make their faces like the backs of their heads." Some said: "We make their faces places where hair grows, like the backs of their heads." And some said: the faces here are a representation of the matter of religion; the meaning is: before We lead them astray as a requital for the obstinacy they are upon, leading them so far astray that they will never believe thereafter.

zajjaj:48-48.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ ويَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشاءُ﴾ — the Muslims agree that what is below the major sins is forgiven, and they disagreed about the major sins. Some said: the major sins for which Allah has threatened the Fire are not forgiven. The elders among the people of jurisprudence and knowledge said: it is possible that everything below that be forgiven through repentance, and through repentance associating partners (shirk) and other sins are forgiven. ﴿وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ افْتَرى إثْمًا عَظِيمًا﴾: "اِفْتَرى" means: he fabricated and lied; "إثْمًا عَظِيمًا", i.e. one that is not forgiven.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ — "ألَمْ تَرَ" means "have you not been told?" according to some; the people of language said: "have you not known?" Its interpretation is a question containing the meaning of informing; its interpretation is: know their story. And according to the course of the language: "has your knowledge not reached these people?" The meaning of "يُزَكُّونَ أنْفُسَهم" is: they claim that they are pure. The interpretation of our saying "زُكاءُ الشَّيْءِ" in the language is its growth in soundness. By this too the Jews are meant: they had come to the Prophet ﷺ with their children and said: "O Muḥammad, do these have any sins?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "No." They said: "So are we: what we do by night is forgiven by night, and what we do by day is forgiven by day." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشاءُ﴾, i.e. He makes pure whomever He wills. ﴿وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلا﴾: its interpretation is: and they will not be wronged by the amount of a fatīl. Some said: the fatīl is the dirt you roll between your fingers. Some said: the fatīl is the fibre in the inner groove of the date-stone. And they said in the exegesis: (it is) what is on its back, from which the palm sprouts. The qiṭmīr is the whole of the fibre wrapped around it.

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ عَلى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ﴾, i.e. they do it and fabricate it. One says "قَدْ فَرى الرَّجُلُ، يَفْرِي" when he makes something and when he cuts; from this is "فَرَيْتُ جِلْدَهُ" (I cut his skin). So its interpretation is that this saying — I mean their declaring themselves pure — is a fabrication (firya) from them. ﴿وَكَفى بِهِ إثْمًا مُبِينًا﴾, i.e. it suffices as a sin; (إثْمًا) is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), i.e. it suffices among sins.

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الكِتابِ﴾ — by it He means the scholars of the Jews, i.e. they were given knowledge of the matter of the Prophet ﷺ and concealed it. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالجِبْتِ والطّاغُوتِ﴾: the people of language said: everything worshipped besides Allah is jibt and ṭāghūt. It was said: the jibt and the ṭāghūt are the soothsayers and the devils. And it was said in some of the exegesis: the jibt and the ṭāghūt here are Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab and Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, the two Jews. This does not depart from what the people of language said, because if they followed the command of these two, they obeyed them instead of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَؤُلاءِ أهْدى مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَبِيلا﴾ — this is a proof and an indication of the obstinacy of the Jews, because they claimed that those who believed in none of the scriptures and (practised) idol-worship were better guided in way than those who agree with them on much of what they believe. This is manifest obstinacy.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿سَبِيلا﴾ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), just as you say "هَذا أحْسَنُ مِنكَ وجْهًا" (this one is better than you in face) and "هَذا أجْوَدُ مِنكَ ثَوْبًا" (this one is finer than you in garment), because in your saying "هَذا أجْوَدُ مِنكَ" you have left vague the thing in which you preferred him — unless you mean that he as a whole is finer than you as a whole, in which case you say "هَذا أجْوَدُ مِنكَ" and stop.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾, i.e. those whom He has distanced from His mercy. We have explained that cursing (laʿna) is distancing throughout the language.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَلْعَنِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ نَصِيرًا﴾, i.e. whomever Allah distances from His mercy is forsaken in his claim and his argument, and overcome. The Jews in particular are the most manifestly forsaken, in that they were overcome from among all the followers of the other religions, because they were the most obstinate, and because they concealed the truth while they knew it.

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿أمْ لَهم نَصِيبٌ مِنَ المُلْكِ﴾ — the meaning is: nay, do they have a share of the kingdom?! ﴿فَإذًا لا يُؤْتُونَ النّاسَ نَقِيرًا﴾ — some said: its meaning is only that had they been given the kingdom, they would not have given people (even) a naqīr (the speck on a date-stone). The mention of the naqīr here is a representation; the meaning is: they would have been niggardly with (even) a little. As for the nominative of "يُؤْتُونَ", it is on the basis of "فَلا يُؤْتُونَ النّاسَ نَقِيرًا إذَنْ" (then they would not give people a naqīr). Whoever put it in the accusative and said "فَإذًا لا يُؤْتُوا النّاسَ" — that is permissible for him outside of recitation; as for the Muṣḥaf, it is not to be contradicted.
Sībawayh said: "إذًا" among the operatives (ʿawāmil) of verbs is in the position of "أظُنُّ" (I think) among the operatives of nouns. So if you begin with "إذَنْ" intending the future, you use the accusative and nothing else; you say "إذَنْ أُكْرِمَكَ" (then I will honour you). If you make it parenthetical you cancel it, and say "أنا إذَنْ أُكْرِمُكَ", i.e. "أنا أُكْرِمُكَ إذَنْ" (I will honour you, then). If you bring it with wāw or fāʾ, you say "فَإذًا أُكْرِمُكَ", or if you wish "فَإذَنْ أُكْرِمَكَ". Whoever says "فَإذَنْ أُكْرِمَكَ" governs the accusative with it and makes the fāʾ attached to it in wording and meaning; and whoever says "فَإذَنْ أُكْرِمُكَ" makes "إذًا" void (laghw) and makes the fāʾ in meaning attached to "أُكْرِمُكَ", the meaning being "فَأُكْرِمُكَ إذَنْ" (so I will honour you, then). The interpretation of "إذَنْ" is: if the matter is as you mentioned, or as has happened. Someone says "زَيْدٌ يَصِيرُ إلَيْكَ" (Zayd is coming to you), and you answer, saying "إذَنْ أُكْرِمُهُ" (then I will honour him); its interpretation is: if the matter is as you describe, his being honoured will occur. So "أنْ" together with "أُكْرِمُهُ" is implied after "إذَنْ"; the meaning is: "your being honoured will occur if the matter is as you said". Sībawayh said: one of the companions of al-Khalīl related from al-Khalīl that "أنْ" is the operative in the chapter of "إذَنْ". As for Sībawayh, what he holds, and what we relate from him, is that "إذَنْ" itself is what governs the accusative. That is because "إذَنْ" is for the future and nothing else in the state of al-nasab «[Translator's note: so in the text (النَّسَبِ); presumably النَّصْبِ, "the accusative", is intended.]», so he made it like "أنْ" in governing, just as "لَكِنَّ" was made the counterpart of "إنَّ" in governing nouns. Both views are good and fine, except that the operative of the accusative in all verbs is, in my view, "أنْ" — and that is better — whether it occurs overt or implied (muḍmara), because the nominative of the future (imperfect) verb is by virtue of its resemblance (muḍāraʿa) (to nouns), so its accusative must be, in what resembles it, that which governs the accusative in the chapter of nouns. You say "أظُنُّ أنَّكَ مُنْطَلِقٌ" (I think that you are departing), and the meaning is "أظُنُّ انْطِلاقَكَ" (I think your departure); and you say "أرْجُو أنْ تَذْهَبَ" (I hope that you go), i.e. "أرْجُو ذَهابَكَ" (I hope for your going). So the light "أنْ" with the future verb is like the maṣdar (verbal noun), just as the heavy "أنَّ" with its noun and predicate is like the maṣdar, and that is the respect in which they resemble each other.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أمْ يَحْسُدُونَ النّاسَ عَلى ما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ — its meaning is: nay, do they envy people?! Here He means by it the Prophet ﷺ. The Jews had envied him for the prophethood Allah gave him, though they knew that prophethood was in "the family of Abraham" — peace be upon him. So it was said to them: do you envy the Prophet ﷺ when prophethood was in his family, and they are the family of Abraham — peace be upon them both? It was said in the exegesis: the Jews said that the Prophet's ﷺ concern is women, out of envy for what was made lawful to him of them; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that the family of Abraham had been given a great kingdom. Some said: they obtained more of women than Muḥammad ﷺ obtained: David had a hundred wives, and Solomon had a thousand, between free women and slave women; so what is the matter with them that they envied the Prophet ﷺ?

zajjaj:55-55.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمِنهم مَن آمَنَ بِهِ﴾, i.e. who believed in the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿وَمِنهم مَن صَدَّ عَنْهُ﴾. It was also said: "مِنهم مَن آمَنَ بِهِ", i.e. in this report about Solomon and David concerning the women they were given.
His saying: ﴿وَكَفى بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا﴾ — the meaning is: Hell suffices in intensity of blaze.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ نارًا﴾, i.e. We will roast them in a fire. It is related that a Jewish woman presented to the Prophet ﷺ a "مَصْلِيَّة" sheep, i.e. a roasted one.
His saying: ﴿كُلَّما نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهم بَدَّلْناهم جُلُودًا غَيْرَها﴾ — it is best to pronounce the tāʾ clearly here with the jīm, so that the jīms do not become many; and if you wish you may assimilate the tāʾ into the jīm, because the jīm is from the middle of the tongue and the tāʾ from its tip, and the tāʾ is a whispered (mahmūs) letter, so you assimilate it into the jīm.
If someone says: the skin that disobeyed was replaced by a skin that is not the disobedient one — that is an erroneous statement, because the one who disobeys and feels pain is the human being, not the skin. It is possible that the cooked skin is replaced and restored as his first skin was, just as you say "قَدْ صُغْتُ مِن خاتَمِي خاتَمًا آخَرَ" (I have fashioned from my ring another ring): even though you changed the fashioning, the silver is one original. The skin had decayed, after the resurrection «[Translator's note: so the text (وقد كان الجلد بلي بعد البعث); the sense seems to be that the skin had decayed and was re-created at the resurrection.]», so its re-creation after the cooking is like its re-creation after the resurrection.
His saying: ﴿لِيَذُوقُوا العَذابَ﴾, i.e. so that their pain is intensified to the utmost.
His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا﴾ — al-ʿAzīz is the one who attains His will, whom nothing overcomes, and He is together with that wise in what He disposes, because the heretics may ask about the punishment, how it occurs; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that all He does is with wisdom.

zajjaj:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾ — the meaning is: beneath them flow the waters of the rivers, because what actually flows is the water.
His saying: ﴿وَنُدْخِلُهم ظِلا ظَلِيلا﴾ — the meaning of "ظَلِيلٌ" is: it shades from the wind and the heat, and not every shade is like that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the shade of the people of Paradise is ẓalīl, with no heat and no cold with it. Likewise His saying ﴿وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 30], because not every shade is extended.

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكم أنْ تُؤَدُّوا الأماناتِ إلى أهْلِها﴾ — this is a general command to the Prophet ﷺ and his whole community. It is related in the exegesis «that al-ʿAbbās, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, asked the Prophet ﷺ to give him the office of providing water (siqāya) and the custodianship (sidāna), which is the guardianship (ḥijba), that is, that he give him, along with the siqāya, the opening and locking of the House. Shayba ibn ʿUthmān disputed it with him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, return to me what you took from me", meaning the key of the Kaʿba; so he ﷺ returned it to Shayba.» His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمّا يَعِظُكم بِهِ﴾ — this has several forms: "نِعِمّا" with kasra on the nūn and the ʿayn and assimilation of the mīm into the mīm; if you wish you may give the nūn fatḥa; and if you wish you may make the ʿayn quiescent and say "نَعْمًا". But the best in my view is assimilation with kasra on the ʿayn. As for whoever read "نِعْمْ ما" with the ʿayn and the mīm quiescent, it is something the Basrans reject; they claim that the meeting of the two quiescent letters — I mean the ʿayn and the mīm — is not permissible. What they said is clear, because it is not possible in pronunciation; one can only contrive it with difficulty in pronunciation.

zajjaj:102-102.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا كُنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾: this hāʾ and mīm refer back to the believers, that is: when you, O Prophet, are among the believers in their campaigns and their fear, ﴿فَأقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلاةَ فَلْتَقُمْ طائِفَةٌ مِنهم مَعَكَ ولْيَأْخُذُوا أسْلِحَتَهم فَإذا سَجَدُوا﴾, that is: when the party that stood with you has prostrated, ﴿فَلْيَكُونُوا مِن ورائِكم ولْتَأْتِ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ ولْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهم وأسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾. It is possible — and Allah knows best — [that it means]: let the whole group take their precautions and their weapons. And it may be that those who are facing the enemy take their weapons, because whoever is in prayer is not fighting. And it is possible that the whole group was commanded to carry weapons, even though some of them are not fighting, because that is more intimidating to the enemy and makes it more likely that he will not attack those who are wary, alert and ready for war in every state.
People have differed about the prayer of fear. Mālik ibn Anas held that the dearest to him of what has been related about it is «that the Prophet ﷺ stood to pray, and a party of the believers stood behind him and a party facing the enemy. He prayed one rakʿa with the party behind him, and stood, and the party completed another rakʿa and gave the salām while he ﷺ was standing. Then they left and stood facing the enemy, while the Prophet ﷺ was standing in the prayer, and the party that had been facing the enemy came, and he prayed with them a second rakʿa of his own, which was the first for this other party. The Prophet ﷺ sat, and they stood and prayed a second rakʿa by themselves while he ﷺ was sitting; and they sat in the second, then he gave the salām and they gave the salām with his salām. So each party of them prayed two rakʿas, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed two rakʿas.» Mālik said: "This is the dearest to me of what has been related about the prayer of fear."
As for «أسْلِحَةٌ», it is the plural of «سِلاحٌ», like «حِمارٌ» and «أحْمِرَةٌ». «سِلاحٌ» is a name for the whole of what people defend themselves with in wars, specifically what is fought with; riding animals and the like are not called «سِلاحٌ».
As for «وَلْيَأْخُذُوا», the reading is with the lām quiescent: «وَلْيَأْخُذُوا»; «وَلِيَأْخُذُوا» with kasra is the original, except that the kasra was felt to be heavy and so it is dropped for lightness. Al-Farrāʾ reported that some Arabs give the lām of command a fatḥa, in your saying «لِيَجْلِسْ», saying «لَيَجْلِسْ» with fatḥa. This is a mistake: it is not permissible to give the lām of command a fatḥa, lest it resemble the lām of emphasis. Some of the Basrans reported giving the lām of the genitive a fatḥa, as in your saying «اَلْمالُ لِزَيْدٍ», you say «اَلْمالُ لَزَيْدٍ». This report is as anomalous as the first, because the consensus and the sound transmissions are that the lām of the genitive and the lām of command take kasra, and no attention is paid to the anomalous, especially when it was not transmitted by the early grammarians, who are the source of transmission. All whom we have mentioned of those who transmitted this anomaly are, in our view, truthful in transmission, except that the one they heard it from was in error.
His saying: ﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: «اَلْجُناحُ» is sin. Its interpretation is from «جَنَحْتُ», when I turn aside from a place, that is: I took a side away from the straight course. So the interpretation of «لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم» is: you are not turning aside from the right if you lay down your weapons, ﴿إنْ كانَ بِكم أذًى مِن مَطَرٍ﴾. «أذًى» is maqṣūr (ending in a short alif); you say «أذِيَ، يَأْذى، أذًى», like «فَزِعَ، يَفْزَعُ، فَزَعًا». The position of «أنْ تَضَعُوا» is accusative, that is: there is no sin upon you in laying down; when «في» dropped, what precedes «أنْ» governed it. And its position may be genitive, in the sense of «في». [Translator's note: the phrase «أنْ تَضَعُوا أسْلِحَتَكُمْ» comes later in this verse; the source discusses it without quoting it.]

zajjaj:103-103.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإذا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلاةَ﴾: He means by it this prayer of fear. ﴿فاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ قِيامًا وقُعُودًا﴾, that is: remember Him by affirming His oneness, thanking Him, glorifying Him, and everything by which one can draw near to Him.
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿فَإذا اطْمَأْنَنْتُمْ﴾, that is: when your hearts are at rest. One says «اِطْمَأنَّ الشَّيْءُ» when a thing becomes still, and «طامَنتُهُ» and «طَمْأنْتُهُ» when I have stilled it. «اِطْبَأنَّ» with bāʾ has also been transmitted, but do not read with it, because the muṣḥaf is not to be contradicted at all.
His saying: ﴿فَأقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾, that is: complete it, because in fear they were granted shortening it, and in safety they were commanded to complete it.
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الصَّلاةَ كانَتْ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ كِتابًا مَوْقُوتًا﴾, that is: obligatory, its obligation fixed in time.

zajjaj:104-104.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَهِنُوا في ابْتِغاءِ القَوْمِ﴾: this is addressed to the believers, and «القَوْمِ» here are the disbelievers who are at war with the believers. The interpretation of «لا تَهِنُوا» in the language is: do not weaken. One says «وَهَنَ الرَّجُلُ، يَهِنُ» when he weakens, so he is «وَهِنٌ». The meaning of «اِبْتِغاءِ القَوْمِ» is: seeking out the people in war.
His saying: ﴿إنْ تَكُونُوا تَأْلَمُونَ فَإنَّهُمْ﴾, that is: if you are suffering pain, they feel pain from the wounds and fatigue that afflict them just as you feel it; and you, besides that, ﴿وَتَرْجُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ ما لا يَرْجُونَ﴾, that is: you hope for the victory Allah promised you, and for your religion to prevail over all the religions of the communities opposed to the people of Islam, and besides that you hope for Paradise, while they — I mean the idolaters — hope for Paradise [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires "do not hope for Paradise", as the following reason shows], because they did not affirm the resurrection; so you hope from Allah for what they do not hope for.
One of the exegetes said: the meaning of «تَرْجُونَ» here is "you fear". The people of the language whose knowledge is relied upon agree that rajāʾ here is in the sense of hope, not explicitly fear. Some of them said: rajāʾ is not used in the sense of fear except with negation. The poet said:
؎لا تَرْتَجِي حِينَ تُلاقِي الذّائِدا ∗∗∗ أسَبْعَةً لاقَتْ مَعًا أمْ واحِدا
(She does not fear, when she meets the one who drives [her] off, whether she has met seven together or one.)
Its meaning is "she does not fear". Likewise His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 13], that is: you do not fear Allah's greatness, nor [heed] admonition. Rajāʾ came to include the meaning of fear only because rajāʾ is a hope which one may fear will not be fulfilled.

zajjaj:105-105.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكَ الكِتابَ بِالحَقِّ لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النّاسِ بِما أراكَ اللَّهُ﴾, that is: by the truth which Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known to you.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَكُنْ لِلْخائِنِينَ خَصِيمًا﴾, that is: do not be a disputant on behalf of, nor a defender of, a traitor. It is related that a man of the Anṣār who was called "Abū Ṭuʿma" or "Ṭiʿma" stole a coat of mail and put it in a sack of flour which had a hole in it, so the flour scattered from the place of his theft to his house. He was suspected of being the thief of the coat of mail, and he was hard pressed in his affair, so he took the coat of mail to a man of the Jews and deposited it with him. Then he went to his people and informed them that when he was accused over the coat of mail its trail was followed, and it was found to be with the Jew, and that the Jew was its thief. So his people — that is, of Ṭuʿma or Ṭiʿma — came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him to clear him before the people, and informed him that the Jew was the one with the coat of mail. Some of them knew that Abū Ṭiʿma had accused the Jew while he was innocent of the coat of mail. The Prophet ﷺ was about to clear him, but Allah revealed to him and acquainted him with his story — that is, Ṭuʿma's — and informed him that he was a traitor, forbade him to argue on his behalf, and commanded him to seek forgiveness for what he had been about to do and to judge by what Allah had revealed in His Book. So He said:

zajjaj:107-107.t: ﴿وَلا تُجادِلْ عَنِ الَّذِينَ يَخْتانُونَ أنْفُسَهم إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ مَن كانَ خَوّانًا أثِيمًا﴾: He means Abū Ṭuʿma and those of his people who helped him while knowing that he was a thief. It is related that this Abū Ṭuʿma fled to Mecca and apostatised from Islam, and that he bored through a wall in Mecca in order to rob its people, and the wall fell on him and killed him.

zajjaj:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ ما لا يَرْضى مِنَ القَوْلِ﴾: everything that is thought over, or gone into, by night has been «بُيِّتَ» (plotted by night).
He means by it this thief, and the speech he plotted by night was that he said: "I will accuse the Jew of being the thief of the coat of mail and swear that I did not steal it, and my oath will be accepted because I am of my religion, and the Jew's oath will not be accepted." This is what he plotted by night of speech — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿ها أنْتُمْ هَؤُلاءِ جادَلْتُمْ عَنْهم في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾: He means by it whoever argued on behalf of this thief. ﴿فَمَن يُجادِلُ اللَّهَ عَنْهم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾, that is: on the day in which [people] are taken to account according to realities, whereas the affair of this world rests on testimonies in matters of rights, and it is possible for testimony to be untrue. So it is as though — and Allah knows best — it were said to them: if disputing and concealing the affair of this thief succeeds in this world, then on the Day of Resurrection neither disputing nor testimony will avail.
The meaning of His saying «ها أنْتُمْ»: «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and it is repeated in «أُولاءِ». The meaning — and Allah knows best — is «ها أنْتُمُ الَّذِينَ جادَلْتُمْ» ("here you are, the ones who disputed"), because «هَؤُلاءِ» and «هَذا», in pointing to those addressed, are in the position of «اَلَّذِينَ» (relative noun), as in the poet's saying:
وَهَذا تَحْمِلِينَ طَلِيقُ
(And this [one] you carry is free.)
That is: «والَّذِي تَحْمِلِينَهُ طَلِيقٌ» ("and the one whom you carry is free").
The root of «المُجادَلَةُ» and «الجِدالُ» in the language is intense contention. «اَلْجَدْلُ» is intensity of killing, and «رَجُلٌ مَجْدُولٌ» means: as though he had been killed. [Translator's note: the source reads «شِدَّةُ القَتْلِ» and «قُتِلَ» ("killing", "killed"); the lexicons have «شِدَّةُ الفَتْلِ» ("tightness of twisting") and «فُتِلَ» ("twisted"), which is probably the intended reading.] «اَلْأجْدَلُ» is the falcon; it is called «أجْدَلُ» because it is among the strongest of birds.

zajjaj:110-110.t: Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that repentance is available for every sin short of shirk (associating partners with Allah), so He — exalted be His praise — said: ﴿وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾, that is: he asks Him for forgiveness while desisting, because if he remains persistent he is not repentant.

zajjaj:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَكْسِبْ إثْمًا فَإنَّما يَكْسِبُهُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ﴾: and no one is taken to account for [another's] sin. [Translator's note: the source reads «ولا يُؤْخَذُ الإثْمُ بِالإثْمِ», literally "a sin is not taken for a sin".]
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أوْ إثْمًا ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 112]: «إثْمًا» is said because Allah has named some acts of disobedience «خَطايا» (faults) and named some of them «آثامًا» (sins). So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that whoever earns a fault — to which the name "sin" or the name "fault" applies — and then casts it upon one who did not do it and is innocent of it, ﴿فَقَدِ احْتَمَلَ بُهْتانًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 112]. «اَلْبُهْتانُ» is a lie at whose enormity and plainness one is left bewildered. One says «قَدْ بَهَتَ فُلانٌ فُلانًا» when he has lied about him, and «قَدْ بُهِتَ الرَّجُلُ، يُبْهَتُ» when he is bewildered. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 258]. And it may be — and Allah knows best — that «وَمَن يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أوْ إثْمًا» means: whoever commits an error, such as killing by error into which people fall and in which there is no sin, and then casts that upon someone else, has borne a calumny.

zajjaj:113-113.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ ورَحْمَتُهُ لَهَمَّتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنهم أنْ يُضِلُّوكَ﴾: this is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, and the party are [the people of] Ṭuʿma, this thief [Translator's note: the source reads «والطّائِفَةُ هم طُعْمَةُ هَذا السّارِقُ», "the party are Ṭuʿma this thief"; the reference is evidently to his people], because some of them had learned that he was a thief and [yet] asked the Prophet ﷺ to clear him. So the interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: were it not for Allah's favour upon you and His mercy, in what He revealed to you and made known to you about this thief, a party would have resolved to lead you astray. The meaning of «هَمَّتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنهم أنْ يُضِلُّوكَ» is: by Allah's favour and mercy, Allah turned you away from doing what the party had resolved upon. Some said: the meaning of «أنْ يُضِلُّوكَ» is: to make you err in your judgement.
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَما يُضِلُّونَ إلا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾, that is: because they are the ones doing the deeds of those astray, and Allah protects His Prophet ﷺ from following them, so the leading astray returns upon them and befalls them.
His saying: ﴿وَما يَضُرُّونَكَ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾, that is: given Allah's protection of you and His support of His religion, the religion of truth.
His saying: ﴿وَأنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الكِتابَ والحِكْمَةَ﴾, that is: He made clear in His Book that in which is the wisdom with which no going astray befalls you.

zajjaj:114-114.t:
His saying: ﴿لا خَيْرَ في كَثِيرٍ مِن نَجْواهُمْ﴾: najwā in speech is what a group or two people confine to themselves, whether secret or open. The meaning of «نَجَوْتُ الشَّيْءَ» in the language is: I extricated it and cast it off. One says «نَجَوْتُ الجِلْدَ» when you have stripped the hide off a camel or another animal. The poet said:
؎فَقُلْتُ انْجُوا عَنْها نَجا الجِلْدِ إنَّهُ ∗∗∗ سَيُرْضِيكُما مِنها سَنامٌ وغارِبُهْ
(I said: strip the hide off her, for her hump and its withers will satisfy you both.)
And «قَدْ نَجَوْتُ فُلانًا» when I have smelt his breath. The poet said:
؎نَجَوْتُ مُجالِدًا فَوَجَدْتُ مِنهُ ∗∗∗ كَرِيحِ الكَلْبِ ماتَ حَدِيثَ عَهْدِ
(I smelt Mujālid's breath and found from him something like the smell of a dog that has recently died.)
And «نَجَوْتُ الوَبَرَ» and «اِسْتَنْجَيْتُهُ» when I have extricated it. The poet said:
؎فَتَبازَتْ فَتَبازَخْتُ لَها ∗∗∗ جِلْسَةَ الأعْسَرِ يَسْتَنْجِي الوَتَرْ
(She thrust out her hindquarters and I bent back for her, in the sitting of a left-handed man drawing out the bowstring.)
The root of all of it is from «اَلنَّجْوَةُ», which is raised ground. The poet said:
؎فَمَن بِنَجْوَتِهِ كَمَن بِعَقْوَتِهِ ∗∗∗ والمُسْتَكِنُّ كَمَن يَمْشِي بِقِرْواحِ
(He who is on his high ground is like him who is in his courtyard, and the one sheltering is like him who walks on open bare land.)
And one says «ما أنْجى فُلانٌ شَيْئًا» and «ما نَجا شَيْئًا مُنْذُ أيّامٍ», that is: he has not relieved himself.
The meaning — and Allah knows best — of «لا خَيْرَ في كَثِيرٍ مِن نَجْواهم» is: of the speech they contrive among themselves, ﴿إلا مَن أمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أوْ مَعْرُوفٍ أوْ إصْلاحٍ بَيْنَ النّاسِ﴾. The position of «مَن» may be genitive (khafḍ); the meaning is: except in the private talk of [one who enjoins] charity, or kindness, or reconciliation between people. And it may be — and Allah knows best — an exception not from the first [category], its position being accusative, in the sense of «لَكِنَّ مَن أمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أوْ مَعْرُوفٍ فَفي نَجْواهُ خَيْرٌ» ("but whoever enjoins charity or kindness, in his private talk there is good").
Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this only benefits one who seeks by it what is with Allah, and said: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾. The meaning of «اِبْتِغاءَ مَرْضاةِ اللَّهِ» is: seeking Allah's good pleasure. «اِبْتِغاءَ مَرْضاةِ اللَّهِ» is accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: whoever does that for the seeking of Allah's good pleasure. And it goes back to the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He said: «وَمَن يَبْتَغِ ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاةِ اللَّهِ» ("whoever seeks a seeking of Allah's good pleasure"). Then the matter returned to mention of this Ṭuʿma and those like him, and He said:

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا النِّساءَ صَدُقاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً﴾. One says: it is the woman's ṣadāq (dower), and the woman's ṣaduqa, and the woman's ṣuduqa.

”صَداقُ المَرْأةِ“ has an open vowel (fatḥa) on its first letter. What is in the Quran is the plural of ”صَدُقَةٌ“.
