Whoever says ”صُدْقَةٌ“ says ”صُدُقاتِهِنَّ“, just as one says ”غُرْفَةٌ“ / ”غُرُفاتٌ“ ("room/rooms"). ”صُدْقاتِهِنَّ“ is permissible, and ”صُدَقاتِهِنَّ“ with a ḍamma on the ṣād and a fatḥa on the dāl, and ”صُدُقاتِهِنَّ“ is permissible. But do not on any account read any of these except what has actually been read, because reading [the Quran] is a sunna (established practice) in which one should not read with everything the grammarians allow. If you follow [what is transmitted], then what has been transmitted of the well-known [forms] in reading is the best according to the grammarians; so in reading — with what has been transmitted — following [the transmission] and affirming what is stronger in proof come together, if Allah wills.

As for the meaning of His saying ﴿نِحْلَةً﴾, there is more than one view about it. Some of them said: "an obligation". Some of them said: "a religious duty" (دِيانَةً); you say ”فُلانٌ يَنْتَحِلُ كَذا وكَذا“, that is, he professes it as his religion. Some of them said: it is a gift (نَحْلَةٌ) from Allah to them, in that He placed the dower upon the men and placed no liability of any kind upon the woman; so that is a gift from Allah to women. One says: ”نَحَلْتُ الرَّجُلَ والمَرْأةَ“ — when you have given to him [or her] as a gift — ”نِحْلَةً، ونُحْلًا“. One also says ”قَدْ نَحِلَ جِسْمُ فُلانٍ، ونَحَلَ“ when [his body] has become thin. As for ”اَلنَّحْلُ“ (bees), it is possible that they were named ”نَحْلًا“ because Allah — exalted be His praise — "gifted" (نَحَلَ) people the honey that comes out of their bellies.

His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿فَإنْ طِبْنَ لَكم عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنهُ نَفْسًا﴾, that is: of something of the dower. ”لَكم“ is an address to the husbands; some of them said: to the guardians here. ”نَفْسًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), because when He says ”طِبْنَ لَكم“ ("they are pleased for you"), it is not known in what category the pleasure occurred; the meaning is: if their souls are pleased with that. We explained it fully before this place.

His saying: ﴿فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا﴾. One says: ”هَنَأنِي الطَّعامُ ومَرَأنِي“ ("the food was wholesome and agreeable to me"). Some of them said: together with ”هَنَأنِي“ one says ”مَرَأنِي“, but if you do not mention ”هَنَأنِي“, you say ”أمْرَأنِي“ with the alif. Its real sense is that ”مَرَأنِي“ [means] I perceived that it would be digested and I commend its after-effect; and when you say ”أمْرَأنِي الطَّعامُ“, its interpretation is that it has been digested and its after-effect has been commended.

If someone says: "It was only said ﴿فَإنْ طِبْنَ لَكم عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنهُ نَفْسًا﴾ ('of something of it'); so how may the man accept the whole dower, when he was only told 'of it' (”مِنهُ“)?" — the answer to that is that ”مِنهُ“ here is for the genus, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Hajj: 30]; we were not commanded to avoid [only] some of the idols, but the meaning is: avoid the abomination which is idols. That is: so eat the thing which is the dower.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أمْوالَكُمُ﴾. Some of them said: "the foolish" are women and children. Some of them said: "the foolish" are the orphans. [The form] ”اَلسُّفَهاءُ“ indicates that He does not mean women alone by it, because for women the plural of ”سَفِيهَةٌ“ that is mostly used is ”سَفائِهُ“, though ”سُفَهاءُ“ is permissible, as one says ”فَقِيرَةٌ“ / ”فُقَراءُ“. Some of them said: its meaning is "do not make gifts of your wealth to the foolish". In my view — and Allah knows best — this is not permissible (and so said our colleagues the Basrans); rather, the foolish person is more deserving of a gift because earning is difficult for him, and if we were forbidden to make gifts to them, it would not be permissible for us to make them heirs. The meaning of ”وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أمْوالَكم“ is only: do not give the foolish their [own] wealth. The proof of that is His saying: ﴿وارْزُقُوهم فِيها واكْسُوهُمْ﴾, and His saying: ﴿فَإنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِنهم رُشْدًا فادْفَعُوا إلَيْهِمْ أمْوالَهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisa: 6]. It was said ”أمْوالَكم“ ("your wealth") only because its meaning is "the thing by which your affairs are sustained", just as Allah said: ﴿ثُمَّ أنْتُمْ هَؤُلاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 85], while no man among them killed himself; rather, some of them killed others, that is: you kill the kind which is your own kind.

It has been read: ”اَللّاتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكم قِيامًا“ and ”قِيَمًا“. One says: ”هَذا قِوامُ الأمْرِ ومِلاكُهُ“ ("this is the mainstay of the matter and its foundation"). The meaning is: [the wealth] which Allah has made to sustain you, so that you stand by it in a [proper] standing (qiyām); so it goes back to this. And the meaning [of qiyam] is: Allah has made it the value of things, so by it your affairs are maintained.

﴿وَقُولُوا لَهم قَوْلا مَعْرُوفًا﴾, that is: teach them — along with your feeding them and clothing them — the matter of their religion.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وابْتَلُوا اليَتامى﴾ means: test the orphans. ﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغُوا النِّكاحَ فَإنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِنهم رُشْدًا﴾: the meaning of ”آنَسْتُمْ“ is: you know; and the meaning of ”اَلرَّشْدُ“ is the upright course of conduct with which you trust that they will safeguard their wealth — then hand over their wealth to them. ﴿وَلا تَأْكُلُوها إسْرافًا وبِدارًا أنْ يَكْبَرُوا﴾, that is: hastening [to consume it] ahead of their growing up. Some of them said: "do not consume it extravagantly" [means]: do not consume of it, but eat [only] sustenance in proportion to your benefit to them in your guardianship over them. Some of them said: the meaning of ﴿وَمَن كانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ is: let him eat by way of a loan, and not take anything from the orphan's wealth, because what is right and recognised (al-maʿrūf) is that a person consumes his own wealth and does not consume the wealth of another. He said: the proof of that is His saying: ﴿فَإذا دَفَعْتُمْ إلَيْهِمْ أمْوالَهم فَأشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمّا تَرَكَ الوالِدانِ والأقْرَبُونَ ولِلنِّساءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمّا تَرَكَ الوالِدانِ والأقْرَبُونَ مِمّا قَلَّ مِنهُ أوْ كَثُرَ﴾. The Arabs used to give inheritance only to one who fought with spears, defended property and gained booty. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the right of inheritance is according to the shares that have been mentioned. «A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ with daughters of hers whose father — her husband — had died, and the two paternal uncles of the girls had resolved to take the property. Then there was revealed: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ في أوْلادِكم لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾ [al-Nisa: 11], the verse. The two uncles said: "O Messenger of Allah, does one inherit who does not fight with spears, does not defend property and does not gain booty?" He ﷺ said: "Give the daughters two-thirds, and give the wife — who is their mother — one-eighth, and what remains is yours." They said: "Then who will take charge of looking after their affairs?" So the Prophet ﷺ commanded the two of them to take charge of that.»

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: these have shares, as we mentioned, in the state of being obligatory. This is emphatic speech, because His saying — exalted be His praise —: ﴿لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمّا تَرَكَ الوالِدانِ والأقْرَبُونَ ولِلنِّساءِ نَصِيبٌ﴾ means: that is made obligatory for them.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإذا حَضَرَ القِسْمَةَ أُولُو القُرْبى واليَتامى والمَساكِينُ فارْزُقُوهم مِنهُ﴾, that is: give them some of it.

Al-Ḥasan — Allah's mercy be upon him — and al-Nakhaʿī said: "We found people dividing among the relatives, the poor and the orphans from the cash" — the two of them meaning silver and gold — "and when the silver and gold had been divided and the division came to lands, slaves and the like, they would speak to them with kind words (qawlan maʿrūfan); they would say to them: May you be blessed." Some people said: the command [to give] to the poor and those mentioned in this verse was abrogated by the prescribed shares in the division and by permitting the deceased a third, to assign wherever he wishes. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: They are agreed that the command to share out from the inheritance to kin, the poor and the orphans was indeed commanded, and they are not agreed that it was abrogated; so the matter in that rests on what has been agreed upon, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِن خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعافًا خافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾. The [usual] speech has ”ذُرِّيَّةً“ with a ḍamma on the dhāl; ”ذِرِّيَّةً“ with a kasra on the dhāl is permissible, and it has been read both ways, except that the ḍamma is better. It is related to ”اَلذَّرُّ“ (tiny ants / particles), being a fuʿliyya [form] from it. Its origin may also be ”ذُرُّورَةٌ“, but the rāʾ was replaced by a yāʾ and the wāw was assimilated into it. As for the kasra on the dhāl, it is because of the kasra on the rāʾ, as they said ”عِتِيٌّ“ for ”عُتِيٌّ“. ”ضِعافٌ“ is the plural of ”ضَعِيفٌ“ and ”ضَعِيفَةٌ“, as you say ”ظَرِيفٌ“ / ”ظِرافٌ“ and ”خَبِيثٌ“ / ”خِباثٌ“; if ”ضُعَفاءُ“ were said, it would be permissible; you say ”ضَعِيفٌ“ / ”ضُعَفاءُ“.

It has been said that the meaning of the verse is that they used to bequeath their wealth according to their whims and leave the weak among their offspring and children [without provision], so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — commanded them to make bequests for them and to carry that out in a proper way. It has also been said: this was said to them on account of the orphans; they were admonished, in their guardianship of orphans, to do as they would like to be done to their own children after them. Both views are permissible and good, except that the "naming of the shares" [of inheritance] abrogated that, through the portions He assigned to the children and to the agnatic relatives.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
Then Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — gave warning, was severe in the matter of orphans and threatened, saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أمْوالَ اليَتامى ظُلْمًا إنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ في بُطُونِهِمْ نارًا وسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا﴾. It is [also] read: ”وَسَيُصْلَوْنَ“ (passive).

In this — I mean in His saying ”يَأْكُلُونَ أمْوالَ اليَتامى“ — is a proof that if something is taken from the orphan's wealth in proportion to looking after him, without exceeding that, it is permissible; but rather one should take precaution in it, if possible, by not touching it at all, because of the severity of the threat concerning it, so that nothing is consumed of it except as a loan. And if one takes a moderate amount, according to need and in proportion to one's benefit to him, there is no harm, if Allah wills.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأُولِي الأمْرِ مِنكُمْ﴾, i.e. obey those in authority among you. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded obedience to Him in what He made obligatory, and obedience to His Messenger and belief in him in what he conveyed from Allah. Those in authority among them are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those of the people of knowledge who followed them. It was also said that they are the commanders (umarāʾ); and the commanders, when they are people of knowledge and religion who adhere to what the people of knowledge say, obedience to them is obligatory. In sum, those in authority among the Muslims are whoever undertakes their affairs in the matter of their religion and everything that leads to its soundness. One says "أدَّيْتُ الشَّيْءَ تَأْدِيَةً" (I conveyed the thing), and al-adāʾ is a noun with long final alif (mamdūd); and "أدَوْتُ الرَّجُلَ، آدُو لَهُ، أدْوًا" when I stalk him to deceive him. The poet said:
أدَوْتُ لَهُ لِأخْتِلَهُ ∗∗∗ فَهَيْهاتَ الفَتى حَذَرا
(I stalked him to deceive him — but how far off! The young man was on his guard.)
And "أدِيَ اللَّبَنُ، أدْيًا" when the milk turns sour.
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ تَنازَعْتُمْ في شَيْءٍ فَرُدُّوهُ إلى اللَّهِ والرَّسُولِ﴾ — the meaning of "تَنازَعْتُمْ" is: you differed and disputed, and each party said: "the (correct) view is my view." The derivation of munāzaʿa (disputing) is that each of the two pulls (yanziʿu) at the argument. In this verse there is an emphatic command indicating that deliberately seeking disagreement is disbelief, and that faith is following the consensus (ijmāʿ) and the Sunna. His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿فَرُدُّوهُ إلى اللَّهِ والرَّسُولِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ cannot be other than one of two things: either you refer what you differ about to the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger, or — if you do not know it — you say: Allah and His Messenger know best. ﴿ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ وأحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلا﴾, i.e. your referring what you differ about to what has come from Allah, and your abandoning fighting one another, is better and best in outcome (taʾwīl) for you, i.e. better in consequence for you. It is also possible that "أحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا" means: better than your own interpretation without your referring it to the Book and the Sunna. "تَأْوِيلًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ أنَّهم آمَنُوا بِما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ وما أُنْـزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ — by it the hypocrites are meant. "أنَّهم" stands in for the noun (object) of "claiming" and its predicate.
His saying: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أنْ يَتَحاكَمُوا إلى الطّاغُوتِ﴾: to the soothsayer and to Satan.
It is related «that a man of the hypocrites was in dispute with a man of the Jews. The Jew said: "Between me and you is Abū al-Qāsim." The hypocrite said: "Between me and you is the soothsayer." The Jew was not content with the soothsayer, and went to the Prophet ﷺ, who judged in favour of the Jew against the hypocrite. The hypocrite said: "I am not content; between me and you is Abū Bakr." Abū Bakr also judged in favour of the Jew, and the hypocrite was not content, and said: "Between me and you is ʿUmar." So they went to ʿUmar, and the Jew informed him that the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr had judged against the hypocrite and he was not content with their judgement. ʿUmar said to the hypocrite: "Is that so?" He said: "Yes." ʿUmar said: "Wait, both of you, for I have a need; I will go in, attend to it and come out to you." He went in, took his sword, came out to the hypocrite, and struck him with the sword until he killed him. His family came and complained of ʿUmar to the Prophet ﷺ, who asked him about his story. ʿUmar said: "He rejected your judgement, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah said: "You are al-Fārūq (the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood)."»

zajjaj:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم تَعالَوْا إلى ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ وإلى الرَّسُولِ رَأيْتَ المُنافِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْكَ صُدُودًا﴾, i.e. they turn away from your judgement.

zajjaj:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذا أصابَتْهم مُصِيبَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾, i.e. so how will their state be when their companion was killed for the treachery he displayed and his rejection of the judgement of the Prophet ﷺ?
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ جاءُوكَ يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إنْ أرَدْنا إلا إحْسانًا وتَوْفِيقًا﴾, i.e. we intended by our demanding the blood (money) of our companion nothing but good and seeking what accords with the truth.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ — Allah knows what is in the hearts of these and the hearts of others, but the benefit of mentioning here "اَلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ" is: those are the ones whom Allah knows to be hypocrites; and the benefit for us is: "know that they are hypocrites".
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأعْرِضْ عَنْهم وعِظْهم وقُلْ لَهم في أنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلا بَلِيغًا﴾, i.e. inform them that if rejection of your judgement and disbelief appear from them, killing is their due. One says "قَوْلٌ بَلِيغٌ" (eloquent speech) when (the speaker) conveys by the expression of his tongue the essence of what is in his heart. One also says "أحْمَقُ بَلْغٌ، وبُلْغٌ" (a fool who is balgh / bulgh), and there are two views about it: that he is a fool who (nonetheless) reaches where he wants; and that "أحْمَقُ بَلْغٌ وبُلْغٌ" means one who has reached the utmost in foolishness. The first view is the view of one whose knowledge is trusted, and the second is a good interpretation.

zajjaj:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن رَسُولٍ إلا لِيُطاعَ بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. permission was given for that. "مِن" has entered for emphasis (tawkīd); the meaning is: We did not send a messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah.
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّهم إذْ ظَلَمُوا أنْفُسَهم جاءُوكَ فاسْتَغْفَرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ — "أنَّ" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ); the meaning is: if their coming had occurred at the time of their wronging themselves, along with their seeking forgiveness, ﴿لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوّابًا رَحِيمًا﴾.

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا ورَبِّكَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — by it the hypocrites are meant — ﴿حَتّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيما شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, i.e. in the disagreement that occurred between them, ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُوا في أنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِمّا قَضَيْتَ﴾, i.e. their breasts are not constricted by your judgement, ﴿وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا﴾, i.e. they submit to whatever judgement of yours comes, not opposing it with anything. "تَسْلِيمًا" is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) (maṣdar muʾakkid), and emphatic maṣdars are equivalent to mentioning the verb a second time: as if, when you said "سَلَّمْتُ تَسْلِيمًا" (I submitted a submitting), you had said "سَلَّمْتُ سَلَّمْتُ" (I submitted, I submitted). The function of emphasis is to confirm what you mention at the beginning of your speech: when you say "ضَرَبْتُ ضَرْبًا" (I struck a striking), it is as if you said "I brought about a striking which I affirm and do not doubt". Likewise "وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا", i.e. they submit to your judgement with a submission into which they admit no doubt.

zajjaj:66-66.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ أنّا كَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أنِ اقْتُلُوا أنْفُسَكم أوِ اخْرُجُوا مِن دِيارِكُمْ﴾ — "لَوْ" is that by which a thing is prevented because of the non-occurrence of something else; you say "لَوْ جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ لَجِئْتُهُ" (had Zayd come to me, I would have come to him), the meaning being that my coming did not occur because Zayd's coming did not occur. So its due is to be followed by verbs, except that the doubled "أنَّ" occurs after it, because "أنَّ" in the language stands in for the noun and the predicate: you say "ظَنَنْتُ أنَّكَ عالِمٌ" (I thought that you are learned), and this is like your saying "ظَنَنْتُكَ عالِمًا" (I thought you learned), the meaning being "ظَنَنْتُ عِلْمَكَ" (I thought your being learned). So the sense of "أنَّ" after "لَوْ" is that it stands in for the verb and the noun, just as it stands in for the noun and the predicate. So the meaning of His saying ﴿وَلَوْ أنّا كَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ is like the meaning of "لَوْ كَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ" (had We prescribed for them). It is also possible that the verb is implied with "أنَّ", with the occurrence of what corresponds to it; the meaning is: "and had it occurred that We prescribed for them: kill yourselves or leave your homes, they would not have done it except a few of them". If you wish you may give it (the nūn of أنْ) kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters — I mean "أنِ اقْتُلُوا أنْفُسَكم" — and if you wish you may say "أنُ اقْتُلُوا", giving it ḍamma because of the ḍamma on the tāʾ.
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ chooses kasra with the nūns specifically, and with everything else in the Quran — when what follows has ḍamma — the ḍamma, except His saying ﴿وَقالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ [Yūsuf: 31] and ﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 32]. I do not know why Abū ʿAmr singled out these two words for kasra, unless he related a transmission and so chose kasra for this reason, or he meant that kasra is also permissible just as ḍamma is permissible — and this is the better of the two interpretations. Kasra and ḍamma in these words are two good ways, and the readers have read with both. As for the nominative of ﴿إلا قَلِيلٌ مِنهُمْ﴾, it is as a badal (substitute) from the wāw; the meaning is: "none did it except a few of them". The accusative is permissible outside the Quran, in the sense of "they did not do it — I except a few of them", and according to what we explained concerning the accusative of the excepted. If in the negation there are two different kinds, the preferred choice is the accusative, and the badal is permissible; you say "ما بِالدّارِ أحَدٌ إلّا حِمارًا" (there is no one in the house except a donkey). al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
وَقَفْتُ فِيها أُصَيْلالًا أُسائِلُها ∗∗∗ عَيَّتْ جَوابًا وما بِالرَّبْعِ مِن أحَدِ
(I stood there in the late afternoon questioning it; it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the encampment,)
إلّا الأوارِيَّ لَأْيًا ما أُبَيِّنُها ∗∗∗ والنُّؤْيُ كالحَوْضِ بِالمَظْلُومَةِ الجَلَدِ
(except the tethering-posts, which I could barely make out, and the trench around the tent like a cistern in hard, untrodden ground.)
So he said "ما بِالرَّبْعِ مِن أحَدٍ", i.e. there is no one in the encampment, except tethering-posts, because tethering-posts are not people. The nominative as a badal may also be permissible even if it is not of the genus of the first, as the poet said:
وَبَلْدَةٍ لَيْسَ بِها أنِيسُ ∗∗∗ إلّا اليَعافِيرُ وإلّا العِيسُ
(And many a land in which there is no companion except the gazelles and the white camels.)
So he made the gazelles and the camels a badal from the companion; and it is possible that the companions of that land are the gazelles and the camels.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحَسُنَ أُولَئِكَ رَفِيقًا﴾ — He means the prophets, because He said: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ والرَّسُولَ فَأُولَئِكَ﴾, i.e. the obedient, ﴿مَعَ الَّذِينَ أنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ والصِّدِّيقِينَ والشُّهَداءِ والصّالِحِينَ وحَسُنَ أُولَئِكَ رَفِيقًا﴾, i.e. the prophets and those with them are excellent as companions. "رَفِيقًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), standing in for "رُفَقاءَ" (companions). Someone said: the singular does not stand in for the plural unless it is one of the nouns of agents (asmāʾ al-fāʿilīn); so "حَسُنَ القَوْمُ رَجُلًا" (excellent are the people as a man) would not be permissible in his view. But there is no difference between "رَفِيقٌ" and "رَجُلٌ" in this sense, because the singular in tamyīz stands in for the plural; likewise in places that can only be plural, such as your saying "هو أحْسَنُ فَتًى وأجْمَلُهُ" (he is the best youth and the handsomest), the meaning being: he is the best of the youths and the handsomest of them. And where the mention of the singular causes no confusion, it conveys the plural, as in the poet's saying:
بِها جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فَأمّا عِظامُها ∗∗∗ فَبِيضٌ وأمّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيبُ
(In it are the carcasses of exhausted camels: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skin, it is hard.)
And another said:
فِي حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقَدْ شَجِينا
(In your throat is a bone, while we have choked.)
He means: in your throats are bones. If you said "حَسُنَ القَوْمُ مُجاهِدًا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ" (excellent are the people as one striving in the way of Allah) and "حَسُنَ القَوْمُ رَجُلًا", it would be the same.
His saying: ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 70] — its meaning is: Allah suffices as knower, and the bāʾ is emphatic; the meaning is: be content with Allah as knower.

zajjaj:166-166.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِما أنْـزَلَ إلَيْكَ﴾: the reading is with the nominative (rafʿ), with ”لَكِنْ“ unstressed (lightened); the accusative is permissible: ”لَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَشْهَدُ“, except that one does not recite with whatever is permissible in Arabic unless a transmission of it is established from the Companions and the readers of the garrison cities. The meaning of ”لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِما أنْزَلَ إلَيْكَ“ is: He makes clear, because the witness is the one who makes clear what he bears witness to; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — makes it clear, and knows, along with making it clear, that it is the truth. ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ وكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾: its meaning is "and Allah suffices as a witness"; the bāʾ has entered for emphasis (muʾakkida). The meaning is: be content with Allah in His testimony. The meaning of ﴿أنْـزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ is: He sent down the Qurʾān in which is His knowledge.

zajjaj:170-170.t:
His saying: ﴿فَآمِنُوا خَيْرًا لَكُمْ﴾: the people of Arabic differed in explaining the accusative of ”خَيْرًا“. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is in the accusative because it goes outside the (main) utterance. He said: the Arabs say this in a complete utterance, such as your saying: ”لَتَقُومَنَّ خَيْرًا لَكَ“; but when the utterance is incomplete they put it in the nominative, saying: ”إنْ تَنْتَهِ خَيْرٌ لَكَ“. Al-Farrāʾ said: this, and His saying ”خَيْرًا لَكم“, is in the accusative because it is connected to the command and is part of its description; do you not see that you say: ”اِنْتَهِ هو خَيْرٌ لَكَ“? When ”هو“ dropped, it became connected to what precedes it, which is definite, and so it became accusative. Neither he nor al-Kisāʾī said which of the accusatives it is, nor did they explain it any further than this. Al-Khalīl and all the Basrans said: this is construed according to the meaning (maḥmūl ʿalā maʿnā), because when you say: ”اِنْتَهِ خَيْرًا“, you are pushing him away from one matter and putting him into another, as if you said: "Desist, and come to what is better for you, and enter into what is better for you." Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh cited the verse of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فَواعِدِيهِ سَرْحَتَيْ مالِكٍ ∗∗∗ أوِ الرُّبى بَيْنَهُما أسْهَلا
(So make a tryst with him at the two trees of Mālik, or the hillocks between them — [a place] more level.)
It is as if he said: ”إيتِي مَكانًا أسْهَلا“ ("come to a more level place").

zajjaj:171-171.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿سُبْحانَهُ أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ ولَدٌ﴾: the meaning of ”سُبْحانَهُ“ is: declaring Him free of having a child. This is the view of the people of Arabic, and it has come from the Prophet ﷺ that the meaning of ”سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ“ is: declaring Allah free of every evil; the explanation of the people of Arabic agrees with what has come from the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَلا تَقُولُوا ثَلاثَةٌ انْتَهُوا﴾: the nominative and nothing else; it is in the nominative by implying (iḍmār) "do not say: our gods are three (آلِهَتُنا ثَلاثَةٌ)". ﴿إنَّما اللَّهُ إلَهٌ واحِدٌ﴾, i.e. He is nothing but one God.
His saying: ﴿إنَّما المَسِيحُ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وكَلِمَتُهُ﴾, i.e.: so how could he be a god when he is the son of Maryam? And how could he be a god when his mother was before him? And Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — is the Eternal, who has never ceased to be. ﴿لا تَغْلُوا في دِينِكم ولا تَقُولُوا عَلى اللَّهِ إلا الحَقَّ﴾: ”اَلْغُلُوُّ“ (excess) is exceeding the measure in wrongdoing.

zajjaj:172-172.t:
His saying: ﴿لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ المَسِيحُ أنْ يَكُونَ عَبْدًا لِلَّهِ﴾, i.e.: the one whom you claim to be a god does not disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor do the angels brought near.
And the angels — and Allah knows best — are nobler than the prophets; do you not see that Nūḥ — peace be upon him — said: ﴿وَلا أقُولُ لَكم عِنْدِي خَزائِنُ اللَّهِ ولا أعْلَمُ الغَيْبَ ولا أقُولُ إنِّي مَلَكٌ﴾ [Hūd: 31]? So He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ المَسِيحُ﴾ from servitude to Allah. The meaning of ”يَسْتَنْكِفُ“ is: he will not scorn. Its origin in the language is from ”نَكَفْتَ الدَّمْعَ“ ("you wiped away the tear"), when you remove it from your cheek with your finger. The poet said:
فَبانُوا فَلَوْلا ما تَذَكَّرُ مِنهُمُ ∗∗∗ مِنَ الخُلْفِ لَمْ يُنْكَفْ لِعَيْنَيْكَ مَدْمَعُ
(They departed; and were it not for the broken promises you recall of them, no tear-flow of your eyes would have [needed to be] wiped away.)
So the interpretation of ”لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ“ is: he will not shrink back, and will not refuse the servitude of Allah.

zajjaj:174-174.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكم نُورًا مُبِينًا﴾: by it is meant — and Allah knows best — the Qurʾān, because light is what makes things clear so that they are seen. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has likened what is known by the heart with clear knowledge to what is seen by the eye with an unveiled, evident seeing. As for ”اَلْكَلالَةُ“, we have explained it at the beginning of the sūra.

zajjaj:176-176.t:
His saying: ﴿إنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ لَيْسَ لَهُ ولَدٌ﴾: placing the noun before the verb is permissible with ”إنْ“ because ”إنْ“ does not govern (lā taʿmal) the past verb, and because it is the mother (principal particle) of conditionals (umm al-jazāʾ). The grammarians hold that with it there is an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one explains; the meaning is: ”إنْ هَلَكَ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ“.
His saying: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكم أنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾: two views have been stated about it. Some said: the meaning is "Allah makes clear to you so that you do not go astray (ألّا تَضِلُّوا)", so ”لا“ is implied. The Basrans said: ”لا“ is not implied; rather the meaning is: ”يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكم كَراهَةَ أنْ تَضِلُّوا“ ("Allah makes clear to you out of aversion that you should go astray"), but ”كَراهَةَ“ was omitted because there is evidence for it in the utterance. Omission is permissible in their view along the lines of His saying: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], the meaning being "and ask the people of the town"; omitting the first (term of the construct) is permissible, and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) remains, pointing to what was omitted. They said: as for omitting ”لا“, which is a particle that came for the meaning of negation, that is not permissible; but ”لا“ does enter the utterance for emphasis, being void (laghw), as in His saying: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ ألا يَقْدِرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29], and like it is the poet's saying:
وَما ألُومُ البِيضَ ألّا تَسْخَرا ∗∗∗ لِما رَأيْنَ الشَّمِطَ القَفَنْدَرا
(I do not blame the fair women for mocking when they saw the grey-haired, ugly old man.)
The meaning is: "I do not blame the fair women for mocking (أنْ تَسْخَرَ)". Like the entry of ”لا“ for emphasis is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 1] and ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذا البَلَدِ﴾ [al-Balad: 1].
If someone says: is it then permissible to say: ”لا أحْلِفُ عَلَيْكَ“, meaning ”أحْلِفُ عَلَيْكَ“ ("I swear to you")? It is said: "No", because ”لا“ is treated as void only when the beginning of the utterance has proceeded on something other than negation; if you build the utterance on negation, you have overturned the affirmation. It was permissible for ”لا“ to be void at the beginning of the sūra only because the whole Qurʾān is like a single sūra; do you not see that the answer to something may occur with sūras between them? As He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said in answer to their saying: ﴿وَقالُوا يا أيُّها الَّذِي نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6] — He said: ﴿ن والقَلَمِ وما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 1] ﴿ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Qalam: 2]. And there is much like it in the Qurʾān.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ في أوْلادِكُمْ﴾. The meaning of ”يُوصِيكم“ is: He makes obligatory upon you, because a charge (waṣiyya) from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — is an obligation. The proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إلا بِالحَقِّ ذَلِكم وصّاكم بِهِ﴾ [al-Anʿam: 151], and this is among what is decisively binding upon us.

﴿لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾: the meaning is: there is established for the male the like of the portion of two females — two-thirds for him and one-third for the daughter. ﴿فَإنْ كُنَّ نِساءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثا ما تَرَكَ وإنْ كانَتْ واحِدَةً فَلَها النِّصْفُ﴾: both ”واحِدَةً“ and ”واحِدَةٌ“ are permissible here, and it has been read both ways, but the accusative is in my view much better, because His saying ﴿فَإنْ كُنَّ نِساءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ﴾ has made clear that the meaning is "if the children are women", and likewise "if the [female] child is one"; for that reason we chose the accusative, and most of the reading is on it.

If someone says: "We have been told only of [the case of] more than two, and one [daughter] has been mentioned; so why were two daughters given two-thirds, two being treated the same as a group?" — people have said more than one thing about this. Some of them said: the two daughters were given two-thirds by an indication [from elsewhere], no named share being prescribed for them [here]. The indication is His saying: ﴿يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكم في الكَلالَةِ إنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ لَيْسَ لَهُ ولَدٌ ولَهُ أُخْتٌ فَلَها نِصْفُ ما تَرَكَ﴾ [al-Nisa: 176]: so the sister has a half, just as the daughter has a half, and "if they are two, they have two-thirds"; so the two daughters were given two-thirds just as the two sisters were given, and the whole group of sisters was given two-thirds by analogy (qiyās) with what Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — mentioned concerning the whole group of daughters. And Allah made known in another place that the portion of two and of more than two is a single portion, in His saying: ﴿وَإنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً أوِ امْرَأةٌ ولَهُ أخٌ أوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما السُّدُسُ فَإنْ كانُوا أكْثَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ فَهم شُرَكاءُ في الثُّلُثِ﴾ [al-Nisa: 12]. This verse shows that when the inheritance is a named share, the portion of a group is a single portion. This is also its analogy in Arabic, because the status of two relative to three is like the status of three relative to four: two is a plurality just as three is a plurality; the prayer of two men and the prayer of two women is a congregation; and two [siblings] exclude [others, ḥajb] just as a group excludes. So this is clear and evident. Allah has made this in His Book so that one part of it indicates another, in order to give the Muslims understanding and teaching, so that they may know, in the matters that befall them, [how to proceed] on [the basis of] these indications.

Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said — and thus Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq said that he said —: in the verse itself there is an indication that two daughters have two-thirds, because when He said ﴿لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾, and the first [possible] number is a male and a female, then the male has two-thirds and the female one-third; so it is evident from this that two daughters have two-thirds, and Allah has made known that more than two have two-thirds [as well].

All these views that we have mentioned are good, fine and clear. As for what is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, that two daughters are in the position of one daughter, I do not reckon this to be authentically from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is impossible by analogy, because the status of two is the status of a plural, and one is outside [the category of] two. One says ”ثُلُثٌ“, ”رُبُعٌ“ and ”سُدُسٌ“ ("third, quarter, sixth"), and these may be lightened because of the heaviness of the ḍamma, so one says ”ثِلْثٌ“ [Translator's note: so in the source, with a kasra; the expected lightened form is «ثُلْثٌ»], ”رُبْعٌ“ and ”سُدْسٌ“. Whoever claims that the origin in them is the lightened form and that it was made heavy is mistaken, because speech is built on brevity and lightness.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلأبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما السُّدُسُ مِمّا تَرَكَ إنْ كانَ لَهُ ولَدٌ فَإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ ولَدٌ ووَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ فَلأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ فَإنْ كانَ لَهُ إخْوَةٌ فَلأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ﴾. The mother has a named share in inheritance from two directions: the naming of a sixth with a child, and the naming of a sixth with brothers, and the naming of a third if he has no child. The father inherits a sixth by way of the named share, and after the named shares he inherits by way of agnatic residue (taʿṣīb). The brothers exclude the mother from the third, so with them she inherits a sixth.

Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: We will mention a case for each thing of this, since the foundation of the shares in property and inheritances is in this sura. If a man or a woman dies leaving two parents, the mother has a third and the remaining two-thirds go to the father; with this the revelation came, and on it the Community is agreed. If the deceased leaves a child, and it is a male, the mother has a sixth, the father a sixth, and what remains goes to the son. If he leaves a daughter and two parents, the daughter has a half, the mother a sixth and the remainder goes to the father: the father takes a sixth by right of the named share and takes the other sixth by right of agnatic residue. If the deceased — being a woman — leaves a husband and two parents, the husband has a half, the mother a third of what remains, and the father two-thirds of what remains, which is a third of the original estate. It has been reported of Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to give the mother a third of the whole estate and give the father a sixth, thus preferring the mother over the father in this situation; but the consensus is contrary to what is narrated from him.

Those who argued along with the consensus said: Had Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known to us that the estate is between the father and the mother without naming [a share] for each, it would have been necessary for us to divide it between them in two halves. When Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known to us that the mother has a third, we knew that the father has two-thirds. Then when someone entered upon the father and mother and took half the estate, the reduction entered upon both of them together, so it followed that the inheritance of the two parents is only the half; thus the mother has a third of the half and the father two-thirds of the half. Another argument has been stated on this: some of them said: it was only said ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ ولَدٌ ووَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ فَلأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ﴾ [where the parents alone inherit], whereas here his parents alone did not inherit him; rather his parents inherited him, and someone other than the parents inherited along with them; so the mother's inheritance reverted to a third of what remains.

The proponents of this argument said: How can the mother be preferred over the father, when the brothers deprive the mother of the third, so that she is restricted to a sixth and the remainder is reserved for the father, the father taking five-sixths and the mother taking a sixth? If a man or woman dies and leaves three or more brothers, a mother and a father, the mother takes a sixth and the father takes the remainder; this is [a matter of] consensus. Something anomalous (shādhdh) has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās on this: they narrated that he used to give the brothers this sixth which the brothers prevented the mother from taking; so he would give the mother a sixth, the brothers a sixth, and give the father two-thirds. This is held by none of the jurists; the jurists of the [major] cities are agreed that brothers do not take [anything] together with the two parents.

If a man dies and leaves two brothers and two parents, the jurists are agreed that the two brothers exclude the mother from the third — except Ibn ʿAbbās, for he did not exclude [her] by two brothers. His argument was that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فَإنْ كانَ لَهُ إخْوَةٌ فَلأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ﴾ ("brothers", plural). [But] all the people of the language have said that two brothers are a plurality just as brothers are a plurality, because when you join one to one, they are a plurality, and they may be called ”إخْوَةٌ“. Sībawayh reported that the Arabs say ”قَدْ وضَعا رِحالَهُما“ ("the two of them put down their saddles", plural), meaning ”رَحْلَيْهِما“ (their two saddles). And whatever has only one of a thing [per owner], its dual is a plural, because the origin is the plural; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4] ("your hearts", plural, for two).

He said ﴿وَلأبَوَيْهِ﴾ ("to his two fathers", i.e. parents) because each of them begot him. The origin for ”أُمٌّ“ (mother) would be to say ”أبَةٌ“, but ”أُمٌّ“ made it unnecessary; and ”أبَوانِ“ is the dual of ”أبٌ“ and ”أبَةٌ“. Likewise, if you made a dual of ”اِبْنًا“ and ”اِبْنَةً“ ("son" and "daughter") — and did not fear ambiguity — you would say ”اِبْنانِ“.

”فَلِأُمِّهِ“ is read with a ḍamma on the hamza, which is the majority of readings, and it is read with a kasra: ”فَلِإمِّهِ“. But when what precedes the hamza is other than a kasra, it is the ḍamma and nothing else, as in His saying ﴿وَجَعَلْنا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وأُمَّهُ آيَةً﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 50] — ”وَإمَّهُ“ is not permissible — and likewise His saying ﴿ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ [al-Mujadila: 2]. ”لِإمِّهِ“ and ”في إمِّها رَسُولًا“ with the kasra are permissible only because a kasra precedes the hamza, and they felt the ḍamma after a kasra to be heavy; there is nothing in the speech of the Arabs on the pattern fiʿul, with a kasra on the first radical and a ḍamma on the second. So when the lām became mixed with the noun, it was treated like a single word, and a kasra was substituted for the ḍamma. Whoever says ”فَلِأُمِّهِ“ with a ḍamma on the hamza brings it in its original form, on the basis that the lām is reckoned as separate.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِها أوْ دَيْنٍ﴾, that is: these shares only become due after the debt has been paid and the bequest of the deceased carried out within his third.

If someone says: "Why did He say 'or a debt' (”أوْ دَيْنٍ“)? Why was it not 'after a bequest he makes and a debt'?" — the answer to this is that ”أوْ“ comes for permission (ibāḥa): it applies to each one individually and also includes the whole group. One says: ”جالِسِ الحَسَنَ، أوِ الشَّعْبِيَّ“ ("Sit with al-Ḥasan or al-Shaʿbī"), and the meaning is: each one of these is worthy of being sat with; if you sit with al-Ḥasan you are correct [and with both, too]. But if you said "Sit with the two men" and you sat with one of them and left the other, you would not be following what you were commanded. So had it been "after a bequest he makes and a debt", the wording would allow that this applies when the bequest and the debt come together, and that when they occur singly there is another ruling. When it is ”أوْ“, it indicates that if one of them exists, the inheritance comes after it, and likewise if both exist.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿آباؤُكم وأبْناؤُكم لا تَدْرُونَ أيُّهم أقْرَبُ لَكم نَفْعًا﴾. There is more than one view about this. As for the exegesis, it is narrated that if the son is of a higher rank in Paradise than his father, he asks that his father be raised to him, and he is raised; likewise the father, if he is of a higher rank than his son, asks that his son be raised to him. So you do not know in this world which of them is nearer to you in benefit; that is, Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has prescribed the shares according to what is, in His sight, wisdom; had He entrusted that to you, you would not have known which of them is more beneficial to you in this world, and you would have placed wealth without wisdom.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾, that is: All-Knowing of what is good for His creation, All-Wise in what He has prescribed concerning this wealth and other things.

His saying: ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ is accusative for emphasis (tawkīd), and as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ”وَلِأبَوَيْهِ“, that is: these heirs have what we have mentioned, as something obligatory; so ”فَرِيضَةً“ emphasises His saying ”يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ“. As for the meaning of ”إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا“ ("Allah was All-Knowing, All-Wise"), there are three views about it. Sībawayh said: the people had witnessed knowledge, wisdom, forgiveness and bounty, so they were told: Allah was like that and has never ceased to be, that is, He has never ceased to be as you have witnessed. Al-Ḥasan said: He was All-Knowing of things before creating them, All-Wise in what He decrees of their arrangement. Some of them said: a report about Allah in these matters in the past tense is like a report in the future and the present, because things are with Allah in a single state — what has passed, what will be and what is. The first two views are the correct ones, because the Arabs were addressed in what they understand, and the Quran was revealed in their language; so whatever exegesis most resembles their speech is the more correct, since the Quran was revealed in their language.

Some of them [also] said [about ﴿لا تَدْرُونَ أيُّهم أقْرَبُ لَكم نَفْعًا﴾]: maintenance for the son is obligatory upon the father if he is in need of it, and likewise the father's maintenance is obligatory upon the son if he is in need of it; so in benefit in this respect it is not known which of them is nearer in benefit. The first view is the one held by the exegetes.

zajjaj:115-115.t:
﴿وَمَن يُشاقِقِ الرَّسُولَ مِن بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ الهُدى ويَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ المُؤْمِنِينَ نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلّى ونُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: because what Allah revealed to His Prophet about this Ṭuʿma's affair had become clear to him, and [Allah] had exposed in the verse enough about his theft to suffice, yet he showed enmity to the Prophet ﷺ, went to Mecca and settled with the idolaters.
The meaning of «نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلّى» is: We leave him to what he chose for himself in this world, because Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — has promised punishment in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:116-116.t:
And He — exalted is He — made known that He does not forgive shirk (associating partners with Allah). Before this verse He mentioned: ﴿وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 110], and after it He made known that it is not possible that He forgive shirk as long as the associator persists in it.
If someone says: He only said ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾, so if a man is called a "disbeliever" but has not associated anything else with Allah, he falls outside His saying ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 48] — the answer to this is that every disbeliever associates [others] with Allah, because when the disbeliever disbelieves in a prophet he claims that the signs he brought are not from Allah, and so he ascribes what can only belong to Allah to other than Allah, and thereby becomes an associator. So every disbeliever is an associator, and the meaning is that Allah does not forgive the disbelief of whoever disbelieves in Him and in one of His prophets, because his disbelief in His prophet is disbelief in Him. ﴿وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالا بَعِيدًا﴾, because making something else [a partner] with Allah is among the farthest of error and blindness. Most of what is said here is on account of those who worshipped idols; the proof of that is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He — right after this: ﴿إنْ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إلا إناثًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 117].
As for «نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلّى ونُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ», there are several options in it. It is permissible to say «نُوَلِّهِي» with the yāʾ retained, and permissible «نُوَلِّهُو» with the wāw retained, and permissible «نُوَلِّهِ» with kasra on the hāʾ. As for «نُوَلِّهْ» with the hāʾ quiescent, and «نُصْلِهْ جَهَنَّمَ», making the hāʾ quiescent is not permissible, because the hāʾ's due is to have a yāʾ with it. As for dropping the yāʾ, it is weak in it; and it is not permissible to drop the yāʾ without the kasra that indicates it remaining.
His saying: ﴿إنْ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إلا إناثًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 117]: «إنْ يَدْعُونَ» — it is read «إلّا أُنُثًا» and «إلّا أُثُنًا», with the thāʾ placed before [the nūn] and after it. Whoever said ﴿إناثًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 117], it is the plural of «أُنْثى», [giving] «إناثٌ». Whoever said «أُنُثٌ», it is the plural of «إناثٌ», because «إناثًا» is on the pattern of «مِثالٌ», and «إناثٌ» / «أُنُثٌ» are like «مِثالٌ» / «مُثُلٌ». Whoever said «أُثُنًا», it is the plural of «وَثَنٌ» (idol); the original is «وُثُنٌ», except that when a wāw takes ḍamma it may be replaced by a hamza, as in His saying — exalted is He —: ﴿وَإذا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 11], where the original is «وُقِّتَتْ». The pattern of «وُثُنٌ» in the plural is like «سُقُفٌ». It may also be «أُثْنٌ», like «أسَدٌ» / «أُسْدٌ»; and it may be that «أُثُنٌ» was originally «أُثْنٌ», and the ḍamma made the [following vowel] follow the ḍamma.

zajjaj:117-117.t: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَإنْ يَدْعُونَ إلا شَيْطانًا مَرِيدًا﴾: He means by it Iblīs, because when they obey him in what he made appealing to them they have worshipped him. «يَدْعُونَ» is in the sense of «يَعْبُدُونَ» (they worship), because when they call upon Allah sincerely they have worshipped Him. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَقالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾ [Ghāfir: 60], that is: worship Me; the proof of that is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِي﴾ [Ghāfir: 60]. The meaning of «مَرِيدٌ» is: departing from obedience, slipping free of it. One says «شَجَرَةٌ مَرْداءُ» when its leaves have fallen; and from that one in whom no beard has grown is called «أمْرَدَ», that is: smooth in the place of the beard. And «قَدْ مَرَدَ الرَّجُلُ، يَمْرُدُ، مُرُودًا» when he is insolent and departs from obedience.

zajjaj:118-118.t:
﴿وَقالَ لأتَّخِذَنَّ مِن عِبادِكَ نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا﴾: it was said about ﴿مَفْرُوضًا﴾ that its meaning is "fixed in time", and in some tafsīr it has come: out of every thousand, one is for Allah and the rest are for Iblīs.
The meaning of ﴿مَفْرُوضًا﴾ — and Allah knows best — is: I make it binding upon myself. The root of «اَلْفَرْضُ» in the language is cutting. «اَلْفُرْضَةُ» is the breach that occurs in a river; one says «سَقاها بِالفِراضِ، وبِالفُرَضِ» ("he watered them at the breaches"). «اَلْفَرْضُ» is the notch in a tooth-stick in which the thread is tied, and the farḍ in a bow is the notch in which the string is tied. Al-farīḍa in everything that is made obligatory is what Allah commanded the servants, making it a binding, decisive matter upon them. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ ما فَرَضْتُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 237], that is: you have assigned them a portion of wealth. And «قَدْ فَرَضْتُ الرَّجُلَ»: I assigned him a portion of the fayʾ (spoils gained without fighting). As for the poet's saying:
؎إذا أكَلْتُ سَمَكًا وفَرْضًا ∗∗∗ ذَهَبْتُ طُولًا وذَهَبْتُ عَرْضًا
(When I eat fish and farḍ, I grow in length and I grow in breadth.)
— farḍ here is dates. Dates were called «فَرْضًا» only because they are taken in the obligatory portions (firāḍ) of the alms.

zajjaj:119-119.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾, that is: I will combine for them, along with leading astray, making them imagine that they will obtain a share of the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 38].
﴿وَلآمُرَنَّهم فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ آذانَ الأنْعامِ﴾: as though — and Allah knows best — [it were]: I will command them to slit the ears of cattle, and they will slit them, that is: they will split them. One says «بَتَكْتُ الشَّيْءَ، أبْتِكُهُ، بَتْكًا» when I have cut it; and «بِتْكَةٌ» / «بِتَكٌ» are like «قِطْعَةٌ» / «قِطَعٌ». This concerns the baḥīra: in the Jāhiliyya, when a she-camel bore five litters and the fifth was a male, they split the she-camel's ear and refrained from making use of her; she was not driven away from water or pasture, and if an exhausted man met her he would not ride her. This is the interpretation of «فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ آذانَ الأنْعامِ»: Iblīs made it seem to them that leaving her unused was an act of drawing near to Allah.
﴿وَلآمُرَنَّهم فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ﴾: it was said that its meaning is that Allah created cattle for them to ride and eat, yet they forbade them to themselves; and He created the sun, the moon, the earth and stones as subjected to people for them to benefit from, yet the idolaters worshipped them, and so they altered Allah's creation — that is, Allah's religion — because Allah fashioned creation upon Islam: He created them from the loins of Adam like tiny particles and made them bear witness that He is their Lord, and they believed; so whoever disbelieves has altered the fiṭra (natural disposition) of Allah upon which He fashioned people. As for His saying ﴿لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Rūm: 30], its meaning is: what Allah created is the sound [way]; no one is able to alter the meaning of the soundness of the religion. Some said: ﴿فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ﴾ is castration, because whoever castrates a stallion has altered Allah's creation.
The meaning of ﴿إنْ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إلا إناثًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 117] is: they worship only what they have named with the names of females — meaning the idolaters, who named the idols «اَللّاتَ», «اَلْعُزّى», «مَناةَ» and the like. And it was said that the meaning of His saying «إنْ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إلّا إناثًا» is: lifeless things; all lifeless things are spoken of as the feminine is spoken of. You say of that: «هَذِهِ الأحْجارُ تُعْجِبُنِي» ("these stones please me" [with a feminine verb]), and you do not say «يُعْجِبُونَنِي»; likewise «اَلدَّراهِمُ تَنْفَعُنِي» ("the dirhams benefit me").

zajjaj:121-121.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا يَجِدُونَ عَنْها مَحِيصًا﴾, that is: they find no turning away from it and no refuge. One says «حِصْتُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ، أحِيصُ», and they transmitted «جِضْتُ عَنْهُ، أجِيضُ», with jīm and dotted ḍād, in the sense of «حِصْتُ». That is not permissible in the Quran, even though the meaning is the same and the script is not contradicted, because the Quran is a sunna in which the transmission from the Prophet ﷺ, his Companions, the Predecessors and the readers of the cities is not to be departed from in favour of what is permissible in grammar and the language; and what is in it is more eloquent than what is [merely] permissible, so following it is more fitting.
One says «حُصْتُ، أحُوصُ، حَوْصًا، وحِياصًا» when I have sewn. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says «حُصْ عَيْنَ صَقْرِكَ», that is: sew [shut] its eye. Al-ḥawaṣ in the eye is narrowness of its outer corner, and «اَلْخَوَصُ» with dotted khāʾ is its sunkenness.

zajjaj:123-123.t:
His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ بِأمانِيِّكم ولا أمانِيِّ أهْلِ الكِتابِ﴾: the noun (ism) of «لَيْسَ» is implied (muḍmar). The meaning is: Allah's reward is not according to your wishes nor the wishes of the People of the Book. Something has preceded which indicates the implied "reward", namely His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أبَدًا وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 122], that is: only whoever believes and does righteous deeds enters Paradise, not as the People of the Book wish, for they used to claim that they were the sons of Allah and His beloved, and they said: ﴿لَنْ تَمَسَّنا النّارُ إلا أيّامًا مَعْدُودَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 80]. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that entering Paradise and Allah's recompense for good and evil deeds is not by wishes but by deeds. Then He mentioned some of that, saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾, that is: his wishing will not benefit him, ﴿وَلا يَجِدْ لَهُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ولِيًّا ولا نَصِيرًا﴾ ﴿وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصّالِحاتِ مِن ذَكَرٍ أوْ أُنْثى وهو مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 124]. So Allah made known that the doer of evil is not benefited by his wishing, no protector takes him under protection and no helper helps him.
A group of the people of al-waʿīd (those who hold that the threat of punishment is necessarily carried out) argued from His saying ﴿وَلا يَجِدْ لَهُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ولِيًّا ولا نَصِيرًا﴾, claiming that this shows that whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. But Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has made known that He forgives what is short of shirk for whom He wills; so for the doer of evil, as long as he is not a disbeliever, pardon and mercy are to be hoped, and the Prophet ﷺ is an intercessor for his community, whose intercession for them is accepted.
The meaning of ﴿وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيرًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 124]: «اَلنَّقِيرُ» is the dot on the back of the date-stone, which is where the palm sprouts from; the meaning is: they will not be wronged by that amount.

zajjaj:125-125.t:
His saying: ﴿واتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلا﴾: «اَلْخَلِيلُ» is the lover in whose love there is no flaw (khalal). So it is possible that Ibrāhīm was called the khalīl of Allah because he is the one whom Allah loved and chose with a complete, perfect love. It was also said: al-khalīl is the poor one, so it is possible [that he was called so as] Allah's poor one, that is: the one who directed his poverty and need to none but Allah, sincerely so. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ أنْتُمُ الفُقَراءُ إلى اللَّهِ﴾ [Fāṭir: 15]. A parallel to Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl being the one poor towards Allah is the saying of Zuhayr praising Harim ibn Sinān:
وَإنْ أتاهُ خَلِيلٌ يَوْمَ مَسْغَبَةٍ ... يَقُولُ لا غائِبٌ مالِي ولا حَرَمُ
(And if a needy man comes to him on a day of famine, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)
It has come in the tafsīr that Ibrāhīm used to host guests and feed the poor. A drought struck the people, so he sent to a friend (khalīl) of his who was in Egypt to obtain provisions from him. That friend said to himself: "If Ibrāhīm wanted the provisions only for himself, I would send them to him, but he wants them for the people." So Ibrāhīm's servants returned without provisions. They passed by a soft sandy valley, took some of the sand that was in it and put it in their containers, out of shame before the people at returning with nothing. When he — peace be upon him — saw them, he asked them for the news and they told him, and sleep overcame him and he slept, troubled. His wife awoke and saw the containers full, so she ordered that some be taken out and baked; and food of the utmost excellence was taken out of them and baked. Ibrāhīm awoke and smelt the smell of the food, and said: "Where is this from?" His wife said: "From your Egyptian friend." Ibrāhīm said: "This is from my Friend, Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He."
This is what is related in the tafsīr, and it is among the signs of the prophets — peace be upon them — and not to be denied; and the derivation we have explained does not contradict it.
«اَلْخُلَّةُ» is friendship, and «اَلْخُلَّةُ» is need. As for the meaning of need, it is the deficiency (ikhtilāl) that afflicts a person in what he needs. As for «اَلْخُلَّةُ» meaning friendship, its meaning is that each lover fills his companion's gap (khalal) in affection and in need of him. «اَلْخَلَلُ» is every gap that occurs in a thing, and «اَلْخِلالُ» is the toothpick; it was called «خِلالًا» only because the gaps between the teeth are followed with it. As for the poet's saying:
؎وَنَظَرْنَ مِن خَلَلِ السُّتُورِ بِأعْيُنٍ ∗∗∗ مَرْضى مُخالِطُها السِّقامُ صِحاحُ
(They looked out through the gaps in the curtains with languid eyes, mixed with sickness yet sound.)
— its meaning is: they looked from the openings that occur in the curtains. As for someone's saying «لَكَ خَلَّةٌ مِن خِلالٍ» ("you have one of [several] options"), its interpretation is that I leave open for you, from my opinion or from what I have, one option out of several. The interpretation of «أُخَلِّي» is really «أُخَلِّلُ»; and «أُخَلِّي» may be from «اَلْخَلْوَةُ» (being empty), and «اَلْخَلْوَةُ» and «اَلْخَلَلُ» go back to one meaning. «اَلْخِلُّ» is a path in sand; its meaning is that an opening has parted in it and become a path. And «اَلْخَلُّ» (vinegar), which is eaten, was called «خَلًّا» only because the taste of sweetness has become deficient (ikhtalla) in it.

zajjaj:126-126.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾, that is: Ibrāhīm, whom Allah took as a khalīl (intimate friend), is Allah's servant and belongs to Him, as does everything in the heavens and the earth.

zajjaj:127-127.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ في النِّساءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكم فِيهِنَّ وما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: the position of «ما» is nominative; the meaning is: «اَللَّهُ يُفْتِيكم فِيهِنَّ، وما يُتْلى عَلَيْكم في الكِتابِ أيْضًا يُفْتِيكم فِيهِنَّ» ("Allah gives you a ruling about them, and what is recited to you in the Book also gives you a ruling about them"). It is possible that «ما» is in the position of the genitive, but that is very far-fetched, because an overt noun is not conjoined to an implied [attached] pronoun; for that reason the nominative was chosen, and also because the meaning of the nominative is clearer, since what is recited in the Book is what made clear what they asked about. So the meaning is: «قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكم فِيهِنَّ، وكِتابُهُ يُفْتِيكم فِيهِنَّ» ("Say: Allah gives you a ruling about them, and His Book gives you a ruling about them").
His saying: ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾: the meaning is «وَتَرْغَبُونَ عَنْ أنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ» ("and you are averse to marrying them").
His saying: ﴿والمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الوِلْدانِ﴾: He means the orphans. The position of «اَلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ» is genitive, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to His saying ﴿وَما يُتْلى عَلَيْكم في الكِتابِ في يَتامى النِّساءِ﴾; the meaning is: and concerning the weak among the children. What gives them a ruling from the Quran is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَآتُوا اليَتامى أمْوالَهم ولا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ ولا تَأْكُلُوا أمْوالَهم إلى أمْوالِكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 2], and what was recited to them concerning marriage is His saying: ﴿فانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكم مِنَ النِّساءِ مَثْنى وثُلاثَ ورُباعَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 3]. So the meaning is: Say: Allah gives you a ruling about them, and these things that are in the Book give you a ruling about them.
His saying: ﴿وَأنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتامى بِالقِسْطِ﴾: «أنْ» is in the position of the genitive; the meaning is: and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women, and concerning your standing up for the orphans with justice.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً﴾. It is read ”يُورَثُ“ and ”يُورِثُ“, with a fatḥa and with a kasra on the rāʾ. Whoever reads ”يُورِثُ“ with the kasra, ”كَلالَةً“ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); whoever reads ”يُورَثُ“, ”كَلالَةً“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The people of the language claim that ”اَلْكَلالَةُ“ comes from your saying ”تَكَلَّلَهُ النَّسَبُ“ ("the lineage surrounded him"), that is, the one who inherits him was neither his son nor his father; the kalāla is [kin] other than the child and the parent. The proof that the father is not kalāla is the poet's saying:
؎فَإنَّ أبا المَرْءِ أحَمى لَهُ ∗∗∗ ومَوْلى الكَلالَةِ لا يَغْضَبُ
(For a man's father is the most protective of him, while the kinsman of the kalāla does not grow angry [on his behalf].)
It is like the crown (al-iklīl) which is upon the head [i.e. surrounding it]. It was inferred that the kalāla here means the brothers by the mother, not by the father, from what is mentioned at the end of the sura: that two sisters have two-thirds and that brothers have the whole estate. So it was known here — since one was assigned a sixth and two a third, and they are not given anything more than the third however many they are — that He means by them the brothers by the mother.

If a woman dies and leaves a husband, a mother and brothers by the mother, the husband has a half, the mother a sixth and the brothers by the mother a third. If she leaves a husband, a mother, full brothers (by father and mother) and brothers by the mother, this case is called by some "the shared case" (al-mas'ala al-mushtaraka) and by some "the donkey case" (al-ḥimāriyya). Some of them said: the third that remains belongs to the brothers by the mother, not to the brothers by father and mother, because those by the mother have a named share, which is the third, while the brothers by father and mother have no named share; so we gave them [the uterine brothers] the third — just as, if a man died and left two brothers by the mother and a hundred brothers by father and mother, the two uterine brothers would be given a third and the hundred would be given two-thirds; so the brothers by the mother come to exceed the full brothers by father and mother in their shares. Others said: the mother is one [and the same, so they share].

They called it "the donkey case" because they [the full brothers] said: "Suppose our father was a donkey" — and they shared [the third] among them; hence it was called "the shared case".

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿غَيْرَ مُضارٍّ وصِيَّةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾. ”غَيْرَ“ is accusative as a ḥāl; the meaning is: he makes the bequest without causing harm. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — forbade causing harm in bequests. It is narrated from Abū Hurayra: «”Whoever causes harm in a bequest, Allah will cast him into a valley of Hell“ — or: ”of fire“». So causing harm in bequests relates to the inheritance. ﴿واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾, that is: All-Knowing of what He has arranged of these shares, Forbearing towards whoever disobeys Him, in that He grants him respite and accepts his repentance. ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Nisa: 13], that is: the bounds which should not be overstepped.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ﴾, that is: "upholds His limits as He has defined them". ﴿يُدْخِلْهُ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾, that is: He will admit them with abiding forever in it decreed for them. A ḥāl (circumstantial) may refer to the future; you say: ”مَرَرْتُ بِهِ مَعَهُ بازٍ صائِدًا بِهِ غَدًا“ ("I passed by him with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow"), that is, intending (with it decreed) to hunt with it tomorrow.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَن يَعْصِ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ ويَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ﴾, that is: oversteps what Allah has defined and commanded. ﴿يُدْخِلْهُ نارًا خالِدًا فِيها﴾: ”خالِدًا“ is part of the naʿt (adjective) of ”نارًا“ [Translator's note: so in the source; grammatically it would have to be a description qualifying the fire while referring to the person], and it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: He will admit him with abiding forever in it decreed for him.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿واللاتِي يَأْتِينَ الفاحِشَةَ مِن نِسائِكُمْ﴾. "The indecency" (al-fāḥisha) is fornication. ”اَلَّتِي“ is pluralised as ”اَللّاتِي“ and ”اَللَّواتِي“. The poet said:
؎مِنَ اللَّواتِي والَّتِي واللّاتِي ∗∗∗ زَعَمْنَ أنِّي كَبِرَتْ لِداتِي
(Of those women — the ones who claimed that my peers have grown old.)
And ”اَللّاتِي“ is formed as a plural both with the yāʾ retained and with the yāʾ dropped. The poet said:
؎مِنَ اللّاءِ لَمْ يَحْجُجْنَ يَبْغِينَ حِسْبَةً ∗∗∗ ولَكِنْ لِيَقْتُلْنَ البَرِيءَ المُغَفَّلا
(Of those women who did not go on pilgrimage seeking reward, but rather to slay the innocent, unwary man.)
﴿فاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أرْبَعَةً مِنكُمْ﴾, that is: from the Muslims. ﴿فَإنْ شَهِدُوا فَأمْسِكُوهُنَّ في البُيُوتِ حَتّى يَتَوَفّاهُنَّ المَوْتُ أوْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلا﴾: this was the prescribed [punishment] for fornication before flogging was revealed and the Prophet ﷺ commanded stoning; the two fornicators used to be confined for life. Some of them said: ﴿أوْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلا﴾ is the ḥadd (prescribed punishment) which abrogated perpetual confinement and the [verbal] harm.

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿واللَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنكم فَآذُوهُما﴾. Some of them said: confinement was for two previously married persons, and harm for two unmarried persons: they would be rebuked, and it would be said to them: "You have fornicated, you have acted wickedly, and you have violated the sanctities of Allah." Some of them said: the harm for them was abrogated along with the confinement. Some of them said: the harm should not be abrogated from them unless they repent, and His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذابَهُما طائِفَةٌ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Nur: 2] is part of the rebuke to them, in that they are exposed before the assembled people. As for what came before concerning the matter of the two wrongdoers, it has been dispensed with, except that its benefit is that testimony in fornication has always been the testimony of four persons.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إنَّما التَّوْبَةُ عَلى اللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ بِجَهالَةٍ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبٍ﴾. Its meaning is not that they do evil while being ignorant, without discernment, for whoever has no reason and no discernment is not subject to any ḥadd (prescribed punishment). The meaning of ”بِجَهالَةٍ“ is only that they are ignorant in choosing the passing pleasure over the lasting pleasure; that ignorance does not remove the punishment from them — if it were so, no one would be punished — but it is ignorance in choice. The meaning of ”يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبٍ“ is: they stop [Translator's note: so in the source, «يَتَوَقَّفُونَ»; possibly a copying error for «يَتُوبُونَ», "they repent"] before death, because what lies between a person and death is near; so repentance is accepted before certainty of death.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا حَضَرَ أحَدَهُمُ المَوْتُ قالَ إنِّي تُبْتُ الآنَ﴾. Repentance is not [accepted] for him only because he repented at a time when it is not possible to desist [from sin] through acting in a way that would make the repentance real.

﴿أُولَئِكَ أعْتَدْنا لَهم عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾, that is: painful and aching. ”اَلْمُؤْلِمُ“ is that whose infliction of pain reaches the utmost extent.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ﴾ — Allah commanded that the believers not cast themselves with their own hands into destruction, that they be wary of their enemy, and that they strive for Allah with true striving, so that Allah may test the good; and along with that He guaranteed them victory. For had Allah the Exalted undertaken the killing of His enemies without any cause on the part of human beings, they would not have been rewarded; but He commanded that precaution be taken, and said: ﴿فانْفِرُوا ثُباتٍ أوِ انْفِرُوا جَمِيعًا﴾. "اَلثُّباتُ" are the scattered groups; its singular is "ثُبَةٌ". Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said:
وَقَدْ أغْدُو عَلى ثُبَةٍ كِرامٍ ∗∗∗ نَشاوى واجِدِينَ لِما نَشاءُ
(Many a morning I have gone out to a band of noble men, merry with drink, finding whatever we wish.)
Sībawayh said: "ثُبَةٌ" is pluralised "ثُبُونَ" and "ثُبِينَ" in the nominative, accusative and genitive. It was pluralised with wāw and nūn only — and likewise "عِزَةٌ" and "عِضَةٌ", as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا القُرْآنَ عِضِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 91] — because the wāw and nūn were made a compensation for the elision of the end of the word. "ثُبَةٌ" meaning a group has its last letter elided; its diminutive is "ثُبَيَّةٌ". "ثُبَةُ الحَوْضِ" is the middle of the cistern, where the water returns (yathūbu) to it; its diminutive is "ثُوَيْبَةٌ", because this one has the middle radical (ʿayn al-fiʿl) elided. The thuba of a group is derived only from "ثَبَّيْتُ عَلى الرَّجُلِ" when I praise a man in his lifetime; its interpretation is that you have gathered the mention of his merits. As for "اَلثُّبَةُ" — the group from a band — its interpretation (here) is: go forth in separate groups, or go forth some of you towards others.

zajjaj:72-72.t:
And He said: ﴿وَإنَّ مِنكم لَمَن لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ﴾, i.e. among those who displayed faith there is one who lags behind from fighting. One says "قَدْ أبْطَأ الرَّجُلُ" and "بَطُؤَ" with one meaning: "أبْطَأ" means he was late, and the meaning of "بَطُؤَ" is he was heavy (slow); (the maṣdars are) "إبْطاءً" and "بُطْئًا". The first lām, in "لَمَن", is the lām of "إنَّ", and the lām in "لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ" is the lām of the oath; and "مَن" is connected (as relative) with what brings in the oath. Were this (spelled out as) speech, you would say: "إنَّ مِنكم لَمَن أحْلِفُ واللَّهِ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ" (among you is one regarding whom I swear: by Allah, he will surely lag behind). The grammarians agree that "مَن", "ما" and "اَلَّذِي" are not given a ṣila (relative clause) consisting of a command or prohibition except with what is implied with it of mention of a statement, and that the lām of the oath, when it comes with these words, has the wording of the oath, or what resembles its wording, implied with it.
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ أصابَتْكم مُصِيبَةٌ قالَ﴾ — this one who lags behind — ﴿قَدْ أنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إذْ لَمْ أكُنْ مَعَهم شَهِيدًا﴾, i.e. I did not share with them in their calamity.

zajjaj:73-73.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أصابَكم فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. you are victorious and take spoils, ﴿لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ﴾ — "كَأنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ" may have occurred here as parenthetical (muʿtariḍ); the meaning is: "وَلَئِنْ أصابَكم فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِيَقُولَنَّ: يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهم فَأفُوزَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا" (and if bounty from Allah reaches you, he will surely say: would that I had been with them, so that I might attain a great triumph), and it would be: "إنْ أصابَتْكم مُصِيبَةٌ قالَ قَدْ أنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إذْ لَمْ أكُنْ مَعَهم شَهِيدًا كَأنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ" (if a calamity strikes you, he says: Allah has favoured me in that I was not present with them — as if there had been no affection between you and him). The meaning of "اَلْمَوَدَّةُ" here is: as if he had not made a covenant with you on faith, i.e. as if he had not displayed affection to you. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — (that it is): "لَيَقُولَنَّ: يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهم كَأنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ" (he will surely say: would that I had been with them — as if there had been no affection between you and him), i.e. as if he had not covenanted with you to strive alongside you. There is then no flaw in it in Arabic, nor does it diminish a meaning; and Allah knows best. ﴿فَأفُوزَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾: "فَأفُوزَ" is accusative as the answer to the wish (tamannī) with the fāʾ.

zajjaj:74-74.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلْيُقاتِلْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. if there is between you and him a covenant of security, then let him fight in the way of Allah with you. ﴿الَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا بِالآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e. they sell. One says "شَرَيْتُ" meaning "بِعْتُ" (I sold), and "شَرَيْتُ" meaning "اِشْتَرَيْتُ" (I bought). Yazīd ibn Mufarrigh said:
وَشَرَيْتُ بُرْدًا لَيْتَنِي ∗∗∗ مِن بَعْدِ بُرْدٍ كُنْتُ هامَهْ
(I sold Burd — would that, after Burd, I had been a dead man's owl.)
"بُرْدٌ" is his slave, and "شَرَيْتُهُ" means: I sold him.

zajjaj:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما لَكم لا تُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — "ما" is separate; the meaning is: what is the matter with you, abandoning fighting? "لا تُقاتِلُونَ" is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَما لَهم عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 49]. "اَلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ" is in the position of the genitive; the meaning is: "and what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and the way of the oppressed".
﴿مِنَ الرِّجالِ والنِّساءِ والوِلْدانِ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أخْرِجْنا مِن هَذِهِ القَرْيَةِ الظّالِمِ أهْلُها﴾ — by the town He means Mecca, i.e. what is the matter with you that you do not strive to rescue these?! His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْ لَنا مِن لَدُنْكَ ولِيًّا واجْعَلْ لَنا مِن لَدُنْكَ نَصِيرًا﴾, i.e. "take charge of us with Your help, and rescue us from the people of Mecca, (the town) whose people are oppressors". So (الظّالِمِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of "اَلْقَرْيَةِ", and "اَلظّالِمِ" is made singular because it is an adjective that occupies the place of the verb: you say "مَرَرْتُ بِالقَرْيَةِ الصّالِحِ أهْلُها" (I passed by the town whose people are righteous), like your saying "اَلَّتِي صَلُحَ أهْلُها" (whose people became righteous).
Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: "والمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ" is in the position of the genitive in two ways. The meaning (of the first) is: "what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and on behalf of the oppressed?!" He said: and it is possible that it is conjoined to the name of Allah, i.e. in the way of Allah and the way of the oppressed. He said: I choose that it be on the basis of "and on behalf of the oppressed", because of the difference between the two ways, since the meaning of "the way of the oppressed" is, as it were, the rescue of the oppressed. The view of most grammarians is as Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd chose; but the second interpretation is, in my view, closer to the meaning, because the way of the oppressed is the way of Allah.

zajjaj:76-76.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِ الطّاغُوتِ﴾ — "اَلطّاغُوتُ", according to all the grammarians, is treated as masculine and as feminine, and in the Quran there is evidence of both its masculine and its feminine treatment. As for its masculine, it is His saying: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أنْ يَتَحاكَمُوا إلى الطّاغُوتِ وقَدْ أُمِرُوا أنْ يَكْفُرُوا بِهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 60]; and as for its feminine, it is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿والَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطّاغُوتَ أنْ يَعْبُدُوها﴾ [al-Zumar: 17]. Abū ʿUbayda said: "اَلطّاغُوتُ" here has the meaning of "a group", as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ المَيْتَةُ والدَّمُ ولَحْمُ الخِنْـزِيرِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 3], whose meaning is: the flesh of all swine. "اَلطّاغُوتُ" is Satan, and everything worshipped besides Allah is a ṭāghūt. The evidence that "اَلطّاغُوتَ" is Satan is His saying: ﴿وَيُرِيدُ الشَّيْطانُ أنْ يُضِلَّهم ضَلالا بَعِيدًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 60].

zajjaj:77-77.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهم كُفُّوا أيْدِيَكم وأقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾ — it was said: the Muslims, before they were commanded to fight, said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Would that you permitted us to make pickaxes with which to fight the idolaters." So they were commanded to refrain and to perform what was made obligatory upon them other than fighting. Then when fighting was prescribed for them, a party of them feared, and they said: ﴿رَبَّنا لِمَ كَتَبْتَ عَلَيْنا القِتالَ لَوْلا أخَّرْتَنا إلى أجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾; the meaning is: "why did You not postpone us?"

zajjaj:78-78.t:
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the enjoyment of this world is little and that the Hereafter is for the people of piety, and He made known to them that their appointed terms will not miss them even if they fortify themselves in the most impregnable fortresses. So He said: ﴿أيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ المَوْتُ ولَوْ كُنْتُمْ في بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ﴾ — because "مُفَعَّلَةٌ" and "فَعَّلَ" are for intensity/multiplicity (taktīr). One says "شادَ الرَّجُلُ بِناءَهُ، يُشَيِّدُهُ، شَيْدًا" «[Translator's note: so in the text: the past شادَ is paired with the imperfect يُشَيِّدُهُ.]» when he raises it, and when he coats it with shīd, which is what a building is coated with of lime, gypsum and the like. One also says "قَدْ أشادَ الرَّجُلُ بِناءَهُ" (the man raised his building). As for (raising) mention, (one says) "أشَدْتُ بِذِكْرِ فُلانٍ" and nothing else, when you have raised the mention of him.
