His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنْ تُصِبْهم حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُوا هَذِهِ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وإنْ تُصِبْهم سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُوا هَذِهِ مِن عِنْدِكَ﴾ — it was said: the Jews, may they be cursed, took the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as an ill omen when he entered Medina, and said: "Since he entered Medina our fruits have decreased and our prices have risen." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that plenty and drought are from Allah.

zajjaj:128-128.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنِ امْرَأةٌ خافَتْ مِن بَعْلِها نُشُوزًا أوْ إعْراضًا فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِما أنْ يُصْلِحا بَيْنَهُما صُلْحًا﴾: nushūz (ill-conduct) on the part of a woman's husband is that he treats her badly in companionship and withholds from her his person and his maintenance. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said concerning women: ﴿وَعاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 19], and said: ﴿فَإمْساكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإحْسانٍ﴾ [al-Baqara: 229], and said: ﴿وَلا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرارًا لِتَعْتَدُوا﴾ [al-Baqara: 231]. So Allah was strict about justice in the matter of women. Had He — Mighty and Majestic is He — not known that the woman's being content with her husband, so as to remain [married] while he withholds — at many times — his person from her and withholds from her some of what is needed, [is acceptable], keeping her would not have been permissible except with the utmost justice and kindness. [Translator's note: the conditional sentence is elliptical in the source; the bracketed words supply its evident sense.] So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made reconciliation permissible between a man and his wife when she is content for him to prefer another wife over her, and He said that there is no sin upon them in reconciling between themselves a reconciliation, and reconciliation is better than separation.
His saying: ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الأنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾: this is that the woman is grasping about her place with her husband, and the man is grasping with himself towards the woman if another is dearer to him than she is.
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تُحْسِنُوا وتَتَّقُوا﴾, that is: if you treat them well and bear with living with them, ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾, that is: He is aware of that and will recompense you for it.
[Translator's note: the source places the poetry mark ؎ before the following paragraph, which is prose.] If someone says: it was only said «وَإنِ امْرَأةٌ خافَتْ» and He did not say «وَإنْ نَشَزَ رَجُلٌ عَلى المَرْأةِ» ("and if a man behaves ill towards a woman") because the one who fears a thing is not certain of it — the answer to this is: if she fears his persisting in ill-conduct and aversion; and she would not fear [his] persisting unless something had already appeared from him.
As for separating «إنْ» of the conditional (jazāʾ) from a past verb, it is good; but if the separation occurs between «إنْ» and an imperfect verb, that is ugly. If you said «إنِ امْرَأةٌ تَخافُ», it is ugly, because «إنْ» is not separated from what it puts in the jussive. In poetry that is permissible with «إنْ» and others. ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
فَمَتى واغِلٌ يَنُبْهم يَحْبُو ∗∗∗ هُ وتُعْطَفْ عَلَيْهِ كَأْسُ السّاقِي
(Whenever an uninvited guest drops in on them, they make him a gift, and the cupbearer's cup is turned towards him.)
As for the past, «إنْ» does not govern its form, and «إنْ» is the mother of the jussive particles, so it is permissible to separate it from the verb. «اِمْرَأةٌ» is nominative by an implied verb indicated by what follows the noun; the meaning is «إنْ خافَتِ امْرَأةٌ خافَتْ» ("if a woman fears — fears"). As for [particles] other than «إنْ», separation is ugly with them with both past and imperfect: if you said «مَتى زَيْدٌ جاءَنِي أكْرَمْتُهُ» ("whenever Zayd came to me, I honoured him") it would be ugly, while if you said «إنِ اللَّهُ أمْكَنَنِي فَعَلْتُ» ("if Allah enables me, I will do [it]") it would be good and fine.

zajjaj:134-134.t: His saying: ﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوابَ الدُّنْيا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوابُ الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾: the idolaters of the Arabs did not believe in the resurrection, yet they acknowledged that Allah was their Creator; so their drawing near to Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — was only so that He would give them of the good of this world and turn its evil away from them. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the good of this world and the Hereafter is with Him.

zajjaj:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوّامِينَ بِالقِسْطِ﴾: «اَلْقِسْطُ» and «اَلْإقْساطُ» are justice. One says «أقْسَطَ الرَّجُلُ، يُقْسِطُ، إقْساطًا» when he acts justly and brings about equity, and one says «قَسَطَ الرَّجُلُ، قُسُوطًا» when he acts unjustly. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَأقْسِطُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 9], that is: be just; Allah loves the just. And He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَأمّا القاسِطُونَ فَكانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 15], that is: the unjust. One says «قَسَطَ البَعِيرُ، قَسْطًا» when its foreleg has become stiff, and «يَدٌ قَسْطاءُ», that is: stiff. So it is as though «أقْسَطَ» means: he set the thing upright in true balance, and as though «قَسَطَ» in the sense of «جارَ» (acted unjustly) means: he made the thing stiff and spoiled its straight direction.
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ عَلى أنْفُسِكم أوِ الوالِدَيْنِ والأقْرَبِينَ﴾: the meaning is: stand by justice and bear witness for Allah with the truth, even if the right is against the witness himself, or against his parents and his near relatives. ﴿إنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أوْ فَقِيرًا فاللَّهُ أوْلى بِهِما﴾, that is: if the one in whose favour testimony is given is poor, Allah is more entitled to him; and likewise if the one testified against is rich, Allah is more entitled to him. So the interpretation is: establish testimony for Allah against yourselves and your relatives, and do not lean in testimony out of pity for the poor, nor be unjust out of regard for the wealth of a rich man in your eyes.
His saying: ﴿فَلا تَتَّبِعُوا الهَوى أنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾, that is: do not follow desire so that you deviate. ﴿وَإنْ تَلْوُوا أوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾: ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and the people of Medina read «تَلْوُوا» with two wāws, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read with one wāw: «تَلُوا». The more likely, according to what has come in the tafsīr and the position of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr — because it has come in the tafsīr — is that «لَوى الحاكِمُ في قَضِيَّتِهِ» means: he turned away [from the right], for Allah is aware of what you do. One says «لَوَيْتُ فُلانًا حَقَّهُ» when you have put him off from it and delayed him. And «وَإنْ تَلُو» may originally be «تَلْوُوا», then the ḍamma-bearing wāw was replaced by a hamza, so it became «تَلْؤُوا» with the lām quiescent; then the hamza was dropped and its vowel thrown onto the lām, so it became «تَلُو», just as it was said of «أدْؤُرٌ»: «أدُورٌ», then the hamza was dropped and it became «آدُرٌ». [Translator's note: the order of the forms in this last illustration is as in the source.] And «وَإنْ تَلُوا» may be from «اَلْوِلايَةُ» (taking charge), with «تُعْرِضُوا»: that is, if you undertake the matter or turn away from it, ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 128].
And His saying: ﴿فَتَذَرُوها كالمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 129]: it was said: like one held captive, neither without a husband nor having a husband.

zajjaj:136-136.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ والكِتابِ الَّذِي نَـزَّلَ عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾: two views have been stated about it. [The first:] "O you who believe, remain firm in faith in Allah", as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ مِنهم مَغْفِرَةً وأجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 29], that is: He promised those of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in this account who remain firm in faith forgiveness and a great reward. And it was said: by this are meant the hypocrites who displayed assent and concealed denial, so it was said: "O you who displayed faith, believe in Allah and His Messenger", that is: hold inwardly the like of what you have displayed. The first interpretation is more likely, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:137-137.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾: more than one view has been stated about it. Some said: the Jews are meant by it, because they believed in Moses, then disbelieved in ʿUzayr, then believed in ʿUzayr, then disbelieved in Jesus, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muḥammad ﷺ. It was said: it may be a combatant who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved. And it was said: it may be a hypocrite who displayed faith and concealed disbelief, then afterwards believed, then disbelieved, and increased in disbelief by persisting in disbelief.
If someone says: Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — does not forgive disbelief [committed even] a single time, so why is it said here concerning one who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾, and what is the benefit in this? The answer to this — and Allah knows best — is that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — forgives the disbeliever when he believes after his disbelief; but if he disbelieves after his faith, Allah does not forgive him the first disbelief, because Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — accepts repentance, [only for the one who holds to it]; so when he disbelieves after a faith preceded by disbelief, he is held to account for all of his disbelief. [Translator's note: the bracketed clause is added to make the argument explicit; the source simply says "because Allah accepts repentance".] It is not possible that, if he believes after that, He would not forgive him, because Allah — exalted be His praise — forgives every believer after his disbelief; the proof of that is His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبادِهِ ويَعْفُو عَنِ السَّيِّئاتِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 25]. This is frequent in the Quran, and it is also akin to consensus.
The meaning of ﴿وَلا لِيَهْدِيَهم سَبِيلا﴾ is: He will not make them guided by their disbelief; rather He leads them astray, because He — Majestic and Mighty is He — leads astray the defiantly disobedient.

zajjaj:138-138.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿بَشِّرِ المُنافِقِينَ بِأنَّ لَهم عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾: the meaning of «ألِيمٌ» is painful. He said «بَشِّرْ» ("give good tidings"), that is: put in place of good tidings for them "for them is the punishment". The Arabs say: «تَحِيَّتُكَ الضَّرْبُ، وعِتابُكَ السَّيْفُ» ("your greeting is a beating and your reproach is the sword"), that is: you get this in place of a greeting. The poet said:
؎وَخَيْلٍ قَدْ دَلَفْتُ لَها بِخَيْلٍ ∗∗∗ تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وجِيعُ
(Many a troop of horse I advanced against with horse; the greeting between them was painful blows.)

zajjaj:139-139.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿أيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ العِزَّةَ﴾, that is: do the hypocrites seek ʿizza (might) with the disbelievers?! «اَلْعِزَّةُ» is invulnerability and great power to prevail, and it is taken from their saying «أرْضٌ عَزازٌ» ("hard ground").
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: «اَلْعَزازُ» is the raised part of the ground [Translator's note: the source has «اَلنَّفَلُ», probably for «اَلنَّشَزُ», "raised ground"], hard and stony, from which water and torrents run off quickly. These are al-Aṣmaʿī's words. So the interpretation of «اَلْعِزَّةُ» is: power to prevail and strength to which no humiliation attaches. Al-Khansāʾ said:
؎كَأنْ لَمْ يَكُونُوا حِمًى يُتَّقى ∗∗∗ إذِ النّاسُ إذْ ذاكَ مَن عَزَّ بَزّا
(As though they had not been a guarded preserve to be feared, when people at that time were such that whoever prevailed despoiled.)
That is: whoever became strong and prevailed plundered. One says «قَدِ اسْتُعِزَّ عَلى المَرِيضِ» when his pain has become severe; and likewise people's saying «يَعِزُّ عَلَيَّ أنْ تَفْعَلَ» ("it is hard on me that you do"), that is: it is severe. As for their saying «قَدْ عَزَّ الشَّيْءُ» when it is not to be found, its interpretation is: its being found has become hard, that is: it is difficult to find. The end result [of all these] is one.

zajjaj:140-140.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ نَـزَّلَ عَلَيْكم في الكِتابِ أنْ إذا سَمِعْتُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِها ويُسْتَهْزَأُ بِها﴾: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known to the believers that the hypocrites mock the Book of Allah, so they were commanded not to sit with them until they engage in some other talk, that is: in talk other than the Quran.
His saying: ﴿إنَّكم إذًا مِثْلُهُمْ﴾, that is: if you sit with them while they engage in mockery of the Book of Allah, you are like them.

zajjaj:141-141.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكم ونَمْنَعْكم مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: the hypocrites say this when the disbelievers have a share [of success]; they say: "Did we not gain mastery over you?", that is: did we not prevail over you through our allegiance to you, and protect you from the believers through the news of them we used to tell you? «نَسْتَحْوِذُ» in the language is «نَسْتَوْلِي عَلى الشَّيْءِ» ("we take control of a thing"). One says «حاذَ الحِمارُ آتُنَهُ» when the [wild] ass has taken control of his she-asses and gathered them; and likewise «حازَها». The poet said:
؎يَحُوذُهُنَّ ولَهُ حُوذِيُّ
(He drives them together, and he has a driving [gait].)
They also transmitted it as «يَحُوزُهُنَّ ولَهُ حُوزِيُّ». The grammarians said: «اِسْتَحْوَذَ» has come out according to its original form. Whoever says «حاذَ، يَحُوذُ» would say only «اِسْتَحاذَ، يَسْتَحِيذُ»; and whoever said «أحْوَذَ» is like those who said «أجْوَدْتَ» and «أطْيَبْتَ» in the sense of «أجَدْتَ» and «أطَبْتَ»: he brought it out according to the original, and said «اِسْتَحْوَذَ».
His saying: ﴿وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلا﴾, that is: Allah is the helper of the believers with proof and with victory, so He will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers.

zajjaj:142-142.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ المُنافِقِينَ يُخادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وهو خادِعُهُمْ﴾, that is: they try to deceive the Prophet ﷺ by displaying faith to him and concealing disbelief; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made trying to deceive the Prophet ﷺ trying to deceive Him, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبايِعُونَكَ إنَّما يُبايِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 10]. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ﴾, there is more than one view about it. Some said: Allah's "deceiving" them is His recompensing them with punishment for their deception; likewise His saying ﴿وَيَمْكُرُونَ ويَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 30]. And it was said: «وَهو خادِعُهم» by His command — Mighty and Majestic is He — to accept from them what they displayed; so Allah outwits them by that.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَحِلُّ لَكم أنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهًا﴾. Its meaning is: that you force them into marriage with you. This was revealed because, when a woman's husband died and he had a son by another woman, his son would throw a covering over her and say: "I have the most right to her," and would marry her on the contract by which his father had married her, so as to inherit from her what she had inherited from his father. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this is forbidden.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾: these [women] are other than those. Allah forbade that a woman be subjected to ʿaḍl; the meaning of ”تُعْضَلُ“ is: she is prevented from marrying. When a man among them had married a woman for whom he had no need, he would keep her confined so that she would ransom herself from him; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this is not lawful. ”تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ“ may be accusative and may be jussive. As for the accusative, it is on [the sense]: "it is not lawful for you to inherit women, nor to prevent them (وَلا أنْ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ)"; and it may be jussive as a prohibition.

﴿إلا أنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾: "the indecency" is fornication. ﴿وَعاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾, that is: with fairness in [allotting] nights and in maintenance, and with graciousness in speech.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنْ أرَدْتُمُ اسْتِبْدالَ زَوْجٍ مَكانَ زَوْجٍ﴾. Its meaning is: if you want to release a woman — when the man wants to take another in her place and she does not want [the separation]. Allah was severe about this in His saying: ﴿وَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا بِبَعْضِ ما آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ [al-Nisa: 19].

﴿وَآتَيْتُمْ إحْداهُنَّ قِنْطارًا فَلا تَأْخُذُوا مِنهُ شَيْئًا﴾: ”اَلْقِنْطارُ“ is a great amount of wealth; we have explained what people have said about it in Surat Al ʿImran.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَلا تَأْخُذُوا مِنهُ شَيْئًا﴾: Allah forbade taking from the dower by way of causing harm, by His saying: ﴿أتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتانًا وإثْمًا مُبِينًا﴾. ”اَلْبُهْتانُ“ is the falsehood at whose falseness one is left bewildered. ”بُهْتانًا“ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) placed in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is: "Would you take it, slandering and sinning?"

zajjaj:21-21.t:
﴿وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وقَدْ أفْضى بَعْضُكم إلى بَعْضٍ﴾. Al-ifḍāʾ: its basic meaning is intercourse. Some of them said: "When he has been alone with her, he has 'gone in unto' her (afḍā), whether he had intercourse or not." ﴿وَأخَذْنَ مِنكم مِيثاقًا غَلِيظًا﴾: some of them said: it is the contract of the dower; some of them said: the solemn covenant is His saying: ﴿فَإمْساكٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإحْسانٍ﴾ [al-Baqara: 229].

And His saying: ﴿وَلا يَحِلُّ لَكم أنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِمّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 229]: releasing with kindness does not consist in your taking her dower from her; that is releasing with ill-treatment, not with kindness.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكم مِنَ النِّساءِ إلا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾. The meaning is: do not marry as those before you used to marry what their fathers had married; this is the meaning of ﴿إلا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾. ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً﴾: the meaning is: except what has already passed, for it was an indecency, that is, fornication, and an abhorrence (maqt); ”اَلْمَقْتُ“ is the most intense hatred. ﴿وَساءَ سَبِيلا﴾, that is: and how evil a way — that is, that way is an evil way. The meaning is that they were made aware that in the Jāhiliyya this used to be called "maqt", and the child born of it was called "al-maqtī"; so they were informed that this which had been forbidden to them had always been reprehensible in their own hearts and abhorred among them.

Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it is possible that ”كانَ“ is redundant (zāʾida), the meaning on this [view] being: "it is an indecency and an abhorrence". He recited for this the poet's saying:
؎فَكَيْفَ إذا حَلَلْتُ بِدارِ قَوْمٍ ∗∗∗ وجِيرانٍ لَنا كانُوا كِرامِ
(So how [would it be] when I alight at the abode of a people, and neighbours of ours, noble ones?)
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: This is an error on the part of Abū al-ʿAbbās, because if ”كانَ“ were redundant it would not put its predicate in the accusative. The proof of this is the very verse he recited: ”وَجِيرانٍ لَنا كانُوا كِرامِ“ — he did not say ”كانُوا كِرامًا“.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكم وبَناتُكم وأخَواتُكم وعَمّاتُكم وخالاتُكم وبَناتُ الأخِ وبَناتُ الأُخْتِ﴾. This is called "the absolute prohibition" (al-taḥrīm al-mubham). Many of the people of knowledge do not distinguish convincingly between the absolute and the non-absolute. This [category] of the forbidden women was called "absolute" only because it is not lawful in any way or for any cause. Attached to it are ﴿وَأُمَّهاتُكُمُ اللاتِي أرْضَعْنَكم وأخَواتُكم مِنَ الرَّضاعَةِ﴾; suckling has brought these forbidden women into the absolute [category].

﴿وَأُمَّهاتُ نِسائِكُمْ﴾: people have disagreed about these. Some of them made it absolute and some made it non-absolute. The one who made it absolute said: when a man marries a woman, her mother becomes forbidden to him whether he has consummated the marriage with her or not; and he argued that ”اَللّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ“ ("with whom you have consummated marriage") is connected only with the stepdaughters. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ﴿وَأُمَّهاتُ نِسائِكُمْ﴾ is among the absolute [prohibitions].

﴿وَرَبائِبُكُمُ اللاتِي في حُجُورِكم مِن نِسائِكُمُ اللاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: ”اَللّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ“ is a naʿt (adjective) of the women who are the mothers of the stepdaughters, and nothing else. He said: the proof of that is people's consensus that the stepdaughter is lawful if the marriage with her mother has not been consummated; and whoever allows His saying ﴿مِن نِسائِكُمُ اللاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ﴾ to refer to "the mothers of your wives", the meaning on his construal would be: "and the mothers of your wives, from among your wives with whom you have consummated marriage" — so it would follow that ”اَللّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ“ [also] refers to the mothers of the stepdaughters. [Translator's note: the sentence is translated as written; the argument appears to be that such a reading would make one qualifier serve two different heads.] The proof that what Abū al-ʿAbbās said is correct is that when two predications differ, their naʿt cannot be one: the grammarians do not allow ”مَرَرْتُ بِنِسائِكَ، وهَرَبْتُ مِن نِساءِ زَيْدٍ الظَّرِيفاتِ“ ("I passed by your women and fled from the women of Zayd, the charming ones"), with ”اَلظَّرِيفاتِ“ being a naʿt for both these women and those women. Those who held this view — I mean those who treated ”أُمَّهاتُ نِسائِكم“ as being governed by His saying ”مِن نِسائِكُمُ اللّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ“ — could only make it accusative on [an implied] ”أعْنِي“ ("I mean"), so that the meaning is: "I mean those with whom you have consummated marriage." But that ”وَأُمَّهاتُ نِسائِكم“ completes these absolute prohibitions, and that "the stepdaughters" are the ones who become lawful if there has never been consummation with their mothers — and not the mothers of your wives — is the excellent, conclusive [view].

As for the stepdaughter (al-rabība), she is the daughter of a man's wife by another man. Its meaning is ”مَرْبُوبَةٌ“ ("fostered"), because the man fosters her. She may be called ”رَبِيبَةً“ because he undertook her upbringing, whether she was in his care or was not brought up in his care, because when a man marries her mother he is called her rabīb (foster-father). The Arabs name agents and patients by what befalls them and what they bring about: they say ”هَذا مَقْتُولٌ“ ("this one is slain") and ”هَذا ذَبِيحٌ“ ("this is a slaughtered animal"), that is, that has befallen them; and ”هَذا قاتِلٌ“ ("this is a killer"), that is, he has killed; and "this is the sacrificial animal (أُضْحِيَةُ) of the family of so-and-so", for what they have sacrificed; likewise ”هَذِهِ قَتُوبَةٌ“ and ”هَذِهِ حَلُوبَةٌ“, that is, [a camel] that is saddled and that is milked.

His saying: ﴿وَحَلائِلُ أبْنائِكُمُ﴾ is the plural of ”حَلِيلَةٌ“, which is the wife of a man's son; she is not lawful to the father, and she is among the absolute [prohibitions]. ”حَلِيلَةٌ“ means ”مُحَلَّةٌ“ ("made lawful"), derived from ”اَلْحَلالُ“ ("the lawful").

﴿وَأنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الأُخْتَيْنِ﴾: ”أنْ“ is in the position of the nominative; the meaning is: these things have been forbidden, and the combining of two sisters. ﴿إلا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾: the meaning is: apart from what has already passed, for that is forgiven you.

zajjaj:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿ما أصابَكَ مِن حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ وما أصابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ﴾ — this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ by which mankind is meant. Addressing the Prophet ﷺ may be (an address) to all people, because he — peace be upon him — is their tongue. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]: He called the Prophet ﷺ alone, and the address came to include him and the rest of his community. So the meaning of "﴿ما أصابَكَ مِن حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ﴾" is: whatever spoils you obtained, or plenty that came to you, is from Allah's bounty. ﴿وَما أصابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ﴾, i.e. of drought or defeat in war, ﴿فَمِن نَفْسِكَ﴾, i.e. that befell you because of what you earned, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَما أصابَكم مِن مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أيْدِيكم ويَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 30]. The meaning of ﴿وَأرْسَلْناكَ لِلنّاسِ رَسُولا﴾: the meaning of "اَلرَّسُولُ" here is emphatic of His saying ﴿وَأرْسَلْناكَ﴾, because "وَأرْسَلْناكَ لِلنّاسِ" (and We have sent you to the people) indicates that he is a messenger. ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾, i.e. Allah has borne witness that he is truthful and that he is His Messenger. "شَهِيدًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), because if you say "كَفى اللَّهُ" (Allah sufficed) and do not make clear in what the sufficing is, you are being vague. The fāʾ entered in His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿ما أصابَكَ مِن حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, because the speech is in the implied sense of a conditional with its apodosis (jazāʾ); it is equivalent to your saying "إنْ تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ" (if good befalls you, it is from Allah).

zajjaj:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أطاعَ اللَّهَ﴾, i.e. whoever accepts what the Messenger brought has accepted only what Allah commanded.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن تَوَلّى فَما أرْسَلْناكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا﴾ — its interpretation, and Allah knows best, is that you do not know what is hidden of them; you have only what appears from them. The evidence for this is what follows it, namely His saying:

zajjaj:81-81.t:
﴿وَيَقُولُونَ طاعَةٌ﴾ — the grammarians said: its implied form is "أمْرُنا طاعَةٌ" (our affair is obedience). Some said: "مِنّا طاعَةٌ" (from us is obedience). The meaning is one, except that implying "أمْرُنا" fits the story more comprehensively and is better.
His saying: ﴿فَإذا بَرَزُوا مِن عِنْدِكَ بَيَّتَ طائِفَةٌ مِنهم غَيْرَ الَّذِي تَقُولُ﴾ — of every matter decided by night one says "قَدْ بُيِّتَ" (it has been plotted by night). The poet said:
أتَوْنِي فَلَمْ أدْرِ ما بَيَّتُوا ∗∗∗ وكانُوا أتَوْنِي لِأمْرٍ نُكُرْ
(They came to me, and I did not know what they had plotted by night; they had come to me for some abominable matter.)
I.e. you are not a guardian over them, knowing what is hidden from you of their affairs. This and its like in the Book of Allah are among the clearest signs of the Prophet ﷺ, because they did not conceal from him any matter but that Allah disclosed it to him.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿واللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ ما يُبَيِّتُونَ﴾ — there are two interpretations of it. It may be — and Allah knows best — that He reveals it to you in His Book; and it may be that "يَكْتُبُ ما يُبَيِّتُونَ" means He records it against them so that they will be requited for it.
His saying: ﴿فَأعْرِضْ عَنْهم وتَوَكَّلْ عَلى اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. do not name these people individually, because Allah wished to keep the affair of the hypocrites covered until the affair of Islam became firmly established. As for His saying ﴿بَيَّتَ طائِفَةٌ مِنهُمْ﴾, using the masculine and not saying "بَيَّتَتْ", it is because with every non-real feminine, expressing it with the masculine form is permissible: you say "قالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ" (a party of the People of the Book said, feminine) and "قالَ طائِفَةٌ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ" (a party of the Muslims said, masculine), because "طائِفَةٌ" (party) and "فَرِيقٌ" (group) have one meaning. Likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمَن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 275].
And His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ قَدْ جاءَتْكم مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 57] — He means the exhortation (al-waʿẓ) when you say "فَمَن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ". The readers read "بَيَّتْ طائِفَةٌ" with the tāʾ quiescent and assimilated into the ṭāʾ. It is related from al-Kisāʾī that this, when in a verb, is ugly. But there is no difference in assimilation here whether in a verb or in a noun: if you said "بَيَّتُ طائِفَةً" and "هَذا بَيْتُ طائِفَةٍ", intending "بَيَّتُّ طائِفَةً" (I plotted against a party by night), it would be the same. Assimilation is permissible only because the tāʾ and the ṭāʾ are from one point of articulation.

zajjaj:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿أفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ القُرْآنَ ولَوْ كانَ مِن عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلافًا كَثِيرًا﴾ — by it the hypocrites are meant. I.e. regarding what they are informed of concerning what they plotted by night and what they conceal, and what is revealed to the Prophet ﷺ — were it not from Allah, the informing of it would not have been free of discrepancy, because none knows the unseen except Allah. This is among the clear signs of the Prophet ﷺ. The meaning of "تَدَبَّرْتُ الشَّيْءَ" is: I looked into its outcome (ʿāqiba). Their saying in the ḥadīth "لا تَدابَرُوا" means: do not be enemies, i.e. let none of you turn his back (dubur) on another. One says "قَدْ دَبَرَ القَوْمُ، يَدْبُرُونَ، دِبارًا" when they perish, and "أدْبَرُوا" when their affair has turned away. Its interpretation is only that their affair has been pursued to its end, so that no remnant of them remained. "اَلدَّبْرُ" is the bees; it is called "dabr" because it leaves behind (yuʿqibu) what is beneficial. "اَلدِّبْرُ" is abundant wealth; it is called "dibr" because of its abundance and because it remains for the descendants (aʿqāb) and those who come after (adbār).

zajjaj:83-83.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا جاءَهم أمْرٌ مِنَ الأمْنِ أوِ الخَوْفِ أذاعُوا بِهِ﴾, i.e. they made it public and proclaimed it among the people. The poet said:
أذاعَ بِهِ في النّاسِ حَتّى كَأنَّهُ ∗∗∗ بِعَلْياءَ نارٌ أُوقِدَتْ بِثُقُوبِ
(He spread it among the people until it was as though it were a fire kindled with kindling on a high place.)
When the Prophet ﷺ knew that he would prevail over a people, being secure from them, or was informed of the gathering of a people of whose like a gathering is to be feared, the hypocrites would broadcast that, so that those of the disbelievers who would take precautions might take precautions, and the hearts of those whose hearts would be strengthened by what they broadcast might be strengthened. The weak among the Muslims would spread it along with them without knowing the harm in that. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Had they referred that to taking it from the Messenger and from those in authority among them..." — i.e. from the people of knowledge and judgement among them.
His saying: ﴿لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنهُمْ﴾, i.e.
these weak Muslims who broadcast it would have learned it from the Prophet ﷺ and the people of knowledge, and they would along with that have known whether it ought to be broadcast or not. The meaning of ﴿يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ﴾ in the language is: they extract it. Its origin is from "اَلنَّبَطُ", which is the water that comes out of a well when it is first dug. From that one says "قَدْ أنْبَطَ فُلانٌ في غَضْراءَ", i.e. he drew out water from pure clay. The Nabaṭ were called "Nabaṭ" only because of their extracting what is brought out of the lands.
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَتُهُ لاتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطانَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ — some said: were it not for the Quran that Allah sent down to you, and the signs He made clear to you on the tongue of His Prophet, you would have followed Satan except a few, i.e. your first state was in proximity to disbelief. This is not the view of any of the people of language. All the people of language said: the meaning of "وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَتُهُ لاتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطانَ إلّا قَلِيلًا" — it is only an exception from His saying "لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنهم إلّا قَلِيلًا" (those of them who extract it would have known it, except a few). The grammarians said: the meaning is "they broadcast it, except a few", and they said: that the exception be from "أذاعُوا بِهِ إلّا قَلِيلًا" is better, because what is known by extraction is not known by the majority; only the few extract, because merits, extraction and drawing-out are found in the few among people. This, in this place, is an error on the part of the grammarians, because this extraction is not something drawn out by reflection and thought; it is only the extraction of a report, and the majority know a report when they are told it; only the few who are extreme in dullness do not know what they are told. The first view, along with these two views, are all permissible — and Allah knows best — because before the Quran was revealed and before the Prophet was sent, there was among people a few who believed without having witnessed the Quran or the Prophet ﷺ. And one may say: whoever was a believer before this believed by the bounty of Allah and His mercy; so no one who attains the reward of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is without bounty and mercy — except that what is intended by it in this place is the Prophet ﷺ and the Quran.

zajjaj:84-84.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَقاتِلْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لا تُكَلَّفُ إلا نَفْسَكَ﴾ — this fāʾ is the answer to His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن يُقاتِلْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيُقْتَلْ أوْ يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 74] — ﴿فَقاتِلْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾. It may also be connected to His saying ﴿وَما لَكم لا تُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 75], i.e. what do you gain by abandoning fighting? So fight in the way of Allah. So Allah commanded him to fight, even if he fought alone, because He had guaranteed him victory. It is related that Abū Bakr — may Allah have mercy on him — said during the apostasy (al-ridda): "Were my right hand to oppose me, I would fight it with my left."
His saying: ﴿عَسى اللَّهُ أنْ يَكُفَّ بَأْسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا واللَّهُ أشَدُّ بَأْسًا وأشَدُّ تَنْكِيلا﴾ — "اَلْبَأْسُ" is severity in everything.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنها ومَن يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً سَيِّئَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ كِفْلٌ مِنها﴾ — "اَلْكِفْلُ" in the language is the share. It is taken from their saying "أكْفَلْتَ البَعِيرَ" when you wrap a cloth around the camel's hump, or around a place on its back, and ride on it. It was called "كِفْلٌ", and (one says) "اِكْتُفِلَ البَعِيرُ", only because the whole back was not used; only a share of the back was used, and not all of it.
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتًا﴾ — some said: "اَلْمُقِيتُ" is the All-Powerful; others said: "اَلْمُقِيتُ" is the Preserver (al-ḥafīẓ). In my view — and Allah knows best — it is closer to "the Preserver", because it is derived from "اَلْقُوتُ" (sustenance): one says "قُتُّ الرَّجُلَ، أقُوتُهُ، قُوتًا" when I preserve his life for him with what sustains him; and "اَلْقُوتُ" is the name of that thing which preserves his life, with no surplus in it beyond the measure of preservation. So the meaning of "اَلْمُقِيتُ" — and Allah knows best — is the Preserver, who gives a thing the measure of preservation it needs. The poet said:
ألِيَ الفَضْلُ أمْ عَلَيَّ إذا ∗∗∗ حُوسِبْتُ إنِّي عَلى الحِسابِ مُقِيتُ
(Is the surplus to my credit or against me when I am called to account? I am a muqīt over the reckoning.)

zajjaj:86-86.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإذا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا بِأحْسَنَ مِنها﴾ — the grammarians said: "أحْسَنَ" here is an adjective that is a diptote (lā yanṣarif), because it is on the pattern "أفْعَلُ" and is an adjective; the meaning is: then greet with a greeting better than it. It was said in the exegesis: "اَلتَّحِيَّةُ" here is the salām (greeting of peace), and it is of the pattern "تَفْعِلَةٌ" from "حَيَّيْتُ". The meaning of "حَيُّوا بِأحْسَنَ مِنها" is: when "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكم" (peace be upon you) is said to you, then say "وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلامُ ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ" (and upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah); so the greeting that is better than it is "وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلامُ ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وبَرَكاتُهُ" (and upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings). It is said: "Everything has a limit, and the limit of the salām is the word (وَبَرَكاتُهُ)." It is related «that someone came in to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وبَرَكاتُهُ", and the Prophet ﷺ said: "وَعَلَيْكَ" (and upon you). Another came in and said: "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكُمْ", and the Prophet ﷺ said: "وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلامُ ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ". Another man came in and said: "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ", and the Prophet ﷺ said: "وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلامُ ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وبَرَكاتُهُ". The first one who came in stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I greeted you and you added nothing to 'وَعَلَيْكَ', while this one stood and said 'اَلسَّلامَ عَلَيْكُمْ' and you gave him more, and this one stood and said 'اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ' and you gave him more." The Prophet ﷺ said: "You left nothing of the salām, so I returned it to you; these two left something of it, so I gave them more."» This is evidence that the last word of the salām in the Sunna is the word "وبَرَكاتُهُ".
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا﴾, i.e. He gives everything, of knowledge, preservation and requital, the measure that is ḥasb for it, i.e. that suffices it. You say "حَسْبُكَ بِهَذا" (this is enough for you), i.e. "be content with this". And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿عَطاءً حِسابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 36], i.e. sufficient. Reckoning in dealings is called "ḥisāb" only because by it is known what is sufficient, with no excess over the measure and no deficiency.

zajjaj:87-87.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾ — this is the lām of the oath, as in your saying "واللَّهِ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم" (by Allah, He will surely gather you). The meaning of "اَلْقِيامَةُ" in the language — and Allah knows best — is of two kinds. It may have been called "al-qiyāma" because people rise (yaqūmūna) from their graves; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ كَأنَّهم جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]. And it may have been called "al-qiyāma" because people stand for the reckoning; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النّاسُ لِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 6]. The meaning of "لَيَجْمَعَنَّكم" — and Allah knows best — is: He gathers you in death and in your graves.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿فَما لَكم في المُنافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾ — this is an address to the Muslims. That is because some of the hypocrites said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We have found the climate of Medina unwholesome; would that you permitted us to go out to the desert." When they went out, they kept travelling stage after stage until they joined the idolaters. Some of the Muslims said: "They are disbelievers, they are disbelievers," and some said: "They are Muslims until we know that they have changed." So Allah commanded that the Muslims agree on declaring disbelievers those who used a ruse against the Prophet ﷺ and opposed him. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَما لَكم في المُنافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾, i.e. what do you gain by disagreeing about them? ﴿واللَّهُ أرْكَسَهم بِما كَسَبُوا﴾: the interpretation of "أرْكَسَهم" in the language is: He turned them upside down and sent them back. One says "أرْكَسَهُ" and "رَكَسَهُ". The meaning of "واللَّهُ أرْكَسَهم بِما كَسَبُوا" is: He returned them to the ruling of the disbelievers.
His saying: ﴿أتُرِيدُونَ أنْ تَهْدُوا مَن أضَلَّ اللَّهُ﴾, i.e. do you say that these are rightly guided when Allah has led them astray?! ﴿وَمَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلا﴾, i.e. a way to the argument. The grammarians said concerning the accusative of "فِئَتَيْنِ": it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Sībawayh said: when you say "ما لَكَ قائِمًا؟!" (what is the matter with you, standing?!), its meaning is only "why did you stand?", and it is put in the accusative on the interpretation "what thing is established for you in this state?" Someone else said: "قائِمًا" here is accusative by way of the verb "مالَ" «[Translator's note: so in the text.]», and he permits "ما لَكَ قائِمًا؟!" and "ما لَكَ القائِمَ يا هَذا؟!". But "ما لَكَ القائِمَ" is wrong, because "اَلْقائِمَ" is definite and so cannot occur as a ḥāl; and "ما" is one of the interrogative particles and does not operate as "كانَ" does. Were "ما لَكَ القائِمَ يا هَذا؟!" permissible, it would be permissible to say "ما عِنْدَكَ القائِمَ" and "ما بِكَ القائِمَ"; and by consensus "ما عِنْدَكَ القائِمَ" is wrong, so "ما لَكَ القائِمَ" is like it — there is no difference in that.

zajjaj:89-89.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنهم أوْلِياءَ حَتّى يُهاجِرُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. do not take as allies any of those who used a ruse against the Prophet ﷺ until they parted from him, i.e. do not say that they are believers, ﴿حَتّى يُهاجِرُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. until they return to the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾, i.e. they turn away from emigrating and persist in remaining in what they are upon, ﴿فَخُذُوهم واقْتُلُوهم حَيْثُ وجَدْتُمُوهم ولا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنهم ولِيًّا ولا نَصِيرًا﴾.

zajjaj:90-90.t:
His saying: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إلى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَهم مِيثاقٌ﴾, i.e. so kill them, except whoever is connected with a people between whom and you there is a covenant. It is related that these were connected with the Banū Mudlij, who were at peace with the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿أوْ جاءُوكم حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهم أنْ يُقاتِلُوكم أوْ يُقاتِلُوا قَوْمَهُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: their breasts were too constricted to fight you or to fight their own people. The grammarians said: "حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهم" means "or they come to you, their breasts having become constricted (qad ḥaṣirat)", because "حَصِرَتْ" cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial) except with "قَدْ". Some said: "حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهم" is a predicate after a predicate, as if He said "أوْ جاؤُوكم" (or they come to you), and then gave a report, saying "حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهم أنْ يُقاتِلُوكم" (their breasts are constricted against fighting you).
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَسَلَّطَهم عَلَيْكم فَلَقاتَلُوكُمْ﴾, i.e. the constriction of their breasts against fighting you is only because Allah has cast terror into their breasts. Some read "حَصِرَةً صُدُورُهم" as a ḥāl.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿والمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ﴾. The reading is with the fatḥa [on the ṣād]; there is consensus on the fatḥa in this [verse], because its meaning is "those who have been made chaste (uḥṣinna) by husbands". If it were read ”والمُحْصِناتِ“, it would be permissible, because they make their private parts chaste (yuḥṣinna) by marrying. The [occurrences] other than this one have been read [both] ”اَلْمُحْصَناتُ“ and ”اَلْمُحْصِناتِ“.

﴿إلا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾, that is: if a man comes to own a married woman in the lands of polytheism, he may have intercourse with her — except that no intercourse at all [is permitted] in [the case of] what the right hand possesses except after istibrāʾ (waiting to establish freedom from pregnancy). Some of them said: when a man comes to own a slave-girl who was married, her sale and his ownership of her have made her lawful [to him], even if she was not married in the lands of polytheism. But the exegesis is as we have described, concerning married women in polytheism.

His saying: ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ is accusative for emphasis (tawkīd), construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of His saying ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisa: 23] is "Allah has prescribed this for you as a prescription", just as the poet said:
؎وَرُضْتُ فَذَلَّتْ صَعْبَةٌ أيَّ إذْلالِ
(I broke her in, and a refractory she-camel was humbled — what humbling!)
because the meaning of ”رُضْتُ“ is "I humbled". It may also be accusative by way of command, with ”عَلَيْكم“ explaining it, the meaning being: "Hold fast to the Book of Allah." It cannot be accusative by ”عَلَيْكم“ [as a verbal noun of command], because your saying ”عَلَيْكَ زَيْدًا“ ("Take hold of Zayd!") has no inflectable governing verb such that its accusative object could be placed before it. As for the poet's saying:
؎يا أيُّها الماتِحُ دَلْوِي دُونَكا ∗∗∗ إنِّي رَأيْتُ النّاسَ يَحْمَدُونَكا
(O you who draw the water, here is my bucket for you; I have seen people praising you.)
”دَلْوِي“ may be in the position of the accusative by an implied "take my bucket" (”خُذْ دَلْوِي“), but not on [the construal] ”دُونَكَ دَلْوِي“, for the reason we have explained. ”دَلْوِي“ may also be in the position of the nominative, the meaning being: "This is my bucket — [it is] for you." And ”كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم“ could be nominative in the sense of "This is Allah's ordinance upon you", as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلا ساعَةً مِن نَهارٍ بَلاغٌ﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

His saying: ﴿وَأُحِلَّ لَكم ما وراءَ ذَلِكُمْ﴾ — and ”أحَلَّ“ (active) too; both are read. The meaning of ”ما وراءَ ذَلِكم“ is: what is beyond that, that is: "what is beyond these things which have been forbidden is lawful, according to what Allah has legislated" — except that the Sunna has forbidden marrying a woman in addition to her paternal aunt, and likewise marrying her in addition to her maternal aunt. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — did not say: "I forbid you nothing other than this," and He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]. I suppose that the maternal aunt is like the mother and the paternal aunt like the father, because the father is like the mother in the obligation of [his] right, and marrying her in addition to her paternal or maternal aunt is among the greatest forms of undutifulness.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أنْ تَبْتَغُوا بِأمْوالِكُمْ﴾ is accusative, or nominative if you wish; the meaning is: "it has been made lawful for you that you seek [them] as muḥṣinīn, not as musāfiḥīn", that is: contracting marriage, ﴿غَيْرَ مُسافِحِينَ﴾, that is: not as fornicators. ”اَلْمُسافِحُ“ and ”اَلْمُسافِحَةُ“ are the two fornicators who do not refrain from fornication [with anyone]; if she fornicates with one [man only], she is one who has a secret lover (dhāt khidn). So Allah forbade fornication in all its forms — open fornication (sifāḥ) and taking a secret friend. Iḥṣān is the guarding of the private parts, that is, keeping them chaste. One says: ”اِمْرَأةٌ حَصانٌ، بَيِّنَةُ الحُصْنِ“ ("a chaste woman, of evident chastity"), ”فَرَسٌ حَصانٌ“ ("a stallion"), of evident taḥaṣṣun and taḥṣīn, and ”بِناءٌ حَصِينٌ“ ("a fortified building"), of evident ḥaṣāna. If ”اَلْحِصانَةُ“ were said for all of it, it would be [acceptable] by consensus. Sifāḥ (fornication) is derived from their saying ”سَفَحْتُ الشَّيْءَ“ ("I poured the thing out"), when you have poured it; fornication is sifāḥ because it flows on without a contract, as if it were like something poured out that nothing holds back.

His saying: ﴿فَما اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنهُنَّ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾. This is a verse about which some people have made a very great error, because of their ignorance of the language. That is, they held that His saying ﴿فَما اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنهُنَّ﴾ is from mutʿa [temporary marriage], which the jurists are agreed is forbidden. The meaning of His saying ﴿فَما اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنهُنَّ﴾ is only: "whomever you have married", on the condition that has been laid down in the verse — the verse of iḥṣān: ﴿أنْ تَبْتَغُوا بِأمْوالِكم مُحْصِنِينَ﴾, that is, contracting the marriage that has been mentioned — "then give them their wages as an obligation", that is, their dowers. If he has enjoyment by consummating the marriage with her, he gives the dower in full; if he has enjoyment [only] through the marriage contract, he gives half the dower. ”اَلْمَتاعُ“ in the language is everything from which benefit is derived; that is mutāʿ.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He — elsewhere: ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلى المُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 236] does not mean "marry them in mutʿa"; the meaning is only: give them something they may enjoy. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَلِلْمُطَلَّقاتِ مَتاعٌ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 241]. Whoever claims that His saying ﴿فَما اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنهُنَّ﴾ is the mutʿa which is the conditional [temporary] enjoyment practised by the Rāfiḍa has made a great error, because the verse is plain and clear.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم فِيما تَراضَيْتُمْ بِهِ مِن بَعْدِ الفَرِيضَةِ﴾, that is: there is no sin upon you in a woman's giving her dower to the man as a gift, or in a man's giving, to a woman with whom he has not consummated marriage, the [other] half of the dower, which is due only to one with whom he has consummated marriage. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾, that is: All-Knowing of what sets the affairs of the servants right, All-Wise in what He has prescribed for them of the marriage contract, by which wealth and lineages are preserved.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكم طَوْلا أنْ يَنْكِحَ المُحْصَناتِ المُؤْمِناتِ﴾. The muḥṣanāt are free women; it has also been said: chaste women. Some of our colleagues said: they are free women specifically. The one who said that they are chaste women claimed that people are forbidden to marry a woman who is not chaste. One should not marry a woman who is not chaste, [but] the proponent of this [other] view argued that His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿الزّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إلا زانِيَةً أوْ مُشْرِكَةً والزّانِيَةُ لا يَنْكِحُها إلا زانٍ أوْ مُشْرِكٌ وحُرِّمَ ذَلِكَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Nur: 3] is abrogated, and that His saying ﴿وَأنْكِحُوا الأيامى مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Nur: 32] can mean: a man may marry whichever women he likes. [Translator's note: the attribution of the two positions in this passage is translated as written; the source is somewhat compressed.] The proof that the muḥṣanāt are the chaste women is His saying: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12], that is: kept her private parts chaste.

”اَلطَّوْلُ“ is the means to pay the dower; so His saying ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكم طَوْلا﴾ means: whoever is unable to pay the dower of a free woman. One says: ”قَدْ طالَ فُلانٌ عَلى فُلانٍ طَوْلًا“, that is, he had superiority over him in means; ”قَدْ طالَ الشَّيْءُ يَطُولُ طُولًا“ ("the thing became long"); ”أطَلْتُهُ إطالَةً“ ("I lengthened it"); and ”قَدْ طالَ طِوَلُكَ، وطِيلُكَ، وطِيَلُكَ“, that is, your span [of life] has been long. The poet said:
؎إنّا مُحَيُّوكَ فاسْلَمْ أيُّها الطَّلَلُ ∗∗∗ وإنْ بَلَغْتَ وإنْ طالَتْ بِكَ الطِّيَلُ
(We greet you — be safe, O ruined encampment, even though you have grown old and long has been your span.)
”اَلطِّوَلُ“ is [also] the tether-rope. The poet said:
؎تُعْرَضُ المُهْرَةُ بِالطِّوَلِّ
(The young mare is paraded on the tether.)
The lām is doubled for the rhyme.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَمِن ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم مِن فَتَياتِكُمُ المُؤْمِناتِ﴾: ”اَلْفَتَياتُ“ are the female slaves; the Arabs call a slave-woman ”فَتاةٌ“ and a slave-man ”فَتًى“. That is: whoever is unable to marry a free woman may marry a slave-woman if he fears sinfulness for himself. ﴿واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِإيمانِكُمْ﴾, that is: act on what is outwardly apparent of you in faith, for you are bound to act on what is apparent of one another.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿بَعْضُكم مِن بَعْضٍ﴾: it was said: in noble descent, that is, all of you are children of Adam. ﴿بَعْضُكم مِن بَعْضٍ﴾ may also mean "your religion is one", because He mentioned here the believing women among the slaves. This was said to them only because the Arabs used to impugn lineages, boast of noble descent and revile [people] for impure birth: they used to call the son of a slave-woman "al-hajīn" (the half-bred). So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the slaves and others are fully equal in faith. Marrying a slave-woman was disliked only when there is a way to [marrying] a free woman, because the children of a free man by a slave-woman become slaves, and because the slave-woman is put to service and drudgery and has much contact with men, which is hard on the husband; for that reason a free man's marrying a slave-woman was disliked. As for boasting of noble descent and reviling lineages, it is a matter of the Jāhiliyya. It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: «”Three things are of the affair of the Jāhiliyya: impugning lineages, boasting of noble descent, and seeking rain by the stars (al-anwāʾ); and they will not be abandoned in Islam.“»

His saying: ﴿فانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإذْنِ أهْلِهِنَّ﴾: Allah commanded that she be married with her master's permission.

His saying: ”فَإذا أحْصَنَّ“ — also read ”أُحْصِنَّ“, with a ḍamma on the alif — ﴿فَإنْ أتَيْنَ بِفاحِشَةٍ فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ ما عَلى المُحْصَناتِ مِنَ العَذابِ﴾, that is: upon them is half the ḥadd (prescribed punishment). The ḥadd is a hundred lashes upon the free man and free woman who are not muḥṣan, and upon the two muḥṣan [persons] stoning. But stoning is killing, and killing has no half; so upon them is only half of the thing that has a half, namely flogging.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَن خَشِيَ العَنَتَ مِنكُمْ﴾, that is: marrying slave-women is permissible for whoever fears al-ʿanat. ”اَلْعَنَتُ“ in the language is severe hardship; from it one says ”أكَمَةٌ عَنُوتٌ“ ("a hard hillock") when it is difficult [to climb]. Abū al-ʿAbbās said: al-ʿanat here is destruction. Others said: its meaning is: that is for whoever fears that desire will drive him to fornication, so that he meets great sin in the Hereafter and the ḥadd in this world. Some of them said: its meaning is that he falls passionately in love with the slave-woman; but there is no passionate love in the verse — though one who is in such love does meet with hardship (ʿanat).

His saying: ﴿وَأنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾, that is: patience is better for you, for the reason we have described, that the children become slaves.

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الرِّجالُ قَوّامُونَ عَلى النِّساءِ﴾ — the man is the one who maintains (qayyim) the woman in what is due to her from him; as for other than that, no. One says "هَذا قَيِّمُ المَرْأةِ، وقِوامُها" (this is the woman's maintainer and her qiwām). The poet said:
اَللَّهُ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَ قَيِّمِها ∗∗∗ يَفِرُّ مِنِّي بِها وأتَّبِعُ
(Allah is between me and her guardian: he flees from me with her, and I follow.)
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assigned that to men because of their superiority in knowledge and discernment, and because of their spending of their wealth on dowries and the provisions of women.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فالصّالِحاتُ قانِتاتٌ﴾, i.e. upholding the rights of their husbands. ﴿بِما حَفِظَ اللَّهُ﴾: its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: by the thing that preserves the command of Allah and the religion of Allah. It may also be in the sense of "بِحِفْظِ اللَّهِ", i.e. by their guarding (the right of) Allah, and that goes back to the command of Allah.
His saying: ﴿واللاتِي تَخافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ﴾ — "اَلنُّشُوزُ" is the aversion of one of the two (spouses) to the other. One says "نَشَزَتِ المَرْأةُ، تَنْشِزُ، وتَنْشُزُ" — both — and both have been read in ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فانْشُزُوا﴾ [al-Mujādila: 11]: "اِنْشِزُوا" and "اُنْشُزُوا", "فانْشِزُوا". Its derivation is from "اَلنَّشْزُ", which is the elevated place of the ground; it is called "نَشْزٌ" and "نَشَزٌ".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿واهْجُرُوهُنَّ في المَضاجِعِ﴾, i.e. in sleeping with them and being near them; for if they love their husbands, being shunned in the beds will be hard on them, and if they are averse, that will suit them, and so it will be an indication of nushūz on their part.
One says "هَجَرْتُ الإنْسانَ، والشَّيْءَ، أهْجُرُهُ، هَجْرًا، وهِجْرانًا" (I shunned the person or the thing); and "أهْجَرَ فُلانٌ مَنصِبَهُ، يُهْجِرُهُ، إهْجارًا" when he speaks obscenely; "هَجَرَ الرَّجُلُ هَجْرًا" when he raves; "هَجَرْتُ البَعِيرَ، أهْجُرُهُ، هَجْرًا" when I put a hijār on it — "اَلْهِجارُ" is a rope tied to the camel's loins and to its pastern; and "هَجَّرْتُ تَهْجِيرًا" when I set out at the time of the hājira, which is midday. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded regarding women that they be dealt with first by admonition, then by shunning afterwards; and if those two do not avail with them, then striking — but it must not be a severe (injurious) striking. If they obey in what is sought from them, then no way is to be sought against them, i.e. no path of harassment is to be sought against them. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا﴾, i.e. He is exalted above imposing anything but what is right and within the measure of capacity.

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقاقَ بَيْنِهِما﴾ — some said: "خِفْتُمْ" here has the meaning of "أيْقَنْتُمْ" (you are certain). This is an error: had we known of the discord for certain, there would be no recourse to the two arbiters; rather discord is (only) feared. Al-shiqāq is enmity; its derivation is from "اَلْمُتَشاقَّيْنِ" (two who are at odds), each of the two being in a shiqq, i.e. on a side. So Allah the Exalted commanded — if you fear the occurrence of enmity between a man and his wife — that they send two arbiters: an arbiter from the woman's family and an arbiter from the man's family. "اَلْحَكَمُ" (the arbiter) is the one who takes charge of what is entrusted to him. It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — that a fiʾām of people — i.e. a large crowd — gathered before him with a woman and her husband between whom a disagreement had occurred. He ordered two arbiters to look into their affair, and said to them: "Do you two know what is incumbent upon you? It is incumbent upon you that if you see fit to separate, you separate, and if you see fit to unite, you unite." Some said: it is upon the two arbiters to admonish, and to make known what each of the husband and the wife has done in overstepping the right; then if they see fit to separate, they separate, and if they see fit to unite, they unite. The reality of the matter of the two arbiters is that they aim at reconciliation; they have no (power of) divorce; it is only upon them to inform the imam of the reality of what they have found. Then if the imam sees fit to separate, he separates, or to unite, he unites. If he delegates to them separation or union, they are in his position. What ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — did is an act which the imam may do, and ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — is sufficient for us as an imam. When he said to them: "If you see fit to unite, you unite, and if you see fit to separate, you separate," he had put them in charge of that and delegated it to them. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا خَبِيرًا﴾, i.e. knowing what is in the welfare of creation, well-informed about that.

zajjaj:144-144.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الكافِرِينَ أوْلِياءَ مِن دُونِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: do not make them your intimates and your close associates. ﴿أتُرِيدُونَ أنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْكم سُلْطانًا مُبِينًا﴾, that is: a manifest proof. «اَلسُّلْطانُ» in the language is proof; the caliph and the emir were called «سُلْطانٌ» only because its meaning is that he is the possessor of proof [i.e. authority]. The Arabs treat sulṭān as feminine and as masculine, saying «قَضَتْ عَلَيْكَ بِهَذا السُّلْطانُ» ("the sulṭān [fem.] decided this against you") and «أمَرَتْكَ بِهِ السُّلْطانُ» ("the sulṭān [fem.] commanded you to do it"). A group of the transmitters claimed that the feminine is more frequent in it, while there is no disagreement about the masculine; I reckon those who transmitted that did not accurately distinguish the frequent from the rare, and the masculine is more frequent in it. As for the Quran, sulṭān does not occur in it except as masculine. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿لَوْلا يَأْتُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِسُلْطانٍ بَيِّنٍ﴾ [al-Kahf: 15], and said: ﴿هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 29], and said: ﴿سُلْطانًا مُبِينًا﴾. So every mention of sulṭān in the Quran is masculine, and had the feminine been more frequent it would have been in the Book of Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He.
If someone says: they only transmitted that «اَلسُّلْطانُ» [meaning the ruler] among people is the feminine one, it is said [in reply]: «اَلسُّلْطانُ» [as ruler] only means "the possessor of sulṭān", and «اَلسُّلْطانُ» is proof; «اَلِاحْتِجاجُ» (argumentation) and «اَلْحُجَّةُ» (proof) have one meaning. As for the feminine, it is correct, except that it is less frequent than the masculine. Whoever says «قَضَتْ بِهِ عَلَيْكَ السُّلْطانُ» means «قَضَتْ عَلَيْكَ بِهِ الحُجَّةُ» ("the proof [fem.] decided it against you") and «قَضَتْ عَلَيْكَ حُجَّةُ الوالِي» ("the governor's proof decided against you"); and whoever says «قَضى بِهِ عَلَيْكَ السُّلْطانُ» has gone to the meaning of «صاحِبُ السُّلْطانِ» ("the holder of authority"), and it is possible that he took it in the sense of «اَلْبُرْهانُ» (demonstration) and «اَلِاحْتِجاجُ» (argumentation), that is: «قَضى بِهِ عَلَيْكَ البُرْهانُ» ("the demonstration [masc.] decided it against you").

zajjaj:145-145.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ المُنافِقِينَ في الدَّرْكِ الأسْفَلِ مِنَ النّارِ﴾: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā said: Hell has adrāk, that is: levels, and each level of it is a darak.
The reading is «اَلدَّرَكِ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ and «اَلدَّرْكِ» with the rāʾ quiescent. The people of Medina and the people of Basra read it «اَلدَّرَكِ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, while the people of Kufa — al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb — read «اَلدَّرْكِ». There is disagreement about it from ʿĀṣim: some transmitted it from him as «اَلدَّرَكِ» and some transmitted it as «اَلدَّرْكِ» — that is, with both the vowel and the sukūn. The people of the language have reported both dialectal forms, except that the preferred choice is fatḥa on the rāʾ, because of the agreement of the Medinans and the Basrans on it, and because none of the ḥadīth transmitters has related it except as «اَلدَّرَكِ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ. For that reason we chose «اَلدَّرَكِ».
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهم نَصِيرًا﴾, that is: no protector will protect them from the punishment of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — and no intercessor will intercede for them.

zajjaj:146-146.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ المُؤْمِنِينَ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾: the yāʾ has been omitted from the script in this place. The grammarians held that the yāʾ was omitted from the script just as it is omitted in pronunciation, because the yāʾ drops from pronunciation owing to its being quiescent and the lām in «اَللَّهُ» being quiescent. Likewise His saying ﴿يَوْمَ يُنادِ المُنادِ﴾ [Qāf: 41]: the yāʾ of «يُنادِ» was omitted in the script for this reason; and likewise ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبانِيَةَ﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 18] and ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 6]: the wāws were omitted here because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
As for the saying of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ذَلِكَ ما كُنّا نَبْغِ﴾ [al-Kahf: 64], it is like His saying ﴿يُنادِ المُنادِ﴾ [Qāf: 41] and ﴿يَدْعُ الدّاعِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 6]: these yāʾs, of the type of «نَبْغِ», were omitted because the kasra indicated the yāʾ, so the yāʾ was omitted for its heaviness; but omitting it is not the preferred way according to the grammarians. As for «اَلْمُنادِي» and «اَلدّاعِي», the yāʾ was omitted from them just as it is omitted before the entry of the alif and lām [i.e. the definite article], because you say «هَذا داعٍ» and «هَذا مُنادٍ». As for ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا يَسْرِ﴾ [al-Fajr: 4], the yāʾ was omitted because it is the end of a verse, and at verse-ends omission is permissible, just as it is permissible at the ends of lines of poetry.

zajjaj:148-148.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿لا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ القَوْلِ إلا مَن ظُلِمَ﴾, and «إلّا مَن ظَلَمَ» — it is read both ways. The meaning is that the one wronged may make his grievance public by way of complaint, while the wrongdoer speaks evil openly out of wrongdoing and aggression. The position of «مَن» is accusative in both cases, because it is an exception not from the first [category]; the meaning is: Allah does not love the public utterance of evil speech, but the one wronged makes his grievance public by way of complaint, and the wrongdoer speaks it openly out of wrongdoing. It is also possible that the position of «مَن» is nominative, in the sense of «لا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ أنْ يَجْهَرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ القَوْلِ إلّا مَن ظُلِمَ» ("Allah does not love that anyone should speak evil openly except the one wronged"), so that «مَن» is a badal (substitute) from the implied sense of «أحَدٌ» (anyone); the meaning is: «لا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ أنْ يَجْهَرَ أحَدٌ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ القَوْلِ إلّا المَظْلُومُ».
There is another option in it, which I do not know the grammarians to have mentioned: that «إلّا مَن ظَلَمَ» is in the sense of «لَكِنَّ الظّالِمَ اجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ القَوْلِ» ("but as for the wrongdoer, speak out evil to him openly"). This, too, is an exception not from the first [category]; it is a good option, and its position is accusative. It has been related that this was revealed concerning the guest who is ill-treated: he may complain to you [Translator's note: so in the source, «فَلَهُ أنْ يَشْكُوَ لَكَ»]. Its true sense is what we have said, and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:153-153.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْألُكَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ أنْ تُنَـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ كِتابًا مِنَ السَّماءِ فَقَدْ سَألُوا مُوسى أكْبَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ﴾: this was when they said to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿وَلَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتّى تُنَـزِّلَ عَلَيْنا كِتابًا نَقْرَؤُهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 93], that is: they asked Moses after he had brought them the signs, ﴿فَقالُوا أرِنا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾. The people of the language have stated two views about «جَهْرَةً». Abū ʿUbayda said: [it means] «قالُوا جَهْرَةً أرِنا اللَّهَ» ("they said openly: show us Allah"), because if they saw Allah, then [even] the hidden would be open; so «جَهْرَةً» describes their saying. Some said: «أرِنا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً» only means «أرِنا رُؤْيَةً بَيِّنَةً مُنْكَشِفَةً ظاهِرَةً» ("show us [Him] with a clear, unveiled, manifest seeing"), because whoever knows Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has increased in knowledge, but they asked Him for a seeing that they could perceive with their eyes.
The proof of this view is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإذْ قُلْتُمْ يا مُوسى لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتّى نَرى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 55]. In my view this is the clear view, if Allah wills.

zajjaj:155-155.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ﴾: «ما» is redundant (laghw) in the wording; the meaning is «فَبِنَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهم حَقًّا» ("so for their breaking their covenant, truly"). Just as «حَقًّا» serves to emphasise the matter, so «ما» has entered for emphasis. The interpretation of their breaking their covenant is that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — took the covenant from them that they would make clear what He had revealed to them concerning mention of the Prophet ﷺ and other things. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَإذْ أخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنّاسِ ولا تَكْتُمُونَهُ فَنَبَذُوهُ وراءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 187]. What brings in the bāʾ and governs it is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 160]; the meaning is: for their breaking their covenant and the things mentioned after it. And His saying «فَبِظُلْمٍ» is a badal (substitute) for His saying ﴿فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿قُلُوبُنا غُلْفٌ﴾, that is: vessels of knowledge. ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾: if you wish, you assimilate the lām into the ṭāʾ; likewise ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 16] is assimilated, so you say «بَـ طُّبِعَ» and «بَـ تُّؤْثِرُونَ». Allah made their recompense for their disbelief that He sealed their hearts.

zajjaj:156-156.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلى مَرْيَمَ بُهْتانًا عَظِيمًا﴾: «اَلْبُهْتانُ» is a lie that bewilders by its severity and enormity. That is because the Jews — may Allah curse them — accused Mary, who is Allah's chosen one above the women of the worlds, of a grave matter.

zajjaj:157-157.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ إنّا قَتَلْنا المَسِيحَ عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: by their confessing to having killed him. ﴿وَما قَتَلُوهُ وما صَلَبُوهُ ولَكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ﴾: so they were punished, or will be punished, with the punishment of one who kills, or [because] it was made to appear so to them, since they committed the act as the killing of a prophet. It has come in the tafsīr that when Allah — exalted be His praise — willed to raise Jesus to Himself and purify him from them, he said to his companions: "Which of you will accept that my likeness be cast upon him, and be killed and crucified, and enter Paradise?" A man of them said: "I." So his likeness was cast upon him and he was killed, and Allah raised Jesus to Himself. None of this is impossible, because we do not doubt that it was made to appear so to them.
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفي شَكٍّ مِنهُ﴾, that is: those who differed about his killing are in doubt, because some of them claimed that he is a god and was not killed, and some of them stated that he was killed, and they are in doubt about that. ﴿ما لَهم بِهِ مِن عِلْمٍ إلا اتِّباعَ الظَّنِّ﴾: «اِتِّباعَ» is accusative by exception, and it is an exception not from the first [category]; the meaning is: they have no knowledge of it, but they follow conjecture. If it were made nominative it would be permissible, by making the following of conjecture [their portion] incumbent on them, just as the Arabs say: «تَحِيَّتُكَ الضَّرْبُ، وعِتابُكَ السَّيْفُ» ("your greeting is a beating and your reproach is the sword"). The poet said:
؎وَخَيْلٍ قَدْ دَلَفْتُ لَها بِخَيْلٍ ∗∗∗ تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وجِيعُ
(Many a troop of horse I advanced against with horse; the greeting between them was painful blows.)
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا﴾: some said: the hāʾ refers to knowledge; the meaning is «وَما قَتَلُوا عِلْمَهم يَقِينًا» ("they did not thoroughly master their knowledge with certainty"), as you say «أنا أقْتُلُ الشَّيْءَ عِلْمًا» ("I 'kill' the thing in knowledge"), whose interpretation is: I know it with complete knowledge. Others said: in «وَما قَتَلُوهُ» the hāʾ refers to Jesus, as He said: ﴿وَما قَتَلُوهُ وما صَلَبُوهُ﴾. Both views are permissible.

zajjaj:158-158.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إلَيْهِ﴾: assimilating the lām into the rāʾ is the [normal] usage, and the reading is according to it, because the lām is close to the point of articulation of the rāʾ, and the rāʾ is a strong letter with something like repetition in it; for that reason assimilation was chosen in it. If it is not assimilated, because it spans two words, that is permissible.

zajjaj:159-159.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ إلا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾: the meaning is: there is not one of them but will surely believe in him. Likewise His saying ﴿وَإنْ مِنكم إلا وارِدُها﴾ [Maryam: 71]: the meaning is: there is not one of you but will come to it. Likewise ﴿وَما مِنّا إلا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 164]: the meaning is: there is not one of us but has a known station. Similar is the poet's saying:
؎لَوْ قُلْتَ ما في قَوْمِها لَمْ تَيْثَمِ ∗∗∗ يَفْضُلُها في حَسَبٍ ومِيسَمِ
(Were you to say, "There is none among her people who surpasses her in lineage and beauty," you would not sin.)
The meaning is: there is no one among her people who surpasses her. So the meaning is: [each] will surely believe in him before his death; the hāʾ in «مَوْتِهِ» refers back to the disbeliever, according to some views. It has been said: there is no one among those who disbelieved in Jesus but will surely believe in him before his death, because the dying person, before his death, sees his deeds plainly and knows the good of them from the bad; and every disbeliever, when he sees plainly, believes in every prophet he disbelieved in, before his death. They said concerning the hāʾ in His saying ﴿لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ﴾: that is, in Jesus; and some said: in Muḥammad ﷺ. The two views are one, because whoever disbelieved in a prophet sees plainly before his death that he was in error, and believes when faith does not benefit him.
Some said: «إلّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ» means: he will believe in Jesus when he descends to kill al-Masīkh al-Dajjāl (the Antichrist). This is far-fetched linguistically, because He said ﴿وَإنْ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ إلا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾, and those who will remain until that time are only a small band of them. But it is possible that all of them say: "Jesus, who will descend to kill the Dajjāl — we believe [in him]"; so it is permissible on this basis, and Allah knows best its true sense.

zajjaj:162-162.t:
His saying: ﴿لَكِنِ الرّاسِخُونَ في العِلْمِ مِنهم والمُؤْمِنُونَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ﴾: by "those firmly grounded" are meant those firm in knowledge among the People of the Book; because of their knowledge they believed in the Prophet ﷺ and the rest of the prophets — peace be upon them. ﴿والمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ﴾ is conjoined (nasaq) to «ما»; the meaning is: they believe in what was revealed to you and in those who establish prayer, that is: they believe in the prophets who establish prayer. Some said: «اَلْمُقِيمِينَ» is conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm [of «مِنهم»]; the meaning is: «لَكِنِ الرّاسِخُونَ في العِلْمِ مِنهم ومِنَ المُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْزِلَ إلَيْكَ» ("but those firmly grounded in knowledge among them and among those who establish prayer believe in what was revealed to you"). This, according to the grammarians, is poor — I mean conjoining to the hāʾ and mīm — because an overt genitive noun is not conjoined to an implied genitive pronoun except in poetry.
Some held that this is a slip by the scribe, and some said: in the Book of Allah there are things which the Arabs will put right with their tongues. This view is, according to the people of the language, very far-fetched, because those who compiled the Quran were the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they are the people of the language, they are the model, and they were close in time to the beginning of Islam. So how would they leave in the Book of Allah something to be put right by others, when they are the ones who took it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and compiled it? This [obligation] is lifted from those after them who do not know, and lifted from those who do know, because they [the Companions] are the ones to be followed. So this is something that ought not to be attributed to them — Allah's mercy be upon them. The Quran is precisely composed; there is no laḥn (grammatical error) in it, and the Arabs do not speak with better iʿrāb than it, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِن حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 42], and said: ﴿بِلِسانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 195].
Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the grammarians have a chapter on this which they call "the chapter of praise" (bāb al-madḥ), in which they have shown the soundness and excellence of this. The grammarians said: if you say «مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ الكَرِيمِ» ("I passed by Zayd the generous") and you want to distinguish Zayd from another, the genitive is the [proper] usage, so that Zayd the generous is known from Zayd who is not generous. But if you intend praise and commendation, then if you wish you put it in the accusative and say «مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ الكَرِيمَ», as though you said «أذْكُرُ الكَرِيمَ» ("I mention the generous one"); and if you wish you say «بِزَيْدٍ الكَرِيمُ», on the implied form «هو الكَرِيمُ» ("he is the generous one"). And «جاءَنِي قَوْمُكَ المُطْعِمِينَ في المَحَلِّ، والمُغِيثُونَ في الشَّدائِدِ» ("your people came to me — those who feed in time of drought, and they are the rescuers in hardships"), in the sense of «أذْكُرُ المُطْعِمِينَ، وهُمُ المُغِيثُونَ في الشَّدائِدِ». The verse is on this [pattern], because when He said ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ وما أُنْـزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾, it was known that they establish prayer and give zakāt, so He said ﴿والمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ والمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ﴾ in the sense of «أذْكُرُ المُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ، وهُمُ المُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ» ("I mention those who establish prayer, and they are the givers of zakāt"). They recited the verses of al-Khirniq bint Badr ibn Hiffān:
؎لا يَبْعَدَنْ قَوْمِي الَّذِينَ هُمُو ∗∗∗ سُمُّ العُداةِ وآفَةُ الجُزُرِ
(May my people not perish, who are poison to enemies and the bane of slaughter-camels,)
؎اَلنّازِلِينَ بِكُلِّ مُعْتَرَكٍ ∗∗∗ والطَّيِّبُونَ مَعاقِدُ الأُزُرِ
(Those who dismount in every battlefield, and the pure in the knots of their waist-wrappers.)
In the sense of «أذْكُرُ النّازِلِينَ» ("I mention those who dismount"); its nominative and accusative are by way of praise. Some put «اَلنّازِلِينَ» in the nominative and «اَلطَّيِّبِينَ» in the accusative; all of it is one — permissible and good. The verse is on this [pattern].
As for whoever said that it is a slip, we have made clear what suffices about it. The argumentation we have mentioned on this is the position of our colleagues, the Basrans.

zajjaj:163-163.t:
His saying: ﴿إنّا أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ كَما أوْحَيْنا إلى نُوحٍ والنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾: this is an answer to them when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to bring down to them a book from heaven; mention of that came before this verse, namely His saying: ﴿يَسْألُكَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ أنْ تُنَـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ كِتابًا مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 153]. So Allah made known to His Prophet that his case with regard to revelation is like the case of the prophets who preceded him, and this is an argument against them. He said: ﴿إنّا أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ كَما أوْحَيْنا إلى نُوحٍ والنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾ and the rest of the prophets mentioned in this verse.
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنا داوُدَ زَبُورًا﴾: the reading in it is with fatḥa on the zāy and with ḍamma. Most readers have fatḥa on the zāy, but a group read «زُبُورًا» with ḍamma on the zāy, among them al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza. Whoever read «زَبُورًا» with fatḥa on the zāy, its meaning is "a book", and this is the [preferred] option according to the people of the language, because the reports have come thus: «زَبُورُ داوُدَ» ("the Zabūr of David"), just as «تَوْراةُ مُوسى» ("the Torah of Moses") and «إنْجِيلُ عِيسى» ("the Gospel of Jesus") have come.
Whoever read «زُبُورًا» with ḍamma on the zāy, its meaning is «وَآتَيْناهُ كُتُبًا» ("and We gave him books"), the plural of «زَبْرٌ», [giving] «زُبُورٌ». One says «ذَبَرْتُ الكِتابَ، أذْبُرُهُ، ذَبْرًا» when I have written, and «ذَبَرْتُ، أذْبُرُ، ذَبْرًا» and «أذْبِرُ» when I have read. «اَلزَّبْرُ» in the language is the firm construction of work in a well specifically; you say «بِئْرٌ مَزْبُورَةٌ» when it is lined with stones. And «اَلزَّبْرُ» is firm writing of a book. As for the poet's saying:
؎هَوْجاءُ لَيْسَ لِلُبِّها زَبْرُ
(Reckless, her core has no firmness.)
— he is describing a wind; he made this a figure for it, as though he said: its state has no strength in steadiness.
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿آتُونِي زُبَرَ الحَدِيدِ﴾ [al-Kahf: 96]: its singular is «زُبْرَةٌ», and they are pieces of iron.

zajjaj:164-164.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَرُسُلا قَدْ قَصَصْناهم عَلَيْكَ﴾: «رُسُلًا» is accusative from two angles. The better of them is that it is accusative by an implied verb which the overt one explains; the meaning is: «وَقَدْ قَصَصْنا رُسُلًا عَلَيْكَ قَدْ قَصَصْناهُمْ» ("We have related messengers to you — We have related them"), just as you say «رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا أكْرَمْتُهُ» ("I saw Zayd, and ʿAmr — I honoured him"), the meaning being: «وَأكْرَمْتُ عَمْرًا أكْرَمْتُهُ». It is also permissible that «وَرُسُلًا» be construed on the sense of ﴿إنّا أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 163], because its meaning is: «إنّا أرْسَلْنا إلَيْكَ، مُوحِينَ إلَيْكَ، وأرْسَلْنا رُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْناهم عَلَيْكَ» ("We have sent [revelation] to you, revealing to you, and We sent messengers whom We have related to you").
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسى تَكْلِيمًا﴾: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — told of His singling out one prophet among those He mentioned, and He — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that Moses was spoken to without [mediated] revelation, and He emphasised that by His saying «تَكْلِيمًا» (a speaking); so it is speech as speech is understood — there is no doubt about that.
